dQVkeGml4z.one_liner: Open-source modular toolkit decomposing Bayesian experimental design into tasks, objectives, training mechanisms, policy architectures, and evaluation.
dQVkeGml4z.problem: BED methods live in bespoke codebases and are evaluated on few tasks, which makes them hard to apply, compare, or extend.
dQVkeGml4z.method: Provides freely composable components spanning tasks, objectives, training mechanisms, policy architectures, and evaluation procedures, plus scalable implementations of primitives such as expected information gain estimators, and uses them to run a large-scale benchmark of contemporary BED methods.
dQVkeGml4z.key_idea: Standardize BED as composable modules (design space, rollout hooks, objective, fitting algorithm) so existing methods are reproduced in one framework and new configurations are cheap.
dQVkeGml4z.evidence: A large-scale benchmark of contemporary BED methods with controlled studies of methodological choices such as time embeddings in design policy architectures.
dQVkeGml4z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular decomposition is clear and useful, the library supports reproducibility and faster research, and the benchmark shows no method is a clear winner while design choices such as time embeddings matter.
dQVkeGml4z.main_concern: Methods received uneven hyperparameter tuning, so the benchmark comparison may be unfair, and the main text lacks concrete examples of how methods map onto the modules.

tgClEkqJ0e.one_liner: Benchmark pairing optimization tasks with given versus data-inferred stochastic parameters to measure LLMs' observation-to-decision gap.
tgClEkqJ0e.problem: Optimization benchmarks usually supply the stochastic quantities explicitly, whereas real operational settings require inferring them from finite observations before optimization can begin.
tgClEkqJ0e.method: Each decision problem is evaluated under matched conditions: in NL2Code the stochastic parameters are given, and in Workflow the agent must infer them from 100 observations before building and executing the optimization procedure. The benchmark has 147 NL2Code and 441 Workflow tasks across 21 human-verified executable protocols, and uses neuron-guided synthesis to reduce behavioral redundancy.
tgClEkqJ0e.key_idea: Hold the optimization problem fixed while switching whether stochastic parameters are given or must be estimated from 100 observations, and select diverse tasks by neuron-activation patterns.
tgClEkqJ0e.evidence: Evaluation of six proprietary and two open-weight LLMs on 147 NL2Code and 441 Workflow tasks, and a comparison of neuron-guided versus embedding-based task selection across four held-out models.
tgClEkqJ0e.claimed_gains: The strongest models achieve over 99% tolerance accuracy when the stochastic parameters are given, while the TL;DR reports that this performance does not carry over to decisions from finite data.
tgClEkqJ0e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched parameters-known versus observation-driven design, with a same-data reference solution, makes the benchmark diagnostically useful for how LLMs behave when parameters must be inferred.
tgClEkqJ0e.main_concern: The main metric is error in the optimal objective value rather than decision quality or feasibility, so it does not directly support claims about decision-making (a correct optimal order quantity can still be scored wrong).

haxFnk2HFV.one_liner: COAL estimates rectified-flow log-likelihood deterministically by amortizing the divergence trace with a learned per-coordinate variance head.
haxFnk2HFV.problem: Per-sample likelihood for flow models needs an O(d^3) divergence integral, and Hutchinson's estimator requires backpropagation through the velocity network at every ODE step and gives a noisy integrand.
haxFnk2HFV.method: Shows via Tweedie's formula that a rectified-flow velocity's divergence equals a scaled trace of the conditional covariance of the velocity residual, and trains a lightweight per-coordinate variance head jointly with the velocity to estimate it in one forward pass per ODE step.
haxFnk2HFV.key_idea: Rewrite the divergence as the trace of the conditional velocity-residual covariance (Tweedie) and predict it with a jointly trained variance head, avoiding input-space backpropagation and stochastic probes.
haxFnk2HFV.evidence: Class-conditional ImageNet with a DiT-XL latent rectified flow, where COAL matches the Hutchinson reference at less evaluation compute, evaluated on all 50k validation images per reviews.
haxFnk2HFV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, deterministic, needs one forward pass per ODE step with less memory than Hutchinson, and is validated at large scale with a clear efficiency gain.
haxFnk2HFV.main_concern: Novelty is overstated relative to the concurrent SCALLOP divergence-head method, and COAL needs an auxiliary variance head trained with the velocity and relies on rectified-flow structure.

UpR5uTu7JV.one_liner: Training-free chunk-indexed sparse attention for pretrained dense LLMs, selecting KV chunks from summaries of existing keys.
UpR5uTu7JV.problem: Attention reads a growing key-value history, making long-context LLM inference increasingly expensive, and existing sparse attention needs training or a costly indexer.
UpR5uTu7JV.method: Selects fixed-size KV chunks using compact summaries derived from the model's existing keys, with one query per KV group whose selection is shared across the group's queries. During prefill, QShare reuses chunk selections across adjacent queries.
UpR5uTu7JV.key_idea: Compact chunk summaries built from existing keys index the KV history without gradient updates, and a single query per KV group picks chunks shared by the whole group.
UpR5uTu7JV.evidence: Evaluation on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano and Ultra and Inkling-Small, with one-layer BF16 kernel benchmarks at batch size 32 and quality tests on MRCR, LongBench v2, GraphWalks and RULER sweeps.
UpR5uTu7JV.claimed_gains: Core attention is 11.7x faster for prefill queries near the end of a 1M-token prompt and 13.0x during decode (8.6x and 3.0x including all measured GPU work), and on Ultra NVFP4 at 4,096 chunks scores stay within 1.5 percentage points of dense attention.
UpR5uTu7JV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free indexer recalibration is simple and practical, evaluated at large scale across models and datasets, and clearly presented with honest limitations.
UpR5uTu7JV.main_concern: Baselines are missing, notably DeepSeek DSA as an upper bound, and there is no ablation separating the effect of QShare (prefill) from chunk-indexed decode on quality.

8KntSQM84T.one_liner: Scaling laws for Product Key Memory, MoE, STEM and dense Transformers relating active parameters, capacity and tokens to loss.
8KntSQM84T.problem: How memory capacity in sparse memory architectures should scale with active computation and training data is poorly understood.
8KntSQM84T.method: Fits separate loss scaling laws for PKM and MoE over active parameters, memory capacity and training tokens using 421 training endpoints from 44 configurations, then applies constrained optimization to the fits to compare architectures and allocate capacity versus compute. A roofline analysis estimates hardware speedup.
8KntSQM84T.key_idea: Architecture-specific loss laws in active parameters, memory capacity and tokens turn capacity-versus-compute allocation into a constrained optimization problem solved on the fitted surfaces.
8KntSQM84T.evidence: 421 measured training endpoints from 44 configurations of dense Transformers, PKM, STEM and MoE with capacities up to 21.9B parameters and up to 128B tokens, plus holdout extrapolation tests and a roofline analysis.
8KntSQM84T.claimed_gains: Fits are validated on 421 endpoints from 44 configurations, and predicted loss favors PKM when capacity is abundant relative to compute, MoE in an intermediate regime, and dense Transformers when compute is abundant.
8KntSQM84T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the scaling laws are well fitted and tested with extrapolation holdouts, and that the constrained-optimization analysis gives practical guidance on capacity-compute allocation.
8KntSQM84T.main_concern: Headline architecture rankings rely heavily on extrapolation (to roughly 29B-1.88T total parameters versus measured maxima of 21.9B for PKM and 6.4B for MoE) without uncertainty analysis, and long-training extrapolation is thinly validated.

No3nTaVABe.one_liner: Synthesizes workflow-style instructions one atomic unit per round, keeping every version as a difficulty spectrum for adaptive RL data selection.
No3nTaVABe.problem: Complex instruction data scales mostly by adding constraints and lacks workflows with interdependent sub-tasks and output-dependent branches, which fixed checklist verification cannot judge.
No3nTaVABe.method: CASCADE expands a seed instruction by adding exactly one constraint, sub-task or conditional branch per round and verifies responses node by node on a check graph (a DAG); held-out seeds give the CascadeEval benchmark. SPIRAL then chooses, at each RL step, which version of each instruction to roll out to match the model's ability.
No3nTaVABe.key_idea: Atomic one-unit expansion yields an ordered difficulty spectrum per instruction, from which RL selects the version matched to the model's current ability at each step.
No3nTaVABe.evidence: SFT and RL experiments on Qwen3.5 models (4B and 9B named in reviews) with IF-Avg and OOD-Avg metrics, the CascadeEval benchmark, and ablations.
No3nTaVABe.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract text provided; a reviewer cites an improvement of about 11 points for CASCADE-hard over the strongest prior corpus.
No3nTaVABe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the workflow-style instruction formulation with DAG verification is meaningful and new, and that the corpus gives substantial gains in SFT and RL beyond the new benchmark.
No3nTaVABe.main_concern: SPIRAL's incremental gains are weakly validated (single seed, no comparison with an established difficulty-aware selection method, small graph-versus-end-to-end verification gap, hyperparameter sensitivity), and the difference from prior structured-instruction work is not clearly drawn.

vFpCgsGGmz.one_liner: Shows LM-agent pairs can learn a private communication channel in-context from one bit of feedback, bypassing confidentiality instructions and monitors.
vFpCgsGGmz.problem: Repeated interactions may let ordinary messages acquire shared private meaning, so agents required to coordinate without disclosing confidential information could leak it.
vFpCgsGGmz.method: A repeated game where a sender observes one of four secret states and picks one of four summaries of the same public report while a receiver infers the state from one bit of correctness feedback, extended to free-form updates in a simulated incident-response task.
vFpCgsGGmz.key_idea: In-context learning at inference time over repeated interactions lets sender and receiver converge on a shared mapping from ordinary wording to secret states, with no codebook.
vFpCgsGGmz.evidence: Pairs of frontier models in repeated games, with a monitor screening every message, message-substitution and receiver-history ablations, and a free-form incident-response task.
vFpCgsGGmz.claimed_gains: Frontier agents recover the confidential finding with near-perfect accuracy, 98.8% against 25% chance, despite explicit instructions prohibiting disclosure and a monitor that screens every message.
vFpCgsGGmz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is important and timely for multi-agent security, and that message-substitution and history ablations show information flows through the messages.
vFpCgsGGmz.main_concern: Limited generality and unclear mechanism: only four secret states with a fixed report make signaling easy, free-form channel formation succeeded in only 2/20 games, the monitor sees single messages, and the paper is hard to read.

34ZCk3JK2f.one_liner: Combines goal-reaching values across trajectories via sampled waypoints and a discounted triangle relation for offline goal-conditioned RL.
34ZCk3JK2f.problem: In long-horizon offline GCRL, one-step TD backups propagate distant-goal value slowly, and existing structured methods need specialized value models or compose only segments from the same trajectory.
34ZCk3JK2f.method: Cross-Trajectory Value Composition (CVC) samples intermediate waypoints across trajectories and uses a discounted triangle relation to combine two shorter goal-reaching problems into a value target. It is added to a hierarchical offline GCRL framework using an ordinary value network.
34ZCk3JK2f.key_idea: Bootstrap the value of (s,g) from the values of (s,w) and (w,g) for a waypoint w sampled from any trajectory, via a discounted triangle relation.
34ZCk3JK2f.evidence: 24 long-horizon OGBench datasets in a hierarchical offline GCRL framework, with a same-trajectory ablation and a figure covering only about five tasks.
34ZCk3JK2f.claimed_gains: Best or tied-best performance on 20 of 24 OGBench tasks, substantially faster learning than prior methods, and strong results on stitching and noisy datasets.
34ZCk3JK2f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find cross-trajectory composition a simple, practical way to propagate long-horizon value without a specialized value architecture, with noticeable gains over hierarchical offline RL baselines.
34ZCk3JK2f.main_concern: Gains are not isolated to the composition loss, since the appendix also changes value parameterization, subgoals, advantage normalization and noise, and the advantage over quasimetric methods is unclear.

Q07fDe8K4W.one_liner: Smooths column-generation duals using a learned prediction of future duals to steer pricing toward columns useful in later iterations.
Q07fDe8K4W.problem: Dual oscillations slow column generation, and smoothing with past duals stabilizes the trajectory but does not guide pricing toward columns that are useful later.
Q07fDe8K4W.method: The current restricted-master dual is combined with a learned prediction of future duals to modify only the pricing objective. The predictor is trained offline on standard column generation trajectories, and exact reduced-cost checks plus fallback pricing with unsmoothed duals preserve correctness.
Q07fDe8K4W.key_idea: Replace past duals in the smoothing combination with a learned finite-horizon prediction of future duals that alters only the pricing subproblem objective.
Q07fDe8K4W.evidence: Experiments on cutting stock and generalized assignment problems (abstract is cut off), with 50 instances in the main runtime table and instance-size generalization studied for cutting stock.
Q07fDe8K4W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method conceptually simple, well motivated, naturally integrated into the column generation loop, and report substantial and consistent improvements on the two studied problems.
Q07fDe8K4W.main_concern: Empirical scope is limited to two synthetic problem families, with a missing simple learned tie-breaking baseline and a reviewer-flagged internal inconsistency in the Table 1 runtime statistics.

Tf0qu9sPJG.one_liner: Quaternionic state space model with input-dependent 4D rotations (pairs of unit quaternions) giving non-commutative state transitions.
Tf0qu9sPJG.problem: Complex-valued diagonal SSM transitions are commutative, which fundamentally limits their expressivity for state tracking.
Tf0qu9sPJG.method: Icosian parametrizes input-dependent SO(4) rotations as pairs of unit quaternions and computes the recurrence with quaternion arithmetic, without materializing rotation matrices. A reviewer notes it uses cumulative quaternion products to reuse existing SSD computation.
Tf0qu9sPJG.key_idea: Parametrize each transition as an input-dependent SO(4) rotation by a pair of unit quaternions, so state updates are non-commutative yet computed with quaternion arithmetic.
Tf0qu9sPJG.evidence: Language modeling from 500M to 3B parameters across multiple seeds against Mamba-3, Gated DeltaNet and Gated DeltaProduct, plus synthetic state-tracking and recall tasks including the non-solvable A5 group and rotation tracking, and a theorem on single-layer capability.
Tf0qu9sPJG.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms Mamba-3, Gated DeltaNet and Gated DeltaProduct in language modeling with extra compute falling to only 3% at 3B parameters, and a single layer length-generalizes on the non-solvable A5 group.
Tf0qu9sPJG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that non-commutative quaternionic transitions are a natural, well-motivated extension of complex SSMs, the paper is clear, and the synthetic state-tracking results are strong.
Tf0qu9sPJG.main_concern: Language-modeling gains are small and statistically unclear (about 0.14%-0.25% perplexity over Mamba-3), no controlled test isolates non-commutativity, and the effect of depth on expressivity is left open.

ul5s1DR0NB.one_liner: Finds lottery tickets cheaply by decoupling search and training hyperparameters and keeping weights near initialization during iterative pruning.
ul5s1DR0NB.problem: Lottery tickets in larger networks and harder datasets need lightly pretrained weights, and the best mask-search hyperparameters contradict those best for training the sparse network.
ul5s1DR0NB.method: The paper studies how search hyperparameters change learning distance and sign flips, adds explicit regularization on distance from initialization, and combines low learning distance with limited sign flips. It pairs this with a cheaper search schedule and more aggressive pruning to cut extraction cost.
ul5s1DR0NB.key_idea: Keep weights close to initialization with limited sign flips during iterative-pruning mask search, using search hyperparameters decoupled from those used to train the final sparse network.
ul5s1DR0NB.evidence: Hyperparameter sweeps in the mask search phase, regularization experiments on learning distance and an extraction-cost comparison, though reviewers note the evaluation is limited to one setting.
ul5s1DR0NB.claimed_gains: Significantly reduces the cost of extracting a lottery ticket and yields more trainable sparse networks; no numbers stated in the abstract.
ul5s1DR0NB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating search-phase from training-phase hyperparameters and using learning distance as an explanation for trainable masks, and see the efficiency results as promising.
ul5s1DR0NB.main_concern: Several design choices change at once and evaluation covers a single setting, so the source of improvement and the role of learning distance versus plain weight decay are unclear.

L5QyVmdaC4.one_liner: Executes sparse attention on CPU over host-memory KV blocks and merges with GPU results via log-sum-exp, avoiding PCIe retrieval.
L5QyVmdaC4.problem: Eviction-based sparse attention loses accuracy, while retrieval-based KV-cache offloading is limited by PCIe bandwidth and bottlenecks decoding throughput.
L5QyVmdaC4.method: RheoServe moves compute to the data by running sparse attention directly on DDR-resident KV blocks on the CPU and merging partial results with GPU attention by Log-Sum-Exp reduction. A unified cache mechanism manages block placement, with dynamic migration keeping frequently accessed blocks on GPU to raise cache hit rate.
L5QyVmdaC4.key_idea: Offload sparse-attention compute to the CPU where KV blocks reside, aggregating host and device memory bandwidth instead of moving blocks over PCIe.
L5QyVmdaC4.evidence: Reasoning benchmarks GPQA, MATH-500 and AIME24/25 on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B against a PCIe Retrieval baseline using the same sparse predictor, run on RTX 3090/5090 GPUs with 16 CPU cores.
L5QyVmdaC4.claimed_gains: Maintains reasoning accuracy and reaches 1.40x and 1.57x the peak throughput of matched PCIe Retrieval for Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, respectively.
L5QyVmdaC4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PCIe is the bottleneck, find the profiling-based motivation convincing, and consider the system design with overlapped CPU attention, GPU attention and migration sound, with a clean evaluation of the core idea.
L5QyVmdaC4.main_concern: The difference from earlier CPU-GPU collaborative attention systems such as MagicPIG and HGCA is not validated by direct comparison, and the CPU cost of the gating predictor and the breadth of the serving evaluation are limited.

LFdwaKqxJL.one_liner: Replaces last-mistake time with total mistakes as the metric for language generation in the limit, with bounds via weighted updates.
LFdwaKqxJL.problem: Existing results on language generation in the limit guarantee eventual consistency but ignore the cumulative number of invalid outputs made during learning.
LFdwaKqxJL.method: The paper reduces mistake-bounded generation to the Learning from Correct Demonstrations framework, giving a recipe for mistake bounds through weighted update rules. It analyzes finite classes, countably infinite streams of languages, and noisy adversaries.
LFdwaKqxJL.key_idea: Count total invalid outputs and bound them with weighted-update algorithms obtained by reduction to Learning from Correct Demonstrations.
LFdwaKqxJL.evidence: Theoretical results only: an algorithm for finite classes, a trade-off theorem for countable streams of languages, and an extension to noisy adversaries.
LFdwaKqxJL.claimed_gains: For finite classes, an optimal last-mistake time of Cdim(L)+1 and a mistake bound of floor(log2 |L|) are achieved simultaneously, while for countable streams O(log i) mistakes preclude prior convergence guarantees.
LFdwaKqxJL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard mistake-bounded generation as a natural, well-motivated analogue of Littlestone's mistake-bound model, and the finite-class result achieving both goals at once as compelling.
LFdwaKqxJL.main_concern: The scope of the countable-class claims is unclear, since Theorem 6.1 gives no stream-independent last-mistake bound and the proof of Theorem 6.4 does not appear to yield the claimed contradiction.

OBTCaUMvFn.one_liner: AVA adapts multi-step backup lengths so bootstrapping ends at junction states, preserving trajectory stitching in offline goal-conditioned RL.
OBTCaUMvFn.problem: Longer backups reduce TD bias accumulation but can skip junction states where reward signals propagate between trajectories, which hinders stitching.
OBTCaUMvFn.method: Adaptive Value Anchoring adapts backup lengths so value targets bootstrap from junction states. Reviews describe a handcrafted junction score based on proximity and downstream state coverage within an existing multi-step value-learning framework.
OBTCaUMvFn.key_idea: Choose where each multi-step backup ends by scoring junction states, so value targets bootstrap from them instead of from a fixed horizon.
OBTCaUMvFn.evidence: Long-horizon OGBench stitching tasks, including subsampled settings with reduced trajectory overlap, where AVA has the highest average success rate among compared methods and the highest mean success in every subsampled setting.
OBTCaUMvFn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the insight that fixed-horizon backups can skip stitching junctions is clear and the gains on long-horizon tasks are meaningful, with one review citing mean success rising from 59.8% to 68.5% over n-step value anchoring.
OBTCaUMvFn.main_concern: The junction-selection rule is a handcrafted heuristic tied to hand-picked coordinates and state inputs, and external baseline scores differ from the original papers, so the ranking needs clarification.

HsDamQe2xt.one_liner: Jointly optimizing syntactic and image-alignment objectives with equal weight stabilizes grammar induction across seeds and improves accuracy.
HsDamQe2xt.problem: Unsupervised grammar induction is unstable across seeds, and prior visually grounded induction gave modest gains without resolving this or testing whether the images themselves matter.
HsDamQe2xt.method: The syntactic objective and a semantic objective aligning constituents with images are optimized jointly with equal weight, together with a harder negative-sampling regime. A control pairs every caption with a random image, keeping the model and objectives intact while removing image information.
HsDamQe2xt.key_idea: Optimize syntax and constituent-image alignment jointly with equal weight, and use a random-image control to test whether visual information drives the gains.
HsDamQe2xt.evidence: Tests across English, French, and Chinese, datasets from Abstract Scenes to MS-COCO, and the COCO-Order task of ARO, with results over five seeds.
HsDamQe2xt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a fundamental problem and reports all five seeds transparently, with one review citing macro span-F1 rising from 38.6 +/- 24.3 to 65.2 +/- 0.5 for DINO-RN50 under hard negatives.
HsDamQe2xt.main_concern: Novelty over the VC-PCFG prior work is not clearly established, since joint optimization of grammar induction and image-text matching already appears there, and baselines such as the Zhao and Titov grammar are missing from Table 2.

WBN8dZAYBd.one_liner: Calibrates Gaussian-mixture proposals for random-feature softmax attention using an exact expected output error at a fixed feature budget.
WBN8dZAYBd.problem: Random-feature attention can miss strongly contributing query-key regions, and lowering kernel error or large-sample variance need not lower output error at a fixed feature count.
WBN8dZAYBd.method: Relates kernel error to proposal coverage and derives an exact expected squared output error through normalization and value aggregation. MINT covers multiple contributing regions with a Gaussian mixture whose weights are chosen by a numerical approximation of that error; MINT# also adapts component shapes.
WBN8dZAYBd.key_idea: Choose mixture proposal weights by minimizing the exact finite-budget expected squared attention output error, which accounts for normalization and value aggregation, rather than kernel variance.
WBN8dZAYBd.evidence: Exact-risk derivation for independent features and blocks including orthogonal random features, a controlled ablation of the calibration criterion, and LLM experiments replacing a subset of heads in Qwen and OLMo.
WBN8dZAYBd.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract, which is cut off before the results.
WBN8dZAYBd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the finite-budget risk analysis clear and useful, and MINT consistently better than FAVOR-style baselines at unchanged inference cost.
WBN8dZAYBd.main_concern: Practical significance is limited: only a subset of heads is replaced, a large perplexity gap to exact attention remains, no latency is reported, and related work (RA/LARA) and post-hoc linearization methods are not compared.

TedbeCjpkV.one_liner: End-to-end benchmark of indirect prompt injection attacks delivered through runtime interaction surfaces in long-horizon agent workflows.
TedbeCjpkV.problem: Existing indirect prompt injection evaluations focus on isolated malicious strings, single-step tool calls, or narrow agent setups rather than long-horizon workflows.
TedbeCjpkV.method: INFUSE provides realistic agent tasks and a taxonomy of attack scenarios across five threat categories, with attacks injected through interaction surfaces met during task execution. It evaluates 19 LLMs plus guard models and defenses.
TedbeCjpkV.key_idea: Inject adversarial instructions through realistic runtime surfaces such as shell output across a whole agent workflow, rather than only in the initial prompt or isolated tool returns.
TedbeCjpkV.evidence: 19 LLMs from the GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families, 41,824 adversarial trajectories (26,220 without defenses) and 720 benign reference runs, with the LLM judge checked against human labels.
TedbeCjpkV.claimed_gains: Mean attack success is 19.6% under LLM-based evaluation and 15.4% under heuristic verification, with per-model ASR-L from 3.2% to 41.9%; guard models give limited protection.
TedbeCjpkV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark realistic and broad, covering many attack surfaces and 19 models with a large number of trajectories.
TedbeCjpkV.main_concern: Novelty over Terminal-Bench-style tasks and prior injection work is limited, and the single LLM judge, reliance on Mini-SWE-Agent, and cost-cap truncation weaken the reliability of attack-success comparisons.

bzRZfhhWFl.one_liner: VPM jointly forecasts multi-view videos and persistent 3D point trajectories using a pretrained world model with a trajectory head.
bzRZfhhWFl.problem: Forecasting future videos from multiple cameras requires them to depict the same evolving 3D scene, which video-only prediction does not tie to a shared 3D motion description.
bzRZfhhWFl.method: VPM extends a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing and a trajectory head that predicts how persistent 3D scene points move over time, and adds robot actions as a token modality denoised jointly with future videos for control. The authors also build VPM-Data (simulated multi-view videos with point trajectories) and the VP-WorldBench forecasting benchmark.
bzRZfhhWFl.key_idea: Supervise a trajectory head on persistent 3D points shared across all views alongside video generation, tying appearance changes in every camera to one 3D motion description.
bzRZfhhWFl.evidence: Evaluated on VP-WorldBench, existing 4D generation benchmarks, and robot control, comparing the video-only variant VPM (V) with the point-supervised VPM (V+T) and with frame-by-frame geometric supervision.
bzRZfhhWFl.claimed_gains: Point supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D motion accuracy over a video-only counterpart; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
bzRZfhhWFl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly forecasting videos and persistent 3D trajectories is a meaningful direction and that the broad comparison between video-only and trajectory-supervised variants shows the value of point supervision.
bzRZfhhWFl.main_concern: Consistency between generated videos and predicted 3D trajectories is neither enforced nor directly evaluated, and point supervision does not cover non-rigid objects such as cloth and hair.

RjAg0NMPjO.one_liner: Buffer-free class-incremental learning with dual-branch LoRA adapters and inter-task orthogonality so tasks can be unlearned by adapter detachment.
RjAg0NMPjO.problem: In class-incremental learning, deleting a task-specific component without past data can still perturb later-task activations and degrade retained performance because of activation-space entanglement.
RjAg0NMPjO.method: CAD uses Anti-Entanglement of Activation (AEA) to enforce inter-task orthogonality in representation space, with dual-branch LoRA adapters separating shared and removable knowledge so unlearning is adapter detachment. It also deletes forgotten-task basis vectors from gradient-projection memory.
RjAg0NMPjO.key_idea: Enforces orthogonality between tasks' activations so a task's removable LoRA adapter can be deleted without disturbing later tasks' activations.
RjAg0NMPjO.evidence: Experiments across multiple benchmarks measuring retention-removal trade-offs and membership-inference risk against existing baselines, with ablations of AEA.
RjAg0NMPjO.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract claims stronger retention-removal trade-offs and lower membership-inference risk, with no numbers).
RjAg0NMPjO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is meaningful and the buffer-free, task-ID-free setting is realistic, with negligible unlearning cost since deletion needs no data or optimization.
RjAg0NMPjO.main_concern: Novelty is questioned because the method largely reassembles existing pieces (InfLoRA-style GPM-constrained LoRA, O-LoRA-style orthogonality loss), and it is unclear that task information is truly removed rather than only the classifier head.

T2fzDguPV2.one_liner: Selects learning rates online to control new-update size relative to the pending update in schedule-free Muon, enabling anytime training.
T2fzDguPV2.problem: Schedule-free optimization avoids a predefined training horizon, but its performance can worsen with continued training at a fixed learning rate.
T2fzDguPV2.method: The authors view schedule-free optimization through the pending update, which accumulates new updates before they are gradually applied to the output iterate. ORA sets learning rates to control the size of new updates relative to the pending update.
T2fzDguPV2.key_idea: Chooses each learning rate so new updates stay a controlled fraction of the accumulated pending update that schedule-free averaging has yet to apply to the output iterate.
T2fzDguPV2.evidence: Local analysis in an aligned subspace of a deterministic two-layer linear model, noisy two-layer regression, and 124M and 720M language model pretraining compared with SF-Muon and tuned Muon cosine baselines.
T2fzDguPV2.claimed_gains: Reaches SF-Muon's validation loss with 42-51% fewer tokens at 124M, and matches strong Muon cosine baselines with 23% and 33% fewer tokens on 124M and 720M models.
T2fzDguPV2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ORA gives non-trivial token savings backed by theory showing SF-Muon need not converge to an optimum, tested on two model sizes against several baselines.
T2fzDguPV2.main_concern: Comparisons are not fully matched (ORA's learning rate and lambda_P are swept while cosine and SF-Muon are not), the controlled SF comparison is only at 124M, and scale is limited with WSD missing.

ndMwLPvInU.one_liner: Pretrained model reads pilot simulator paths and outputs an importance-sampling proposal or control-variate integrand, giving unbiased variance reduction without retraining.
ndMwLPvInU.problem: Monte Carlo estimation of expectations of stochastic-process functionals needs prohibitively many samples, and prior learned variance-reduction models are trained per task.
ndMwLPvInU.method: A model pretrained on a broad family of synthetic stochastic processes reads a small set of observed paths, functional evaluations, and the driving noise distribution, and outputs a task-specific controller (an importance sampling proposal or control variates integrand). Splitting paths between identification and estimation gives a test-time scaling mechanism.
ndMwLPvInU.key_idea: Amortizes variance reduction by in-context identification: a pretrained network maps pilot paths to an importance-sampling or control-variate controller, with unbiasedness preserved by construction.
ndMwLPvInU.evidence: Pretraining on synthetic stochastic processes; demonstrations on finance and biology applications, including real volatility and limit-order-book data and stochastic optimization (per reviews), with matched wall-clock comparisons.
ndMwLPvInU.claimed_gains: Significant variance reduction at matched wall-clock speed; no numbers stated in the abstract.
ndMwLPvInU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that amortizing variance reduction across tasks without retraining is a useful direction, with a clean identification-versus-estimation split, unbiased estimators, and broad application coverage.
ndMwLPvInU.main_concern: The black-box claim is overstated because the method needs access to the driving noise (with Brownian-motion assumptions behind the Girsanov and martingale-representation arguments), and the method description is inconsistent between main text and appendix.

Kvbf46f5gD.one_liner: A judge picks among generator-proposed actions via function-class refinement, optimistic exploration, and pessimistic final selection in fixed-budget pure exploration.
Kvbf46f5gD.problem: Classical pure exploration assumes the learner picks actions directly, but agentic systems get candidate actions from a black-box generator over a large implicit space, and a separate judge decides which to execute.
Kvbf46f5gD.method: A black-box generator proposes small candidate sets and a judge selects which to execute, with offline reward data from other context-action pairs and a function class capturing shared reward structure. The judge uses evolving uncertainty through function class refinement, optimistic exploration, and pessimistic final selection to find a near-optimal action for a target context within a fixed budget.
Kvbf46f5gD.key_idea: Offline data narrow the plausible reward functions while online feedback resolves the rest; the judge refines the function class, explores optimistically, and selects pessimistically.
Kvbf46f5gD.evidence: A fixed-budget theoretical guarantee with a worst-case lower bound (abstract truncated), plus experiments including an LCBench reward-function class and a small LLM judge (per reviews).
Kvbf46f5gD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem formulation is interesting and the theoretical analysis is rigorous, with upper and lower bounds covering generator coverage and reward-function complexity.
Kvbf46f5gD.main_concern: Experiments are limited and toy-sized (weak baselines, a very small LLM judge, no history-dependent LLM generator), and the guarantees rely on a realizable reward class and a generator that proposes near-optimal actions with positive probability.

mNppVx2XtI.one_liner: Simulation-free Schrödinger bridge learning on Riemannian manifolds via heat-kernel-based entropic coupling and Gaussian bridge approximations around geodesics.
mNppVx2XtI.problem: Simulation-free Schrödinger bridge learning is hard to extend to Riemannian manifolds because Brownian transition kernels and conditional bridge distributions generally lack closed forms.
mNppVx2XtI.method: SSR-FM uses a small-noise heat-kernel expansion to approximate the endpoint transport cost, obtains the entropic coupling with Sinkhorn, and approximates conditional bridge marginals as Gaussian fluctuations around minimizing geodesics, giving flow and score targets without simulating diffusion paths. Under regularity assumptions, the reconstructed SDE reproduces the marginals of the approximate probability path.
mNppVx2XtI.key_idea: Approximate bridge transport cost with a small-noise heat-kernel expansion and bridge marginals with Gaussians around geodesics, giving tractable flow and score matching targets on manifolds.
mNppVx2XtI.evidence: Benchmarks with analytically specified and data-estimated geometries (reviews cite NOAA, IBTrACS, a 3D surface, and single-cell data), plus a theorem on marginal reproduction under regularity assumptions.
mNppVx2XtI.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says SSR-FM preserves manifold structure while achieving competitive hidden-time distribution matching among existing methods.
mNppVx2XtI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the geometry-aware coupling and conditional Gaussian paths clearly presented, with theory backing the construction.
mNppVx2XtI.main_concern: Improvements over existing methods are marginal on most real-world datasets and often within standard deviation, and the closely related geometry-aware SF2M-Geo baseline is missing.

PojV5P2w7y.one_liner: Likelihood Score Approximation learns an observation-conditioned likelihood score on top of a frozen unconditional diffusion prior for inverse problems
PojV5P2w7y.problem: Inverse-problem solvers either pair a pretrained prior with a known degradation model or train a conditional model on paired data, leaving unknown degradations learned from few pairs unaddressed.
PojV5P2w7y.method: Keeps a pretrained unconditional model fixed and learns an observation-conditioned model that approximates the likelihood score from paired samples, within a conditional stochastic-interpolant framework trainable in score or velocity coordinates with deterministic or stochastic sampling. The prior model can be swapped after training.
PojV5P2w7y.key_idea: Learn only an additive, observation-conditioned likelihood-score correction from paired samples within stochastic interpolants, while the unconditional prior stays frozen.
PojV5P2w7y.evidence: Speech and image inverse problems, including the ImageNet-256 benchmark, with known and unknown degradations and self-generated training pairs, compared against posterior-sampling baselines.
PojV5P2w7y.claimed_gains: Operates effectively at roughly 0.01% of the full training dataset; on ImageNet-256 it achieves competitive or better restoration quality than strong posterior-sampling baselines with up to several orders of magnitude fewer network evaluations and much lower inference latency.
PojV5P2w7y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the modular framework separating the frozen prior from observation-dependent adaptation, covering both known and unknown degradations, with extensive speech and image experiments.
PojV5P2w7y.main_concern: The evaluation protocol is weak (100 samples for metrics like FID, sparse baselines, differing priors) and the advance over DEFT is not isolated empirically.

IIxKNLBE43.one_liner: ShapleyOG speeds adaptive Shapley estimation with a Gaussian-process surrogate on the game's odd component, sparse refits, and quadrature updates
IIxKNLBE43.problem: ShaplEIG's adaptive coalition selection is sample-efficient but refits a Gaussian process surrogate every iteration, so its overhead limits use on costly games with low evaluation budgets.
IIxKNLBE43.method: Fits a Gaussian process only to the odd functional component of the game, which under paired sampling gives the same Shapley posterior and selection criterion from half as many observations. It refits the surrogate only on a sparse schedule and updates the selection criterion efficiently, with quadrature-based computation schemes.
IIxKNLBE43.key_idea: Since Shapley values depend only on the odd functional component, model that component alone with a GP under paired sampling, halving observations, and update the selection criterion efficiently.
IIxKNLBE43.evidence: A proof that full and odd GPs give equivalent Shapley posterior and information-gain criterion under paired observations with fixed hyperparameters, plus experiments on several games; total runtime combines measured overhead with an assumed cost per evaluation.
IIxKNLBE43.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the results)
IIxKNLBE43.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and that the theoretical equivalence of the odd and full GPs gives a sound basis for the computational savings.
IIxKNLBE43.main_concern: The practical runtime advantage is not validated with a real expensive model, and the large-player-count quadrature results and odd-versus-even GP comparison are missing or left to the appendix.

l2m0rp84rU.one_liner: Diffusion-based no-box watermark forgery attack learning residuals from removal-built proxy data, plus self-verifiable message defenses SeedBind and ContentBind.
l2m0rp84rU.problem: Forgery attacks that embed a counterfeit watermark into arbitrary content to falsely attribute it to a target model threaten AI provenance, and watermark security against them is underexplored.
l2m0rp84rU.method: EraseForge repurposes watermark removal to build a proxy dataset of watermark-free images, from which a conditional diffusion model learns to estimate and reproduce the watermark residual rather than regenerating the image. The defenses SeedBind and ContentBind turn verification from a lookup in a finite message pool into a structural consistency check.
l2m0rp84rU.key_idea: Learn the watermark as an image-conditioned residual from removal-based pairs; defend by binding the embedded message to a seed or the content.
l2m0rp84rU.evidence: Forgery attacks across multiple watermarking schemes and datasets, including the multi-message defense at N=20,000 and N=50,000 samples, a residual-versus-full-image ablation, and defense evaluations against estimator-based and residual-based attacks.
l2m0rp84rU.claimed_gains: Forgery performance with as few as 1,000 training samples, a 5x improvement in data efficiency over existing methods, and over 91% bit accuracy at N=20,000 samples where prior methods fail at N=50,000.
l2m0rp84rU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the attack is intuitive and well motivated, learns from removal-based pairs without clean images or detector access, and is evaluated across multiple schemes and datasets.
l2m0rp84rU.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to WMCopier and WMForger, and the defenses are not fully evaluated: EraseForge is not tested against ContentBind and acceptance rates for genuine images are not reported.

w9BVpxnDll.one_liner: Diagnoses the plan declaration-execution gap and routes tasks, via LLM-declared planning modes, to pattern-specific executors.
w9BVpxnDll.problem: Final task success cannot show whether an agent failed by choosing a poorly matched plan or by deviating from its structured plan during execution.
w9BVpxnDll.method: They introduce a diagnostic framework for the Plan Declaration-Execution Gap and Planning-as-Routing, where the LLM declares one of four planning modes (Predefined, Sequential, Hierarchical, or Search) and a deterministic router sends the task to the matching pattern-specific executor.
w9BVpxnDll.key_idea: Separate plan selection from plan execution by having the LLM declare a planning mode and a deterministic router enforce it through a dedicated executor.
w9BVpxnDll.evidence: Four benchmarks (ALFWorld, Mind2Web, WebArena, and SWE-bench Verified per reviews), three LLMs, and three seeds, with retry-matched and permutation-null controls.
w9BVpxnDll.claimed_gains: Generic Plan+ReAct preserves the declared planning structure in only 12-45% of trajectories across three benchmarks, whereas pattern-specific executors enforce the intended structure.
w9BVpxnDll.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating plan selection from execution is a useful diagnostic lens and that the evaluation is broad and checks plan adherence, not just final success.
w9BVpxnDll.main_concern: Planning-as-Routing itself is poorly supported (Routing@1 trails the best fixed pattern on 10 of 11 benchmark-model pairs), and the plan-adherence verifier agrees poorly with human judgment.

TP87m7HjKC.one_liner: Gradient inversion attack that aligns dummy-input features with low-rank attention-gradient subspaces via continuous embedding-subspace distance optimization.
TP87m7HjKC.problem: Existing transformer gradient inversion attacks scale poorly, need an enumerable token vocabulary (blocking non-text inputs), or break under numerical noise such as quantization or differential privacy.
TP87m7HjKC.method: TIGER exploits the low-rank structure of attention gradients, with an objective that aligns the features of dummy inputs across layers with the low-rank gradient subspaces. One framework recovers text from causal and bidirectional attention models and multimodal inputs.
TP87m7HjKC.key_idea: Replace DAGER's hard span-membership test with a continuous distance from dummy-input layer features to the low-rank attention-gradient subspaces.
TP87m7HjKC.evidence: Settings with bidirectional and causal attention, multimodal inputs, and robustness tests under quantization and noise.
TP87m7HjKC.claimed_gains: Substantially better reconstruction than prior work with bidirectional attention, images recovered at roughly 720p in the multimodal setting, and significantly greater robustness on causal models under quantization and (abstract cut off).
TP87m7HjKC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the continuous subspace-distance reformulation simple and well motivated, and an advance over DAGER that removes the finite-vocabulary requirement.
TP87m7HjKC.main_concern: The differential-privacy-style robustness evaluation is weak (i.i.d. Gaussian noise on unclipped gradients, no clipping or privacy budget), and the recovery guarantee restricts the number of tokens.

6ZJ4tRAdDw.one_liner: A continual loop updates a physics-plus-neural-residual dynamics model and the policy during deployment, with a recurrent encoder identifying hidden conditions.
6ZJ4tRAdDw.problem: Learning-based robot controllers are trained once and cannot use deployment experience when dynamics change from wind, payload, battery drain or wear.
6ZJ4tRAdDw.method: The method learns a condition-aware dynamics model from real state-action data by combining an analytical physics prior with a neural residual, and updates model and policy in a loop of about 10 s. A recurrent encoder infers the current condition so the policy can reuse earlier adaptations when conditions recur.
6ZJ4tRAdDw.key_idea: Share one latent condition space between a recurrent encoder inferred at deployment and the dynamics model used to sample conditions during policy training.
6ZJ4tRAdDw.evidence: Simulation studies and real-world quadrotor experiments, including propeller damage, with timing of the roughly 10-second update loop reported in an appendix.
6ZJ4tRAdDw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of continual improvement during real deployment is practical and the shared latent design and real quadrotor experiments are valuable.
6ZJ4tRAdDw.main_concern: Knowledge retention and forgetting are not directly evaluated, and gains are mostly against retraining from scratch with novelty over existing adaptation methods not isolated.

qpF9OmZ3Qq.one_liner: Benchmark of 300 webpage-development tasks where agents must selectively use one to five reference screenshots, scored by keypoints and judges.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.problem: Existing web benchmarks reconstruct visual targets or generate from text alone, overlooking the common workflow of developing from visual examples.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.method: RefCraft has 300 multimodal tasks combining instructions with screenshots of one to five reference webpages. Agents render, inspect and refine outputs, which are scored with independently verifiable keypoints plus programmatic and VLM judges.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.key_idea: Tasks specify how each reference should be used, and outputs are scored by verifiable keypoints with a minimum-based aggregation across components.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.evidence: Nine frontier (M)LLMs evaluated under a unified harness, with agreement studies for the evaluator.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.claimed_gains: The strongest system achieves an overall score of only 52.12 out of 100.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reference-conditioned setting is realistic and well formulated, and that the dual-track evaluation with rendered evidence is meaningful.
qpF9OmZ3Qq.main_concern: The minimum-based aggregation makes overall scores sensitive to the lowest or noisiest component, and its choice is insufficiently justified.

Ig6xq18LXJ.one_liner: RIFT fits adaptive point scatterers with spherical-harmonic complex reflectance through a generalized Radon transform forward model using only radar data.
Ig6xq18LXJ.problem: Predicting complex-valued radar measurements at unseen sensor poses and recovering 3D geometry from radar alone, without visual or LiDAR priors, initialization or supervision.
Ig6xq18LXJ.method: A scene is a set of point scatterers with learnable positions and direction-dependent complex reflectance in spherical harmonics, optimized by matching predicted and measured complex radar signals through a generalized Radon transform forward model. Signal-loss gradients trigger local increases in spatial resolution and spherical-harmonic degree.
Ig6xq18LXJ.key_idea: Grow point-scatterer resolution and spherical-harmonic degree where signal-loss gradients are large, while fitting complex radar returns through a generalized Radon transform forward model.
Ig6xq18LXJ.evidence: Evaluated on a simulated RIFT-Dataset and real GOTCHA data, comparing predictions at held-out sensor poses with held-out complex measurements and extracted geometry with ground-truth geometry.
Ig6xq18LXJ.claimed_gains: not stated in the available abstract text; a reviewer reports Complex RelMSE improving from 46.12% to 0.3909% and Chamfer from 0.8179 to 0.4813 on RIFT-Dataset, and Complex RelMSE from 128.5% to 54.33% on GOTCHA.
Ig6xq18LXJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the radar-only complex-valued formulation is interesting and clean, with an adaptive representation that serves both novel-view synthesis and reconstruction, evaluated on simulated and real radar data.
Ig6xq18LXJ.main_concern: Unclear contribution against related RF and radar view-synthesis work (Radar Fields, DART, NeWRF, GSRF, RFDT, mmIR), with limited ablations of the adaptive design.

jDGymN6uyq.one_liner: Represents a bag as an empirical measure and reads out cumulant-generating-function statistics at learned tilt locations for MIL.
jDGymN6uyq.problem: Existing MIL methods compress an instance set into a finite-dimensional representation whose retained information is fixed by the mechanism, though tasks may need different forms of compositional information.
jDGymN6uyq.method: TiltMIL treats each bag as an empirical probability measure in a task-specific feature space and uses its cumulant-generating function as a functional representation. It learns tilt locations to extract finite CGF values and cumulants, fuses them with a lightweight hierarchical mechanism, and adds empirical perturbation consistency for stability.
jDGymN6uyq.key_idea: Learn exponential-tilt locations at which to evaluate a bag's cumulant-generating function, giving task-specific finite statistics instead of a fixed pooling form.
jDGymN6uyq.evidence: Three WSI-MIL benchmarks (reviews name PANDA, TCGA-NSCLC and TCGA-RCC) with two feature encoders and ten MIL baselines, plus three controlled tasks (Presence, Co-occurrence, Competitive).
jDGymN6uyq.claimed_gains: not stated beyond consistent improvements across pathology classification tasks (a review cites 80.73% on PANDA).
jDGymN6uyq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the task-adaptive distributional-statistics view well motivated and the results competitive against ten baselines and two feature extractors.
jDGymN6uyq.main_concern: It is unclear whether the gains come from the CGF formulation or simply from multiple learnable queries with extra statistics, since the readouts resemble multi-query attention with weighted means and variances.

CiUbdvTbtb.one_liner: Selects pretraining data by mixing documents from the most and least central hosts of the Common Crawl web graph.
CiUbdvTbtb.problem: Existing pretraining data selection relies on auxiliary classifiers for document scoring or mixture optimization, adding compute overhead and dependence on labeled data.
CiUbdvTbtb.method: WEBGRAPHMIX computes structural centrality scores over the Common Crawl host-level web graph and varies the proportion of central versus peripheral documents in the pretraining mixture, integrated into the DataComp-LM pipeline.
CiUbdvTbtb.key_idea: Rank hosts by web-graph centrality (e.g., betweenness) and sample a balanced mixture of the most and least central hosts instead of scoring document content.
CiUbdvTbtb.evidence: Models of 400M and 1B parameters trained on 8B and 28B tokens in the DataComp-LM pipeline, evaluated on 23 tasks plus 26 held-out tasks.
CiUbdvTbtb.claimed_gains: At 1B scale a 1:1 mixture of the most and least central hosts by betweenness reaches 41.4% average versus 39.8% for uniform sampling, ahead on 19 of 23 tasks and on 26 held-out tasks.
CiUbdvTbtb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the centrality signal is simple and cheap, needs no classifier or proxy-model training, and is complementary to content-based quality filters.
CiUbdvTbtb.main_concern: The gain is fragile: configurations were selected on the same 23 test tasks, 1B comparisons rely on single training runs, and the best recipe changes between the 400M and 1B scales.

OCq0ecFKSi.one_liner: Shows causal foundation models combine unit-level variances as independent, undercovering group effects, and corrects with joint predictions.
OCq0ecFKSi.problem: Credible intervals from causal foundation models for group-averaged treatment effects lose nominal coverage as the group grows.
OCq0ecFKSi.method: They show formally that posterior uncertainty over the data-generating process correlates unit errors, so independent aggregation understates variance by a factor that grows with group size, and they propose models that give joint predictions (CNP and latent NP architectures) to recover coverage.
OCq0ecFKSi.key_idea: Unit-level variances are summed as if independent although posterior uncertainty correlates errors; a design-effect factor predicts the undercoverage, and joint predictions across units recover most of it.
OCq0ecFKSi.evidence: Coverage failures are shown for CausalPFN on six benchmarks including ACIC 2016 plus controlled synthetic experiments, while the proposed models are tested on a simple synthetic family.
OCq0ecFKSi.claimed_gains: No numeric gain for the fix is visible in the truncated abstract; on ACIC 2016 temperature-calibrated 95% CausalPFN intervals fall below nominal coverage beyond groups of 30 out of 4802 units, and full-sample intervals contain the true value in only 20% of datasets.
OCq0ecFKSi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies an important, under-examined coverage failure in causal foundation models and that the theory clearly explains it as group size grows.
OCq0ecFKSi.main_concern: The proposed solutions adapt existing CNP and latent NP architectures and are validated only on a simple synthetic family, not on the benchmarks where the failure was shown.

dxRoNNR0WF.one_liner: Benchmark of 200 evidence-controlled task pairs measuring unnecessary defensive actions by coding agents under the ATMA risk framework.
dxRoNNR0WF.problem: Coding agents may take unwarranted defensive risk treatments, and existing evaluations examine related behaviors separately without a unified framework.
dxRoNNR0WF.method: ParanoiaEval operationalizes the Avoidance-Transfer-Mitigation-Acceptance treatments with 200 repository-level task pairs that differ only in treatment-defining evidence, plus metrics for risk-treatment violations and evidence responsiveness scored by a human-calibrated agentic judge.
dxRoNNR0WF.key_idea: Pair tasks that differ only in the evidence that justifies a risk treatment, so an agent's defensive action can be judged as warranted or not.
dxRoNNR0WF.evidence: Large-scale experiments on 8 models over 200 task pairs from 50 repositories covering 44 situations, plus a post-hoc human study.
dxRoNNR0WF.claimed_gains: Unnecessary risk treatment occurs in 11.2%-58.7% of runs despite explicit evidence, with substantial variation across agent configurations.
dxRoNNR0WF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree unnecessary defensive behavior is an important problem and the paired, expert-checked benchmark makes evidence responsiveness measurable.
dxRoNNR0WF.main_concern: The 'unnecessary' labels may reflect annotator preference (author-team labels with no reported agreement), and the trade-off between unnecessary treatment and final safety is not measured.

YBgwqExyFZ.one_liner: Post-hoc contextual sparsification via bytes-per-token knapsack allocation and distillation, with token-by-token controllable sparsity.
YBgwqExyFZ.problem: Memory-bound LLM decoding trades generation quality against speed, and there is no post-hoc way to give any trained dense or MoE model a controllable sparsity level in a single checkpoint.
YBgwqExyFZ.method: Elastic Decoding frames contextual sparsification as a multiple-choice knapsack problem with bytes-per-token as the budget, allocates capacity heterogeneously across the architecture, then distills the model into a single sparse checkpoint using under 5B finetuning tokens. The quality-speed trade-off can be switched token by token during decoding.
YBgwqExyFZ.key_idea: Solve a multiple-choice knapsack over bytes per token to allocate sparsity heterogeneously across layers and unit types, then distill into one checkpoint.
YBgwqExyFZ.evidence: Dense and MoE models (such as Gemma4-31B and Qwen3-14B) with optimized on-device kernels, nine benchmarks, and a dense parity check against llama.cpp.
YBgwqExyFZ.claimed_gains: It can reduce the active number of parameters by up to 83% with end-to-end speed-ups of up to 4.6× (e.g., on Gemma4-31B), and sparsified Qwen3-14B runs faster and more accurately than Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-4B.
YBgwqExyFZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the system is complete and well ablated, with real wall-clock speedups on hardware and non-uniform knapsack allocation beating uniform allocation.
YBgwqExyFZ.main_concern: The near-lossless quality claim is weakly supported: several benchmarks are near saturation with only aggregate averages reported, and speedups are measured against bf16 rather than quantized dense baselines or unmodified MoE models.

xo3Algm0r8.one_liner: Extends polytopic matrix factorization identifiability to fewer measurements than latent components using face-span geometry and determinant maximization.
xo3Algm0r8.problem: Existing PMF identifiability requires at least as many measurements as latent components, which rules out overcomplete dictionary learning.
xo3Algm0r8.method: They keep PMF's source-correlation determinant-maximization (Det-Max) criterion and combine its maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid sufficient scattering condition with a face-span skeleton formed by intersecting the polytope with linear spans of low-dimensional faces. Under explicit assumptions, every global maximizer recovers the mixing matrix and latent samples up to linear automorphism of the polytope.
xo3Algm0r8.key_idea: Add a face-span skeleton (polytope intersected with spans of low-dimensional faces) to the scattering condition so Det-Max recovers overcomplete mixtures exactly in the noiseless case.
xo3Algm0r8.evidence: A finite-sample exact-recovery theorem for noiseless observations, plus synthetic recovery experiments and qualitative image-dictionary visualizations.
xo3Algm0r8.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims exact recovery of the mixing matrix and latent samples up to linear automorphism of the polytope under explicit assumptions, with no numbers.
xo3Algm0r8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending PMF to the underdetermined regime is a meaningful theoretical contribution, with a general face-span framework and a clear split between structural recovery and determinant maximization.
xo3Algm0r8.main_concern: The sufficient sample conditions are extremely demanding (about 480 million samples for the r=25, p=4 case) and the theory assumes noiseless data and global optima, leaving a large gap to experiments that are mostly qualitative and lack baseline comparisons.

1XQKFnGKk4.one_liner: Minimal-pair video benchmark testing whether MLLMs track single socially relevant differences in belief, goal and moral judgments.
1XQKFnGKk4.problem: It is unclear whether MLLMs reliably distinguish behaviors that differ in a single socially relevant factor, even though small differences can change interpretations of beliefs, goals and norms.
1XQKFnGKk4.method: SMORE has 427 video pairs (854 videos) and 1,281 questions on belief-conditioned rationality, helping and hindering, and intentionality, responsibility and norm violations; each pair shares actors, environment and interaction but differs in one factor. Models are tested with paired-video relative discrimination and single-video absolute evaluation, including Joint-Pair Accuracy.
1XQKFnGKk4.key_idea: Pair videos that differ in one socially relevant factor and credit a model only when it answers both members of the pair correctly.
1XQKFnGKk4.evidence: Multiple open-source and proprietary MLLMs compared with human baselines (65 annotators per a reviewer), on videos rendered in VirtualHome or generated with Gemini Omni.
1XQKFnGKk4.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before the human and model scores, and the TL;DR reports only a substantial gap between current models and humans.
1XQKFnGKk4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled minimal-pair design isolates sensitivity to behavioral differences, and the evaluation is broad, with human baselines and useful diagnostic analysis.
1XQKFnGKk4.main_concern: Scale and domain coverage are limited: about 50 pairs per sub-class, synthetic videos from two different pipelines (VirtualHome templates and Gemini Omni), and human validation of the generated videos is limited.

L0aAEhQKo6.one_liner: Convolutional autoencoder that learns temporally sparse, orthogonal-subspace latent factors from single-trial spiking activity.
L0aAEhQKo6.problem: Discovering distinct neural processes in single trials requires both disentangling signals mixed within neurons and denoising stochastic spiking in large populations.
L0aAEhQKo6.method: pSCA uses a convolutional autoencoder with a masked training procedure to seek latents that occur sparsely in time and reside in orthogonal subspaces, yielding denoised factors without prior knowledge of the processes' identity or timing.
L0aAEhQKo6.key_idea: Jointly learn Poisson denoising and sparse, orthogonal-subspace latent factors, with temporal filtering and coordinated dropout, so factors isolate distinct neural processes.
L0aAEhQKo6.evidence: Synthetic ground-truth simulations with ablations plus multiple mouse and monkey cortex recordings, including a macaque comparison of interpretability and held-out prediction.
L0aAEhQKo6.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims latents aligned with task events and behavioral variables and compositional structure, with no numbers.
L0aAEhQKo6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear and that jointly learning denoising and sparse factors recovers recognizable task-related structure in simulations and recordings.
L0aAEhQKo6.main_concern: Evidence that the factors are distinct neural processes is limited: behavioral selectivity is judged with the same labels used for interpretation, the method is incremental over SCA, and GPFA/LFADS-then-SCA baselines are missing.

jUA7xVo4V6.one_liner: Computes the exact worst-case asymptotic contraction factor of Nesterov's accelerated gradient for smooth strongly convex functions.
jUA7xVo4V6.problem: The exact worst-case asymptotic factor for the squared distance to the minimizer under Nesterov's method with its standard constant parameters was not characterized.
jUA7xVo4V6.method: Candidate worst-case trajectories combine planar spirals with a common contraction factor under a self-similarity condition, and the exact factor is the optimal value of a linear optimization problem over probability measures on a disk with smooth strongly convex interpolation constraints. The rate is realized by a single finite-dimensional function and matched by a uniform upper bound.
jUA7xVo4V6.key_idea: Build self-similar planar-spiral worst-case trajectories and optimize over probability measures on a disk under interpolation constraints to get the exact factor.
jUA7xVo4V6.evidence: Theory only: a matching lower bound realized by a single finite-dimensional function and a uniform upper bound over all functions in the class and all dimensions.
jUA7xVo4V6.claimed_gains: The exact factor is 1-4/(3√κ)+o(κ^{-1/2}) as κ→∞, where κ=L/μ is the ratio of the gradient Lipschitz constant to the strong convexity parameter.
jUA7xVo4V6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact asymptotic characterization is technically substantial, notably that one fixed objective attains the worst case and that the link to linear optimization over probability measures is interesting.
jUA7xVo4V6.main_concern: Significance and novelty relative to existing interpolation and performance-estimation work are questioned: the result fixes only a constant (4/3) for standard NAG, and slight modifications of AGD already achieve optimal rates.

RHWY8K0lke.one_liner: Bilinear probe finds a CLIP patch subspace binding objects to agent and patient roles; ablating it hurts role-swap matching.
RHWY8K0lke.problem: CLIP-style models fail to distinguish captions with swapped agent and patient roles, leaving open whether role information is absent from their representations or present but insufficiently used.
RHWY8K0lke.method: A bilinear probe is trained on ordered pairs of object patches to find a relation-binding subspace in CLIP-style ViT patch representations. The subspace is then ablated, and exchange interventions test how it affects image-text matching on role-swapped captions.
RHWY8K0lke.key_idea: Learn a bilinear probe over ordered patch pairs to isolate a low-dimensional role-binding subspace, then test it causally by ablation.
RHWY8K0lke.evidence: Probing, ablation and exchange-intervention experiments on CLIP-style ViT encoders, using one annotated dataset and few models (per a reviewer).
RHWY8K0lke.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says ablating the subspace reduces image-text matching accuracy on role-swapped captions more than on any other caption modification.
RHWY8K0lke.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well motivated and that combining probing, ablation and exchange interventions gives a coherent test of whether role information is encoded versus used.
RHWY8K0lke.main_concern: The probe may exploit category, typical-interaction or scene-context shortcuts rather than true object-to-role binding, and evaluation is limited to one dataset and few models.

roKrJAZ0Fh.one_liner: Analyzes off-policy correction rules for stale LLM RL rollouts via per-token coefficients and off-policy gradient alignment.
roKrJAZ0Fh.problem: LLM reinforcement learning increasingly reuses stale rollouts, and continued training on them can erode earlier gains, but what learning signal different off-policy corrections extract is unclear.
roKrJAZ0Fh.method: Each correction is factored into per-token advantage, weight and gate coefficients, gradient magnitude is separated from off-policy gradient alignment (OGA), and a local condition links alignment and step size to realized improvement. Policy drift is proposed as an observable state variable for reuse control and stopping rules.
roKrJAZ0Fh.key_idea: Measure how well each correction's update direction aligns with a fresh gradient (OGA) at shared model states, and use policy drift to decide when to stop reusing stale data.
roKrJAZ0Fh.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and instruction following with a Qwen3 1.7B model (one training seed per a reviewer), comparing correction rules on common checkpoints and stale responses, with one-step reward experiments and calibrated stopping rules.
roKrJAZ0Fh.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract says stopping rules calibrated on earlier runs limit late losses, but the sentence is cut off before any figures.
roKrJAZ0Fh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the comparisons at shared model states, holding the checkpoint and stale responses fixed, cleanly separate each correction operator's effect on a timely problem.
roKrJAZ0Fh.main_concern: The link to real training is not fully tested: one model scale (1.7B), two tasks and one seed, alignment measured before AdamW, a drift statistic that is not a true KL, and KL-based stopping barely beating fixed-step stopping.

Y2Yoidbgnf.one_liner: Defines a joint Bellman operator that truncates task value by a safety value, learned with two-timescale TD.
Y2Yoidbgnf.problem: Safe RL methods either need a priori knowledge for strict guarantees (such as safety filters) or learn jointly but satisfy safety constraints only on average.
Y2Yoidbgnf.method: A joint Bellman operator unifies performance and safety into one value function. Temporal-difference learning on it runs on two timescales, estimating the safety value of the joint policy on the fast timescale and the joint value on the slow timescale, with convergence shown through an occupation-averaged differential inclusion.
Y2Yoidbgnf.key_idea: Combine task and safety values in one Bellman operator with a safety-value truncation, learned with a fast safety timescale and a slow joint-value timescale.
Y2Yoidbgnf.evidence: Convergence theory under two-timescale stochastic approximation, tabular optimality tests, and continuous-control (MuJoCo) experiments with neural approximation under adversarial disturbances.
Y2Yoidbgnf.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports stable convergence with near-zero safety violations at test time on continuous control tasks.
Y2Yoidbgnf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint Bellman operator is a clear, conceptually clean idea backed by substantial theory and experiments in both tabular and function-approximation settings.
Y2Yoidbgnf.main_concern: Theory and practice are mismatched: guarantees assume a finite or tabular setting, while the continuous experiments show stable convergence under adversarial disturbances rather than optimality, and baseline and evaluation-adversary details are unclear.

jP1CaRJ03z.one_liner: Stochastically replaces student agent actions with teacher actions using KL-based probability, trained by importance-weighted reverse KL.
jP1CaRJ03z.problem: In multi-turn agentic tasks, early student errors accumulate and trajectories drift from the teacher's rollout distribution, making the teacher's token-level supervision unreliable or counterproductive for on-policy distillation.
jP1CaRJ03z.method: STI-OPD estimates teacher-student policy discrepancy with KL divergence, maps it to an intervention probability, and samples whether the teacher replaces the student's proposed action. An Importance-Weighted Reverse KL objective trains on the resulting mixed-policy trajectories.
jP1CaRJ03z.key_idea: Intervene stochastically with probability set by teacher-student KL, and correct for teacher-sampled tokens with importance weights in the reverse-KL loss.
jP1CaRJ03z.evidence: Multiple student and teacher sizes and tool-use agentic settings with baseline and ablation comparisons per reviews; the abstract is cut off before the results.
jP1CaRJ03z.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract is cut off before any results.
jP1CaRJ03z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the importance-weighting correction for teacher-sampled tokens is a principled contribution and the design is coherent, with broad baselines and ablations.
jP1CaRJ03z.main_concern: The theory does not match the implementation: the unbiased importance identity breaks under adaptive takeover and PPO-style ratio clipping, and the effect of the deviation is not quantified.

ujzMfQhwLV.one_liner: Shows MoE expert routing reflects hidden-state geometry through linear routers, not necessarily domain expertise.
ujzMfQhwLV.problem: The mechanisms behind expert specialization in Mixture-of-Experts language models remain poorly understood.
ujzMfQhwLV.method: Because routers are linear maps, hidden-state similarity is argued to explain expert-usage similarity at token and sequence level across five pre-trained models, and load-balancing loss is proven to suppress shared hidden-state directions. They then test whether routing patterns are human-interpretable via cross-model expert overlap, prompt-level versus rollout-level routing, and deep-layer activation.
ujzMfQhwLV.key_idea: Because routers are linear, routing similarity is bounded by hidden-state similarity, so specialization reflects representation geometry rather than domain-specific modules.
ujzMfQhwLV.evidence: Five pre-trained MoE models at token and sequence level, expert-pruning analyses contrasting prefill and decoding, and a small-scale load-balancing experiment.
ujzMfQhwLV.claimed_gains: not stated; the closest figure is about 60% expert overlap between different models answering the same question, no higher than between entirely different questions.
ujzMfQhwLV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric account is consistent across five pre-trained MoEs and usefully separates expert selection from functional expertise, including prefill versus generation.
ujzMfQhwLV.main_concern: The theory supports a narrower claim than 'necessary and sufficient': Proposition 1 is only an upper bound on routing differences, and the load-balancing result holds in a small-logit regime with limited experiments.

3ObHj7a5Re.one_liner: Extends semidefinite bound propagation to general activations using sector and quadratic bounds as optimizable linear bounds.
3ObHj7a5Re.problem: SDP-CROWN's quadratic outer approximation relies on ReLU's piecewise linear structure, and linear bound propagation loses tightness for general activations.
3ObHj7a5Re.method: Quadratic outer approximations are derived from sector bounds and quadratic bounds, converted into optimizable linear bounds over ellipsoidal domains that are refined recursively, and plugged into the standard bound-propagation recursion for l-infinity and l2 adversaries.
3ObHj7a5Re.key_idea: Convert sector and quadratic constraints on general activations into optimizable linear bounds over ellipsoids, keeping layer-wise linear bound propagation without solving dense SDPs.
3ObHj7a5Re.evidence: Verification benchmarks with general activations, measuring verified accuracy under a 300-second timeout against GenBaB on MNIST and CIFAR-10 feed-forward networks.
3ObHj7a5Re.claimed_gains: On representative benchmarks, verified accuracy over GenBaB improves from 12% to 57% on MNIST under l2 perturbations and from 23% to 87% on CIFAR-10 under l-infinity perturbations.
3ObHj7a5Re.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a principled generalization of SDP-CROWN that keeps bound propagation scalable and shows consistent verification gains on general-activation networks.
3ObHj7a5Re.main_concern: Runtime, memory and implementation details are missing (number of bounds and ellipsoids, optimizer, branch-and-bound setup, no code), and positioning against prior quadratic-constraint SDP verification work (Fazlyab et al.) is unclear.

RlytBuXm9m.one_liner: Neural-process-style amortized inference of a shared latent intensity from variable-size sets of replicated point patterns.
RlytBuXm9m.problem: Bayesian inference of latent point-process intensities usually relies on per-dataset sampling or optimization, which makes repeated inference computationally expensive.
RlytBuXm9m.method: A Neural Process-based amortized variational framework maps a variable-size set of realizations sharing a latent intensity to a variational distribution over that intensity in a single forward pass, trained from event times with the point process likelihood and no intensity supervision.
RlytBuXm9m.key_idea: Pool replicated realizations with a permutation-invariant encoder into a variational posterior over the shared intensity, trained end-to-end on the point-process likelihood.
RlytBuXm9m.evidence: Synthetic data (intensity recovery and credible-interval coverage as realizations increase) and bicycle-sharing data compared with LGCP and other baselines such as FIM-PP, PSTH and KDE.
RlytBuXm9m.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says it achieves the highest mean held-out log likelihood on bicycle-sharing data among evaluated approaches and substantially less inference time than the LGCP baseline.
RlytBuXm9m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses a practically relevant problem and combines low inference cost with accurate intensity recovery and uncertainty quantification.
RlytBuXm9m.main_concern: Baselines and novelty are weak: no multi-pattern baseline from the introduction, only held-out log likelihood on real data, missing standard deviations for some baselines, and the replicated setting may reduce to standard intensity inference with an exposure factor.

2M4nt7AFuD.one_liner: Learns state-conditioned corrections to CLS attention outputs of a frozen receiver to repair model stitching.
2M4nt7AFuD.problem: The effect of a stitching mismatch varies sharply with receiver state, so downstream accuracy alone does not characterize functional compatibility.
