2M4nt7AFuD.method: Controlled token and attention interventions identify messages from patch tokens to CLS as the key pathway. RIMA (Receiver Internal Message Adaptation) then learns state-conditioned corrections to CLS attention outputs while keeping the pretrained models and stitch frozen.
2M4nt7AFuD.key_idea: Correct the CLS attention outputs of the frozen receiver with small state-conditioned adapters, targeting the patch-to-CLS pathway identified by interventions.
2M4nt7AFuD.evidence: Heterogeneous model pairs and classification benchmarks against conventional stitch optimization and parameter-matched receiver adaptation, with intervention analyses across model families, stitching directions, interface locations and objectives.
2M4nt7AFuD.claimed_gains: On DeiT B to DeiT S, RIMA adds 0.02M trainable parameters and improves ImageNet 1K top 1 accuracy from 68.538% to 73.752%.
2M4nt7AFuD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers largely agree that the receiver-side interventions motivate the RIMA design and that the experiments suggest benefits for model stitching, with clear statistical reporting.
2M4nt7AFuD.main_concern: Comparisons and ablations are missing: no LoRA or other parameter-efficient baselines, no ablations of state conditioning, features, location or loss, and the paper is hard to follow (for example undefined 'receiver states').

X9p1kvkC0e.one_liner: Pairs top and bottom views with fold-contact affordance maps and an online bandit scorer for cloth unfolding.
X9p1kvkC0e.problem: Visible shape alone can leave support and fold relationships ambiguous, since the same overhead silhouette can conceal different arrangements of folds and support.
X9p1kvkC0e.method: A transparent-table dual-arm setup pairs a top segmentation mask with a bottom contact mask. Fold residual, contact overlap, fold-contact frontier and silhouette-edge maps feed an attention encoder and a residual action prior, and an online linear contextual-bandit-style scorer adapts the prior's target ranking from reward, self-supervised progress, or a mixture.
X9p1kvkC0e.key_idea: Derive parameter-free fold-contact affordance channels from top and bottom masks and connect them to grasp-target selection through an online bandit scorer.
X9p1kvkC0e.evidence: Long-horizon cloth-unfolding comparisons in simulation (a randomized campaign, a fast screen and a 21-run residual-prior ablation) plus real garments with manual fold checks.
X9p1kvkC0e.claimed_gains: Affordance channels reduce folded area by 82.2% relative to raw dual masks in a fast screen, and the reward-bandit bottom-view scorer performs best in the 21-run residual-prior ablation with within-panel geometry score 0.840 ± 0.047.
X9p1kvkC0e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dual-view sensing and parameter-free affordance channels are intuitive, well motivated and tied explicitly to control, with controlled comparisons and real-world evaluation.
X9p1kvkC0e.main_concern: Practical reach is limited: the method needs a transparent table with accurate view registration, fails on 3–4 layer stacks, and key details (reward weights, progress formula, gating) are underspecified.

VlcNX0DTOY.one_liner: Benchmark and training-free search framework for deciding when LLM agents should ask clarifying questions about incomplete optimization problems.
VlcNX0DTOY.problem: Real operations-research requests are often incomplete, yet existing evaluations assume a complete specification and overlook whether agents know when to clarify before modeling.
VlcNX0DTOY.method: OR-Clarify presents partial problem descriptions with hidden structured slots and evaluates agents through bounded interaction with a simulated user, in open-ended and choice-based protocols. InterOPT is a two-stage framework that identifies unresolved formulation-critical gaps and uses them to decide whether to ask the next question or stop.
VlcNX0DTOY.key_idea: Track unresolved formulation-critical gaps explicitly and use them to choose the next clarifying question or to stop asking.
VlcNX0DTOY.evidence: Choice-based and open-ended experiments on OR-Clarify with a simulated user, measuring slot recovery, stopping behavior, silent assumptions and interaction cost against baselines and prior methods such as ORPilot and GATE.
VlcNX0DTOY.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; InterOPT substantially outperforms all baselines in exact slot recovery in choice-based experiments and remains competitive with strong prior methods in the open-ended setting.
VlcNX0DTOY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree pre-formulation clarification is a meaningful, practically relevant problem and the benchmark with hidden-slot annotations and simulated users is a useful evaluation.
VlcNX0DTOY.main_concern: Evidence for InterOPT is narrow and not tied to final models: it wins clearly only under the choice protocol against the authors' own baselines, no end-to-end check shows recovered slots yield better optimization models, and all benchmark cases contain missing requirements.

FfRlG0JV9Q.one_liner: Searches continuous semantic directions from population anchors, scored by history-conditioned expected best response among real items.
FfRlG0JV9Q.problem: Recommenders usually choose the next item, but interest exploration and generative recommendation first need to decide where in content space to go next.
FfRlG0JV9Q.method: NORTH learns behavioral representations from shared population feedback; the user's history turns population opportunity into a personalized direction score. A learned policy starts from population anchors, decides where to search and whether to stay or move, and proposes continuous displacements, each grounded in a fixed-size core of real items and scored by the same scorer.
FfRlG0JV9Q.key_idea: Learn a personalized direction scorer over population-derived behavioral representations and search continuous displacements from anchors, grounded in fixed-size cores of real items.
FfRlG0JV9Q.evidence: KuaiRec-Full and KuaiRec-FO, evaluated with Best-Realization Value (the best observed response within a fixed realization budget) against population-only bank selection and OPEN generators, with ablations.
FfRlG0JV9Q.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; NORTH exceeds population-only bank selection in all four evaluated settings and leads the compared OPEN generators on KuaiRec-Full and KuaiRec-FO.
FfRlG0JV9Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reframing recommendation as next semantic direction selection is a principled, well-motivated formulation with a comparable fixed-size real-item realization budget.
FfRlG0JV9Q.main_concern: The added value of continuous search is not isolated from simpler baselines (such as the personalized bank incumbent), and key details and evaluation scope (KuaiRec only, BRV needing fully observed sets) are under-specified.

knv4wu3JP5.one_liner: Interleaves gradient ascent on target-domain data into pretraining so unwanted knowledge is harder to recover by fine-tuning.
knv4wu3JP5.problem: Open-weight language models can be fine-tuned to acquire hazardous knowledge, and post-pretraining unlearning is quickly undone while corpus filtering offers only partial resistance.
knv4wu3JP5.method: DETER interleaves simple gradient ascent on the target domain (medical PubMed text) with standard pretraining, and varies suppression strength to trade off fine-tuning difficulty against held-out loss on retained pretraining data.
knv4wu3JP5.key_idea: Actively suppress target-domain knowledge during pretraining by interleaving gradient-ascent steps with ordinary pretraining.
knv4wu3JP5.evidence: Models pretrained from scratch at three sizes compared with filtering, token filtering and post-hoc RMU, using adversarial PubMed fine-tuning, held-out loss, downstream tasks and three fine-tuning seeds.
knv4wu3JP5.claimed_gains: At 0.5B parameters, reaching the held-out PubMed loss of an unfiltered model requires over 13× as many PubMed fine-tuning tokens as after filtering alone.
knv4wu3JP5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the simple interleaved gradient ascent is effective in a clean controlled study, beating filtering, token filtering and post-hoc RMU, with the gap growing with model size.
knv4wu3JP5.main_concern: The evidence does not isolate pretraining as the key stage or show robustness: resistance is small in absolute terms against a single full-fine-tuning attack, each size uses one pretraining seed, and late-onset suppression suggests timing matters.

o1OZndgUCX.one_liner: Derives Pareto frontiers between worst-case and expected competitiveness under pure tail constraints for online bidding, line search, and TCP acknowledgment.
o1OZndgUCX.problem: Tail risk in competitive analysis has been studied only for non-adaptive online problems, where algorithm feedback is essentially a binary success indicator.
o1OZndgUCX.method: A worst-case ratio bound is fixed and randomization is allowed only over deterministic algorithms meeting it (per a reviewer). Exact Pareto frontiers are derived for online bidding and line search, a TCP acknowledgment algorithm matches ski rental's known tradeoff, and constraints implied by tail bounds give a nontrivial lower bound in the adaptive TCP setting.
o1OZndgUCX.key_idea: Restrict randomization to deterministic algorithms with bounded worst-case ratio, using a step-ratio lemma that forces geometric search sequences.
o1OZndgUCX.evidence: Theoretical analysis only: exact frontiers for online bidding and line search, and an algorithm plus lower bound for TCP acknowledgment.
o1OZndgUCX.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract states exact Pareto-optimal frontiers for online bidding and line search and a TCP acknowledgment algorithm whose tradeoff coincides with the known ski rental tradeoff.
o1OZndgUCX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact frontiers and the step-ratio lemma are substantive theoretical contributions that give clear structural insight into dependability constraints.
o1OZndgUCX.main_concern: For TCP acknowledgment the upper and lower bounds do not match, and the constructive strategies largely adapt established algorithms, so novelty rests mainly on the lower-bound techniques.

8nVhRvPkoB.one_liner: Computes the fewest closure-orientation retractions that invalidate a chosen adjustment set under expert background knowledge.
8nVhRvPkoB.problem: Expert knowledge can fix uncertain edge orientations in an equivalence class, but there is no query-specific measure of how many wrong assertions a chosen adjustment set can survive, and structural Hamming distance is a poor proxy.
8nVhRvPkoB.method: The breakdown radius is the fewest closure orientations that must be contradicted before a fixed adjustment set can fail, given a correct equivalence class, computed exactly by retractions (with a SAT certificate and upward search) without enumerating knowledge states.
8nVhRvPkoB.key_idea: Count the minimal contradicted Meek-closure orientations needed to invalidate an adjustment set, computed by retraction search with a SAT certificate.
8nVhRvPkoB.evidence: Over 4,000 synthetic instances with three- and four-tier knowledge corruption and 33 published networks with LLM-elicited knowledge across six language models, compared with structural Hamming distance and a graph-separation proxy.
8nVhRvPkoB.claimed_gains: On targeted synthetic graphs the breakdown radius tracks survival to corrupted knowledge at a rank correlation of 0.75 to 0.81 versus at most 0.14 for structural Hamming distance; without targeting, the radius ranks survival at 0.29 and the structural proxy separation at 0.34.
8nVhRvPkoB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the metric is clearly formulated, addresses an interesting robustness question relevant to LLM-assisted causal discovery, and is evaluated on both synthetic graphs and published networks.
8nVhRvPkoB.main_concern: Practicality is unclear: there is no complexity analysis for an apparently hard computation, the choice of SAT, search depth and other design parameters is under-motivated, and the method assumes a correct equivalence class.

adgpjDiBa8.one_liner: Mirror-descent bandit convex optimization on the simplex using multinomial sampling policies and a mixed count and self-normalized score.
adgpjDiBa8.problem: Large-scale simplex optimization from noisy one-point feedback needs regret bounds with good dependence on the dimension K, but the multinomial policy value can be nonconvex.
adgpjDiBa8.method: A multinomial-policy mirror descent algorithm uses a weighted score mixing a count score with a self-normalized score, which lets the analysis compare the policy value with the original convex objective. Worst-case regret bounds, support-dependent bounds for sparse optimizers, and matching lower bounds are proved.
adgpjDiBa8.key_idea: Sample allocations from a multinomial policy and update with a weighted mix of count and self-normalized scores, comparing the nonconvex policy value to the convex objective.
adgpjDiBa8.evidence: Regret upper and lower bound theory plus numerical experiments against benchmarks, using separable test objectives per a reviewer.
adgpjDiBa8.claimed_gains: Worst-case regret bounds of order Õ(K^{1/2}T^{3/4}) for general convex objectives and Õ(K^{1/3}T^{2/3}) for smooth objectives, with matching worst-case lower bounds for sufficiently large horizons.
adgpjDiBa8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multinomial construction is natural and the improved dependence on K is a valuable theoretical contribution that handles the nonconvex policy value carefully.
adgpjDiBa8.main_concern: Significance and practical scope are limited: the horizon exponents match classical one-point methods, the bound is nontrivial only for a narrow range of K versus T, MP-convexity is a method-specific assumption, and experiments use simple separable objectives.

DmheI1vMDA.one_liner: Proves a canonical form for shallow networks with uncoupling activations and characterizes all equivariant constraints, including inter-layer ones.
DmheI1vMDA.problem: Prior work characterized only single-output invariant shallow ReLU networks (Agrawal and Ostrowski, 2022), leaving modern activations and general equivariance unaddressed.
DmheI1vMDA.method: They prove existence and uniqueness of a canonical form for shallow networks whose activations are uncoupling (including GELU, SiLU and ELU), then characterize all equivariant shallow networks as equivariance constraints on weights and biases, including exotic inter-layer constraints beyond layerwise equivariance.
DmheI1vMDA.key_idea: Fix a canonical form for shallow networks with uncoupling activations so equivariance reduces to explicit parameter constraints, some of which couple layers.
DmheI1vMDA.evidence: Mathematical proofs plus comparisons of optimization behavior between layerwise and exotic networks and tests of equivariant structures in the MLP blocks of equivariant vision transformers (ViT-L per a reviewer).
DmheI1vMDA.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims layerwise and exotic networks can have qualitatively different optimization behavior, without numbers.
DmheI1vMDA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and gives a meaningful, mathematically sound framework that extends equivariance characterizations to modern activations and beyond layerwise symmetry.
DmheI1vMDA.main_concern: Practical impact is unclear and the experimental conclusions are overstated: the baseline reaches 75.9% top-1 versus 75.1% for the layerwise variant, exotic models use periodic projection, and the evaluation is narrow.

FszvpTQqwg.one_liner: Retrieves reference videos at test time to complete partially observed objects in video outpainting with decoupled spatial-temporal adaptation.
FszvpTQqwg.problem: Video outpainting struggles with object-level appearance and motion consistency in complex scenes because objects near the frame boundary are only partially observed.
FszvpTQqwg.method: RAVO retrieves relevant videos to complement incomplete object observations and adapts at test time with Object-Specific Adaptation (learns transferable part-level correspondences while retaining source identity cues) and Spatial-Temporal Decoupled Adaptation (separately adapts spatial appearance and temporal dynamics).
FszvpTQqwg.key_idea: Test-time adapt a video outpainting model on retrieved reference objects using part-level correspondences and separate spatial and temporal adaptation instead of coupled 3D attention.
FszvpTQqwg.evidence: Comparisons with existing outpainting methods, ablations on retrieval and decoupling (Table 3, LPIPS and FVD), and a proposed ObjectBench; the abstract is cut off before results.
FszvpTQqwg.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract gives no figures.
FszvpTQqwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrieving external object references addresses a practical limitation of video outpainting and that qualitative results show more complete, consistent objects.
FszvpTQqwg.main_concern: Novelty and evidence are unclear: STDA builds on existing attention decoupling and OSA on established components, sensitivity to retrieval quality is untested, and ablations and ObjectBench construction are incomplete.

bRUtHtqtC3.one_liner: Adds structured audio-primitive supervision and shallow-layer acoustic gating to a single-codebook semantic speech tokenizer for general audio.
bRUtHtqtC3.problem: Semantic speech tokenizers focus on linguistic abstraction, causing acoustic blindness that limits their use beyond speech-centric tasks.
bRUtHtqtC3.method: Semantic-Acoustic Primitives (SAP) supervise the tokenizer by decomposing audio into linguistic content, vocal attributes, and auditory-scene primitives. Semantic-Acoustic Equilibrium (SAE) uses a content-aware gate to add informative acoustic cues from shallow layers.
bRUtHtqtC3.key_idea: Structured three-part primitive supervision plus a content-aware gate that injects shallow-layer acoustic features into a semantic tokenizer's representation.
bRUtHtqtC3.evidence: Evaluated on speech reconstruction and TTS, and with a downstream LLM on audio understanding and generation (reviews cite a Qwen2.5-3B backbone with MMAU, MMAR, MMSU, and ESC-50 cluster purity).
bRUtHtqtC3.claimed_gains: No numbers in the abstract; it claims to outperform all single-codebook baselines on both understanding and generation when integrated with downstream LLMs.
bRUtHtqtC3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is relevant and the single-codebook tokenizer gives strong general audio understanding while keeping good speech reconstruction and TTS quality.
bRUtHtqtC3.main_concern: Limited methodological novelty and missing related work on hybrid semantic-acoustic tokenizers (e.g., SPEAR, DashengTokenizer), with SAP's gain not isolated from extra training data.

dO5dyGWc9P.one_liner: Learns attribution-oriented step representations from frozen-LLM hidden states using contrastive and ranking losses to locate root-cause failures in agent trajectories.
dO5dyGWc9P.problem: Hidden states used as step representations for failure attribution in LLM-based agent systems separate root-cause steps from other steps poorly.
dO5dyGWc9P.method: ReCast selects attribution-relevant layers of a frozen LLM, builds complementary pattern and deviation features, and trains an encoder with contrastive and ranking objectives to produce contextualized step representations. It also introduces ReCast-2K, a training dataset for failure attribution.
dO5dyGWc9P.key_idea: Select attribution-relevant layers of frozen-LLM hidden states, form pattern and deviation features, and train a contextual encoder with contrastive and ranking losses to rank root-cause steps.
dO5dyGWc9P.evidence: An empirical study of hidden-state separation, then evaluation on four failure-attribution benchmarks (including Who&When Algorithm and Handcrafted, AFTraj-2K, TraceElephant) with ablations and repeated experiments.
dO5dyGWc9P.claimed_gains: Best Hit@1 across four benchmarks, surpassing the strongest baseline by 5.65 and 9.19 pp on Who&When Algorithm and Handcrafted.
dO5dyGWc9P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the attribution-oriented representation idea is well motivated and gives consistent gains over baselines across multiple benchmarks, with ablations supporting each component.
dO5dyGWc9P.main_concern: Comparisons with embedding-based baselines are confounded by different input features and learning frameworks, and ReCast-2K labels from LLM voting plus manual review may not satisfy the counterfactual root-cause definition.

CxWnjRy2cg.one_liner: Learns a shared Bayesian token-level reward model from demonstrations, preferences, edits, ratings, and stops, each with its own likelihood.
CxWnjRy2cg.problem: Post-training pipelines rely mainly on demonstrations and preferences, leaving other feedback types underused and without a way to learn from them jointly.
CxWnjRy2cg.method: Each feedback type is modeled through its own likelihood over a latent token-level reward, and Bayesian inference learns a shared distribution over rewards. The resulting probabilistic reward model supplies dense rewards with uncertainty estimates and is then used to optimize the policy (MELT).
CxWnjRy2cg.key_idea: Treat every feedback type as an observation of one latent token-level reward with a feedback-specific likelihood, and infer a shared posterior with Bayesian inference.
CxWnjRy2cg.evidence: Four mathematical reasoning benchmarks for best-of-16 selection, RewardBench safety ranking, error-localization experiments, and policy optimization on three math reasoning benchmarks versus SFT+DPO and scalar-reward PPO.
CxWnjRy2cg.claimed_gains: Best feedback combinations improve best-of-16 selection accuracy over a scalar preference-trained reward model by up to 3.7 percentage points, and policy optimization matches or beats SFT followed by DPO or scalar-reward PPO on three benchmarks.
CxWnjRy2cg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying diverse feedback types in one token-level reward model is practical and technically solid, and that token-level rewards help error localization and PPO.
CxWnjRy2cg.main_concern: Gains are hard to attribute: the scalar baseline uses only preferences, benefits do not hold on RewardBench 2 math, more feedback types sometimes hurt (safety), and a style shortcut on the RewardBench math subset is suspected.

1vmM17t1R8.one_liner: Shows early CEM search rounds, not late ones, decide world-model planning outcomes, and proposes Exact-to-Local CEM.
1vmM17t1R8.problem: Sampling-based planners give every candidate in every round the same full world-model evaluation, and it is unclear which evaluations actually shape the decision.
1vmM17t1R8.method: They replace scores at chosen search stages with a run-time linear operator while holding the world model and planner fixed, and compare effects across rounds. E2L-CEM scores early rounds exactly, scores later rounds with the operator refitted every few rounds, and reinvests the time saved in the search.
1vmM17t1R8.key_idea: Score early CEM rounds exactly and approximate later rounds with a linear operator refitted every few rounds, since proposal contraction shrinks late selection errors.
1vmM17t1R8.evidence: Pretrained latent world models on PushT, Reacher, and Two-Room with CEM, iCEM, and MPPI planners, using paired comparisons, noise controls, and early-stopping comparisons.
1vmM17t1R8.claimed_gains: Approximating late-round scores does not change success detectably on any task, and on PushT the operator's displacement falls 2.7-fold across rounds while its rank correlation stays at 0.21-0.28.
1vmM17t1R8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the stage-wise controlled experiments (fixed world model and planner, paired comparisons, noise controls) give useful evidence that evaluation timing matters, with real runtime reported.
1vmM17t1R8.main_concern: E2L's practical advantage over simply stopping CEM early is small or unresolved, and novelty over prior evaluation-scheduling work is insufficiently established.

9YVNlDplEi.one_liner: Empirically shows that model growth, boundary operators, and recursion can improve scaling-law exponents, using 30+ scaling ladders.
9YVNlDplEi.problem: How architecture changes affect scaling-law coefficients, meaning the constant versus the exponent, is rarely examined.
9YVNlDplEi.method: They run more than 30 distinct scaling ladders over roughly 10^18 to 10^20 FLOPs with per-architecture tuning, and compare variants such as Untied-Grow (untied model growth with a boundary operator). They also analyze computational depth to explain the gains.
9YVNlDplEi.key_idea: Architectural changes (growth, boundary operators, untied versus shared-weight recursion) can raise scaling exponents, and exponent gains correlate with faster growth in computational depth.
9YVNlDplEi.evidence: More than 30 scaling ladders at about 10^18 to 10^20 FLOPs, extrapolation to 10^21 FLOPs compared with GPT-3 13B on CORE, and multi-epoch data-constrained experiments.
9YVNlDplEi.claimed_gains: Untied-Grow achieves a 1.55x compute-efficiency gain at 10^20 FLOPs, and the trend extrapolates to 10^21 FLOPs, where the model matches GPT-3 13B on CORE.
9YVNlDplEi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparisons, with separately tuned recipes per architecture, are the main strength and show architecture matters for scaling laws.
9YVNlDplEi.main_concern: Uncertainty in the exponent comparisons is understated (loss floor fixed from the vanilla fit, very small exponent differences), and inference cost and larger-scale data-constrained results are not covered.

15WIjPDesA.one_liner: Explains AdEMAMix's advantage over AdamW: a slow momentum raises parameter norms, acting as an endogenous annealing schedule.
15WIjPDesA.problem: Multiple momentum timescales improve LLM pretraining over AdamW, but the mechanism behind the gain is poorly understood.
15WIjPDesA.method: They derive exact norm dynamics under decoupled weight decay, showing the parameter norm depends on the temporal correlation of updates, and run controlled interventions (such as norm transplants) on AdEMAMix language-model pretraining.
15WIjPDesA.key_idea: A slow momentum with independent weight raises parameter norm while adding negligible instantaneous update power, which slows parameter rotation and acts as an annealing schedule.
15WIjPDesA.evidence: Exact norm-dynamics theory plus controlled interventions in AdEMAMix language-model pretraining (norm transplant, removing radial updates, fixing radius per reviews), on a single model size with single seeds.
15WIjPDesA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory gives a clear explanation of how slow momentum changes parameter norms and relative update sizes, and that interventions such as norm transplants support it.
15WIjPDesA.main_concern: The main LLM evidence comes from one model size and single seeds with no variance reported, and the interventions do not fully isolate the norm mechanism.

kXZkkYseBp.one_liner: Benchmarks whether tool-using LLM agents disclose private records on self-asserted requester claims, across 275 live tasks in four apps.
kXZkkYseBp.problem: Existing benchmarks do not separate evidence that a claimed identity is eligible from evidence of who the requester actually is when agents decide whether to disclose records.
kXZkkYseBp.method: SaysWho has 275 live recipient-authorization tasks across Gmail, Notion, Slack, and Discord, evaluated in stages on 12 models: forged blind-role claims with no identity evidence, then a directory of people's names and relationships, then a trusted requester identity supplied by the system.
kXZkkYseBp.key_idea: Isolate recipient authorization by varying independent requester-identity evidence (none, eligibility directory, trusted system identity) while holding the request text fixed.
kXZkkYseBp.evidence: 275 live tasks derived from PrivacyLens on Gmail, Notion, Slack, and Discord, 12 models, staged evaluation with paired tests, multiple-comparison corrections, and confidence intervals.
kXZkkYseBp.claimed_gains: Benchmark finding rather than a gain: forged blind-role claims raise disclosure, e.g., DeepSeek V4 Flash from 8.4% to 70.8%, and a directory reduces disclosure to unsupported claims in all 12 models.
kXZkkYseBp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between eligibility evidence and requester identity is important and that the controlled comparisons (directory on or off, identity supplied) make the failure clear.
kXZkkYseBp.main_concern: The setting's practicality is unclear (an agent with record access deciding who may receive them), benchmark labels are weakly validated (only 73 of 275 protected facts passed the strict source check), and there is no mitigation control.

dLmZ7qe8hE.one_liner: Adds an advantage-side off-policy correction with two-sided clipped TD reweighting to token-level ratio masking for asynchronous LLM RL.
dLmZ7qe8hE.problem: Asynchronous LLM RL trains on stale trajectories, and policy-side importance-ratio control alone leaves advantage estimates mismatched with the behavior policy (advantage staleness).
dLmZ7qe8hE.method: COPC is an actor-critic method that combines token-level ratio masking on the policy side with a dedicated advantage-side correction, and coordinates the strengths of the two channels using derived bias and variance decompositions for a two-channel actor update.
dLmZ7qe8hE.key_idea: Correct both policy weights and advantage estimates for staleness, coordinating the two channels because their errors couple multiplicatively in bias and amplify variance.
dLmZ7qe8hE.evidence: Math and search tasks on Qwen and Llama models against six baselines, with ablations (e.g., COPC without ratio correction) and a joint sweep of the two correction strengths; reviews note single runs.
dLmZ7qe8hE.claimed_gains: The visible abstract is truncated before results; a review quotes it as stating gains persist at 64-step policy staleness.
dLmZ7qe8hE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree advantage staleness is a real, practical problem in asynchronous LLM RL and that the advantage-side correction is simple, low-overhead, and shown to matter by ablation.
dLmZ7qe8hE.main_concern: The advantage-side correction closely resembles Retrace/V-trace without clear discussion, and results use single runs with untuned baselines and possibly test-selected hyperparameters.

fExXlIkcJY.one_liner: Shows political-persona prompting restructures LLM representation geometry, shifting semantic axes and making truthfulness and morality probes give slanted ratings.
fExXlIkcJY.problem: Activation-monitoring methods assume features keep a consistent representation across contexts, but personas may change the underlying conceptual relations.
fExXlIkcJY.method: They extract representations of over 9,000 common words and 33 semantic axes from models prompted as liberal or conservative personas, compare them with two neutral baselines, and apply linear probes, SAE-based classifiers, and word-representation classifiers trained without a persona to persona-conditioned models.
fExXlIkcJY.key_idea: Compare word and semantic-axis geometry under persona prompts against neutral baselines, then apply probes trained without a persona to persona-conditioned models to expose representation shift.
fExXlIkcJY.evidence: Eight models across families (per reviews), analyses across layers, comparison with political text corpora, and steering experiments linking geometry to behavior.
fExXlIkcJY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric shifts are consistent across models and layers, backed by baseline checks, corpus comparisons, and steering experiments linking geometry to behavior.
fExXlIkcJY.main_concern: Truth and morality probe results rely on statements labeled by expected partisan endorsement rather than ground truth, and the scope is limited to American liberal and conservative personas.

ScBr29kgTF.one_liner: Refines UI-to-code output by grounding visual discrepancies to DOM components and applying render-verified local code patches.
ScBr29kgTF.problem: Full-page refinement of VLM-generated webpages leaves the link between a local visual error and its responsible code implicit and can disturb already-correct regions.
ScBr29kgTF.method: IterUI detects discrepancies between a reference screenshot and the current render, grounds them to DOM components, and generates patches from localized visual evidence, component code, and ancestor layout context, accepting each only after full-page render verification. It also trains IterUI-Coder-8B on refinement trajectories (with GSRPO per reviews).
ScBr29kgTF.key_idea: Treat refinement as local visual code editing: pair a DOM-grounded component with an executable patch, mask non-target pixels, and accept it only if the full-page render verifies.
ScBr29kgTF.evidence: Evaluation on over a thousand examples across four UI-to-code datasets, a controlled pilot, component and training analyses, and a human evaluation by three frontend developers.
ScBr29kgTF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that DOM-grounded local editing with full-page render verification is a practical alternative to full-page regeneration and that the pipeline is coherent.
ScBr29kgTF.main_concern: It is not cleanly shown that local editing, rather than render verification and candidate selection, drives the gains, and benefits are inconsistent across configurations.

uUEYnWlfrv.one_liner: Grafts frozen 3D reconstruction features, bound to robot-relative metric coordinates, into a flow-matching action expert via cross-attention.
uUEYnWlfrv.problem: Pretrained VLAs and world-action models leave interaction-relevant metric geometry implicit, and reconstruction features lack robot-relative positional grounding.
uUEYnWlfrv.method: A lightweight module binds frozen reconstruction features to metric, robot-relative geometry to form spatial tokens, which are cross-attended into the late layers of the flow-matching action expert without modifying the host's perceptual pathway.
uUEYnWlfrv.key_idea: Bind frozen reconstruction latents to end-effector-relative metric coordinates and inject them by cross-attention into late layers of the action expert, leaving the host's perception untouched.
uUEYnWlfrv.evidence: Two VLAs and two world-action models, four simulation benchmarks (including RoboTwin 2.0), and three real-robot platforms with single- and dual-arm configurations.
uUEYnWlfrv.claimed_gains: On RoboTwin 2.0 the graft improves every host, and with simulator depth π₀.₅ gains 10.9 (rest truncated in the batch); a review cites real-robot success rising from 23/60 to 45/60.
uUEYnWlfrv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree one graft interface improves all four tested hosts on RoboTwin across VLAs and world-action models, with real-robot results adding support.
uUEYnWlfrv.main_concern: Metric, end-effector-relative grounding is not isolated by matched controls (extra features or capacity could explain the gains), and prior work such as FALCON, Act3D, and 3D Diffuser Actor covers much of the design.

vLHXDi6ZEs.one_liner: Learns cost-aware LLM routers from sparse model feedback by acquiring informative feedback and sharing capability information across related queries.
vLHXDi6ZEs.problem: Training a router needs costly execution of candidate models on historical queries, and prior work ignores whether serving savings recover this upfront supervision cost.
vLHXDi6ZEs.method: SaveRouter selectively acquires informative query-model feedback and shares capability information across related queries, while keeping query-level refinement for fine-grained routing. Routing is evaluated by jointly counting supervision expenditure and serving-time savings.
vLHXDi6ZEs.key_idea: Actively acquire only informative query-model quality feedback, share capability estimates across query groups, and refine per query, judged by break-even deployment volume.
vLHXDi6ZEs.evidence: Four routing benchmarks plus an appendix benchmark, supervision-budget analyses, and model-pool expansion experiments.
vLHXDi6ZEs.claimed_gains: Uses about 33-41% of available training feedback while keeping competitive or better routing quality, and reduces break-even deployment volume by about 1.9-9.5x versus the fastest conventional router.
vLHXDi6ZEs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that counting supervision cost when deploying routers is practical and relevant, and that the evaluation (four benchmarks, budget analyses, model-pool expansion) is reasonably comprehensive.
vLHXDi6ZEs.main_concern: Strong baselines such as kNN and EmbedLLM are run with full supervision, so budget-matched comparisons are missing, and the margin over the best baseline is very small on some benchmarks without uncertainty estimates.

SRe6x2HBqk.one_liner: Optimizes agent harnesses by localizing consequential decisions from failures and installing executable local controllers at explicit runtime boundaries.
SRe6x2HBqk.problem: Runtime decisions in agent harnesses (tool use, state changes, error recovery) are hard to optimize jointly because intervention placement, signals, and policies interact.
SRe6x2HBqk.method: Backward localization finds consequential decisions from residual failures within runtime boundaries that constrain observable signals and feasible interventions; an optimizer searches local policies and expands the signal representation when search stalls. Accepted controllers are installed sequentially, with residuals re-mined and candidates compared against the evolving incumbent.
SRe6x2HBqk.key_idea: Decompose harness optimization into sequentially installed, boundary-constrained local controllers found by backward failure localization and judged by downstream task value.
SRe6x2HBqk.evidence: Experiments on BFCL Agent Memory and AppWorld across multiple host models, plus composition with GEPA prompt optimization.
SRe6x2HBqk.claimed_gains: Stated as improvements across multiple host models and environments and additional gains when composed with GEPA; no numbers in the visible abstract.
SRe6x2HBqk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree harness-level optimization is a timely, practical problem and that tying interventions to explicit boundaries with executable controllers is a sensible design.
SRe6x2HBqk.main_concern: Gains are modest and inconsistent against baselines (GEPA is better on some host and benchmark pairs), and the method section is hard to follow with heavy notation and unclear inputs and outputs.

BtlwC1vGkY.one_liner: Benchmark of 17 dynamic VRPTW approaches across 135 demand configurations varying scale, dynamism, arrival pattern, and spatial evolution.
BtlwC1vGkY.problem: Existing dynamic VRP benchmarks model demand with limited realism and rarely vary several demand factors jointly, so they cannot show when each method has an advantage.
BtlwC1vGkY.method: DVRPTW-Bench evaluates 17 approaches covering decision timing, dispatch, and routing on 135 demand configurations with 10 instances each, varying problem scale, degree of dynamism, temporal arrival pattern, and spatial demand evolution.
BtlwC1vGkY.key_idea: A factorial grid over four demand factors crossed with three planning components (decision timing, dispatch, routing) under one protocol, to locate where each method wins.
BtlwC1vGkY.evidence: 17 approaches on 135 configurations with 10 instances each, plus analyses of computational budgets, training distributions, and trigger sweeps.
BtlwC1vGkY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are extensive and well organized across many methods and demand configurations, and that the three-component framing helps interpret results.
BtlwC1vGkY.main_concern: Novelty and insight are limited because components come from existing work, and findings may reflect a mismatch between static training and small dynamic snapshots plus confounded demand factors.

xXJTi2nkrq.one_liner: Low-rank multi-task inverse RL pools data across agents, factorizing policy logits with shared bases so rewards transfer to unvisited states.
xXJTi2nkrq.problem: Reward transfer to modified environments needs strict state coverage per task, and per-task planning scales poorly with the number of tasks.
xXJTi2nkrq.method: It pools data from multiple agents with different rewards in the same environment under a low-rank assumption, so planning cost scales with rank rather than the number of tasks. It provides finite-sample guarantees on reward recovery and on policy learning in new environments.
xXJTi2nkrq.key_idea: Assume task policy logits share a rank-k basis, so rewards are recovered at states only other tasks visited and planning scales with rank, not task count.
xXJTi2nkrq.evidence: Finite-sample theory on reward recovery and policy learning in new environments, plus experiments with limited coverage, targeted-deletion controls, and comparison against per-task baselines (e.g., GenPQR per reviews).
xXJTi2nkrq.claimed_gains: Lower target-environment regret than baselines and a computational advantage over per-task methods that widens as tasks grow; no numbers stated.
xXJTi2nkrq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared low-rank logit-basis idea is well motivated and the paper has clear assumptions and a solid coverage-to-transfer theory backed by targeted experiments.
xXJTi2nkrq.main_concern: The theory covers the exact plug-in reward while experiments use the cheaper k-step approximation, and strong normalization assumptions plus the lack of a shared-representation baseline without the rank limit weaken the support.

gJFBMqK6U2.one_liner: Replaces the actor's critic signal with a worst-plausible-regret objective, relaxed into DR3O and estimated from counterfactual action samples.
gJFBMqK6U2.problem: In actor-critic RL the critic is only an imperfect proxy for environmental return, so the actor faces a robustness problem even without environment shift.
gJFBMqK6U2.method: It defines worst plausible regret as the gap between the current policy and the best action under the same plausible critic, replaces hard hindsight search with a soft comparison to get DR3O, and applies it to twin critics to decide which Q the actor sees. A data-dependent ellipsoidal bonus gives further gains.
gJFBMqK6U2.key_idea: Minimize worst-case regret over plausible critics using a soft, sampling-based relaxation, which for twin critics reduces to a state-dependent choice between the two Q-values.
gJFBMqK6U2.evidence: Experiments on MuJoCo, MetaWorld, and the DeepMind Control Suite with matched training backbones, plus theory bounding the relaxed objective between canonical soft regret and hard worst-case regret (per reviews).
gJFBMqK6U2.claimed_gains: Changing the actor-facing signal improves matched training backbones across MuJoCo, MetaWorld, and the DeepMind Control Suite without additional effort; no numbers stated.
gJFBMqK6U2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing critic uncertainty as regret minimization is well motivated, with a principled derivation and a simple critic-selection rule applicable to multi-critic algorithms.
gJFBMqK6U2.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate regret-guided critic selection from simply changing the actor-facing signal (e.g., no mean-Q or equal-critic baseline), and the paper is dense and hard to follow.

MqT1XHOXTv.one_liner: Analyzes whether early layers of encoder-free multimodal LLMs act as implicit audio and visual encoders, finding largely context-invariant representations.
MqT1XHOXTv.problem: Encoder-free multimodal LLMs feed raw samples, pixels, or spectral features to the language model, and it is unknown whether their early layers learn encoder-like functions.
MqT1XHOXTv.method: Empirical analysis of Gemma-4 12B and Inkling-Small using context-invariance tests, independent versus joint encoding in early layers on multimodal reasoning tasks, and layer-wise probing compared with popular encoder models.
MqT1XHOXTv.key_idea: Test whether early-layer representations stay invariant to cross-modal context and whether independent early encoding matches joint encoding, then probe layers against dedicated encoders.
MqT1XHOXTv.evidence: Analyses on Gemma-4 12B and Inkling-Small, including LibriSpeech context-invariance, MIEB image classification and clustering for vision, and activation-patching experiments (per reviews).
MqT1XHOXTv.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; reports that independently encoding modalities in early layers matches the accuracy of jointly encoding them from the first layer.
MqT1XHOXTv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is timely and the experiments are well designed, with the audio-side invariance finding interesting.
MqT1XHOXTv.main_concern: Evidence is much weaker for vision than for audio, covers few benchmarks, and the paper does not define what properties an encoder should have.

pVh91XsXd3.one_liner: Adds a teacher-minus-student mean-latent direction during early sampling steps to transfer capabilities to flow-matching image models without training.
pVh91XsXd3.problem: Open flow-matching image models fail specific checkable capabilities (e.g., exact three-box diagrams) that stronger models handle, and closing the gap should not need training or teacher calls at inference.
pVh91XsXd3.method: DFS encodes about twenty teacher images with the student's VAE, takes the difference between the mean teacher latent and the mean student latent as a unit steering vector, and adds it to the latent during the first sampling steps only.
pVh91XsXd3.key_idea: The mean teacher-minus-student latent difference, computed once offline from clean latents, equals the guidance a second model would add at the first step.
pVh91XsXd3.evidence: Fresh-seed experiments on a constructed benchmark of capability failures (counting, diagrams, document layout), a human-validated judge, diversity measurements, and a finite-sample analysis of fitted steering directions.
pVh91XsXd3.claimed_gains: The abstract reports that in the first steps 99% of a fitted direction is noise; a review reports a 56.8% pass rate on the structural subset versus 45.8% for a comparison truncated in the batch.
pVh91XsXd3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DFS is a simple training-free intervention that improves the student on structural requirements without extra sampling cost, with diversity measured.
pVh91XsXd3.main_concern: Each direction is computed per prompt, so transfer to new prompts is not shown, and the cost versus simply using the teacher is not established.

CRHLdRAVgK.one_liner: Trains LLMs to respond safely under partially applied harmful weight perturbations, resisting later harmful fine-tuning.
CRHLdRAVgK.problem: Harmful fine-tuning erodes safety alignment, and existing alignment-stage defenses overlook how harmful weight changes accumulate collectively.
CRHLdRAVgK.method: JWP estimates a harmful perturbation from the current model, masks different parts of it, and trains the model to respond safely in the resulting perturbed states, exposing it to different combinations of harmful perturbation parts.
CRHLdRAVgK.key_idea: Alignment-stage training on states with different masked subsets of a harmful weight perturbation, to reduce sensitivity to the joint accumulation of harmful updates.
CRHLdRAVgK.evidence: Experiments across downstream tasks and model families against defenses such as SFT, Vaccine, RepNoise, and Booster (per reviews), with ablation and sensitivity studies.
CRHLdRAVgK.claimed_gains: Stronger resistance to harmful fine-tuning than prior defenses while largely preserving task performance; no numbers stated.
CRHLdRAVgK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the collective-failure observation motivates a simple method that markedly reduces harmfulness while preserving downstream performance, with clear writing.
CRHLdRAVgK.main_concern: The joint-amplification finding rests on a behavioral harmful score and may simply reflect a larger total perturbation, and the baseline set omits stronger defenses (TAR, Antibody, AsFT).

Me43SH7Yd6.one_liner: Couples model replicas through structured, local M-cover interactions rather than uniform coupling to improve generalization of replicated learning.
Me43SH7Yd6.problem: It is unclear whether the internal structure of the temporary replica lift in replicated learning can be tuned so that replica fluctuations induce task-relevant corrections.
Me43SH7Yd6.method: A local M-cover replicates and rewires a model's factor graph so replica fluctuations interact through structured coupling. The paper derives replica-difference dynamics near synchronization and a generalization-improvement condition, and analyzes a random-feature model with two trainable linear layers.
Me43SH7Yd6.key_idea: Tune the interaction geometry among replicas so replica-difference modes displace the predictor in alignment with the source-posterior correction.
Me43SH7Yd6.evidence: Theory for general models and a tractable random-feature model, plus benchmarks across tasks, architectures (MLPs, ResNets, Transformers, PINNs), optimizers, and overparameterization regimes.
Me43SH7Yd6.claimed_gains: Structured M-covers outperform established replicated-learning methods across tasks, architectures, learning dynamics, and overparameterization regimes; no numbers stated.
Me43SH7Yd6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating replica-interaction geometry as a design choice is interesting, with local theory and random-feature studies giving interpretable checks and the method working across optimizers and architectures.
Me43SH7Yd6.main_concern: The theory only partly matches the implemented coupling and the stochastic benchmarks, and missing related work and baselines beyond SAM leave the evidence for broad gains incomplete.

YsNbLWIKrd.one_liner: Automated pipeline that builds plot-digitization benchmarks by mapping real bioRxiv figures to author-released source data; yields PlotGround-1k.
YsNbLWIKrd.problem: It is unclear how accurately models recover plotted values from real scientific figures, since existing benchmarks use synthetic charts or limited chart types.
YsNbLWIKrd.method: PlotGround maps figures to source tables, identifies reconstructable panels, and generates quantitative questions with source-grounded reference values. PlotGround-1k holds 1,119 human-verified questions from 1,066 bioRxiv preprints.
YsNbLWIKrd.key_idea: Take reference answers from author-released source tables paired with the figures, so numerical precision can be scored at tight relative-error tolerances.
YsNbLWIKrd.evidence: Sixteen multimodal models on 1,119 human-verified questions at ±5% and ±2% tolerance, plus a figure-versus-source-table comparison with a coding agent.
YsNbLWIKrd.claimed_gains: The best model reaches 87.5% accuracy at a ±5% relative-error tolerance, tightening to ±2% lowers every model's accuracy by 11-24 percentage points, and source tables instead of figures raise a coding agent's accuracy from 90.0% to 97.4% while cutting cost by 72%.
YsNbLWIKrd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark has traceable, human-verified numerical references from real figures and source data at substantial scale, with useful findings about precision and source tables.
YsNbLWIKrd.main_concern: The practical need for precise value reading is questioned, some findings are expected, and the strict-tolerance results need calibration against the human audit and input resolution.

r2RWJGIEOD.one_liner: Regularizes diffusion transformers with InfoNCE whose negative dispersion is anchored to clean-sample representation distances to suppress a noise shortcut.
r2RWJGIEOD.problem: Naive InfoNCE regularization gives only marginal gains for diffusion transformers because near-orthogonal noise components let the loss enlarge negative-pair distances while weakening positive-pair alignment.
r2RWJGIEOD.method: CRAN (Clean Representation-ANchored Contrastive) regularization anchors contrastive dispersion with clean-sample representation distances, transferring clean relational semantic structure to noisy diffusion representations.
r2RWJGIEOD.key_idea: Anchor the contrastive dispersion target to distances between clean-sample representations so noisy-input features cannot enlarge negative distances through noise components.
r2RWJGIEOD.evidence: ImageNet experiments across model scales and training budgets against internal feature-alignment, dispersive regularization, and external DINO-guided REPA baselines, with ablations.
r2RWJGIEOD.claimed_gains: Consistently improves diffusion transformer training across model scales and budgets, outperforming internal feature-alignment and dispersive baselines and matching DINO-guided REPA; no numbers in the visible abstract.
r2RWJGIEOD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the noise-shortcut explanation of why InfoNCE fails in diffusion transformers is concrete and testable, supported by diagnostics and ablations, and that the fix is minimal and effective.
r2RWJGIEOD.main_concern: Evidence does not rule out a timestep shortcut or show the clean-representation anchor matters beyond limiting negative-pair separation (a fixed distance threshold gets much of the gain), and experiments are ImageNet-only.

rZ7eO7DZmc.one_liner: Distills an optimized agent harness into model weights via a harnessing agent that corrects student responses before execution.
rZ7eO7DZmc.problem: Harness gains depend on retaining the specialized harness at deployment, and guidance from an optimized harness cannot directly supervise a target harness with a different action space and information.
rZ7eO7DZmc.method: A harnessing agent, guided by the optimized harness, corrects student responses before execution in the target harness's action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment.
rZ7eO7DZmc.key_idea: Convert optimized-harness guidance into target-harness-valid demonstrations by minimally correcting the student's own responses, then fine-tune on those trajectories.
rZ7eO7DZmc.evidence: Experiments across knowledge work, tool use, and science domains (including SpreadsheetBench, AppWorld, and USPTO per reviews) with direct-distillation baselines and ablations.
rZ7eO7DZmc.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract, which is truncated; a review says the claim is that distillation surpasses the optimized harness on SpreadsheetBench and AppWorld.
rZ7eO7DZmc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation of harness distillation is precise, the action-space and information mismatch obstacles are clearly identified, and the reported gains are notable.
rZ7eO7DZmc.main_concern: The source of gains is not isolated: baselines lack the same guidance or action-space alignment, training data are success-filtered and partly written by a frontier model, and cost and per-domain training limit generality.

NzSg5915EZ.one_liner: Measures when open LLMs can stand in for closed ones, using log-odds and leave-one-out attributions from API-accessible outputs.
NzSg5915EZ.problem: Mechanistic interpretability needs model internals, but most deployed models expose only output log-probabilities, so it is unclear when findings on open models transfer to closed ones.
NzSg5915EZ.method: They define surrogate fidelity at the prediction, attribution, and mechanistic levels, using log-odds as an API-compatible readout of representation space and leave-one-out attributions, and compare eleven models from four families.
NzSg5915EZ.key_idea: Log-odds differences between inputs give an API-compatible readout of representation differences, so prediction and attribution agreement across models can be compared without internals.
NzSg5915EZ.evidence: Eleven models in four families (Llama, Qwen, GPT, Gemini; 0.5B-70B) on four classification benchmarks, plus system-prompt interventions (per reviews).
NzSg5915EZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad across eleven models and that the API-compatible log-odds approach gives practitioners a practical check on surrogate use.
NzSg5915EZ.main_concern: The claims about mechanisms overreach what input saliency and coarse internal signals measure, and attention fidelity is treated as equivalent to representational fidelity.

GdKO2AKqcX.one_liner: Composable, GPU-batched framework and benchmark for meta-black-box optimization with swappable components and over 11,000 problem instances.
GdKO2AKqcX.problem: Method-specific MetaBBO implementations couple components, which makes controlled comparisons hard, and repeated runs across problems and seeds are computationally costly.
GdKO2AKqcX.method: Task-specific interfaces let researchers assemble components for algorithm selection, configuration, solution manipulation, and generation under shared conditions, with train, validation, and test manifests and EvoX-based GPU batching of optimization runs.
GdKO2AKqcX.key_idea: Define task-specific component interfaces so parts can be swapped under shared manifests, and batch optimization runs on GPUs through EvoX.
GdKO2AKqcX.evidence: Runtime studies of LDE and GLHF, component studies on configuration and learned control, and baseline recipes across numerical, combinatorial, and real-world suites.
GdKO2AKqcX.claimed_gains: GPU execution accelerates LDE training and testing by up to 107.6x and 174.9x, respectively, compared with CPU execution.
GdKO2AKqcX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework makes controlled component substitution practical and addresses a real methodological gap in attributing MetaBBO gains.
GdKO2AKqcX.main_concern: The scope of GPU acceleration is unclear since runtime is studied only for LDE and GLHF, and reimplemented baselines are not validated against the original implementations.

uawBXVdSFq.one_liner: Benchmark of 1.04 million cases for ranking earlier papers a researcher will newly cite, from their publication history alone.
uawBXVdSFq.problem: It is unclear how much of the literature shaping a researcher's next paper, including works they had not cited before, can be anticipated from their past publications.
uawBXVdSFq.method: MUSES builds cases from S2ORC (140,278 in the test split) where a system ranks 2.33 million earlier candidates given a researcher's pre-cutoff papers, scored mainly on previously uncited works. It adds 1,633 author-collected cases from asking authors what shaped their papers, and a classifier grounded in human coding for citation contexts of building on a work.
uawBXVdSFq.key_idea: Evaluation is prospective with a time cutoff and scores works the researcher had not cited before, complemented by direct author attestation of influence.
uawBXVdSFq.evidence: Lexical, dense, citation-graph retrievers and supervised models are compared on the benchmark, with popularity as a baseline and an author-attested subset.
uawBXVdSFq.claimed_gains: History-based retrievers place a newly cited work in their top 100 for 30-37% of cases, against 5% for popularity.
uawBXVdSFq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is well formulated with a time cutoff and exclusion of previously cited work, and that the author-attestation study adds human-grounded value to a large benchmark.
uawBXVdSFq.main_concern: Previously uncited is only a proxy for novel influence, the author-attested set is selective and reproduces the citation construct, and baselines are too narrow to support the claim that the limit is information more than representation.

VpmBLzRi9r.one_liner: Python library that builds navigation scenarios from declarative YAML files, with agent skills for LLM-written scenario configs.
VpmBLzRi9r.problem: Constructing diverse, reproducible navigation scenarios usually needs simulator-specific code, complex GUIs, manual configuration, or heavy compute, which makes scenarios hard to reuse across experiments.
VpmBLzRi9r.method: IR-SIM represents objects, behaviors, sensors, maps, and environment parameters as human-readable YAML, supports robot models and sensors, and keeps interfaces to high-fidelity simulators. Provided agent skills let LLM agents compose and modify scenario files.
VpmBLzRi9r.key_idea: Describe whole navigation scenarios as composable declarative YAML configs so humans and LLM agents edit files instead of simulator code.
VpmBLzRi9r.evidence: Execution benchmarks across robot counts, LiDAR and sensor-free settings, and CPU and batched GPU execution against other simulators, plus RL training time and an LLM scenario-authoring study.
VpmBLzRi9r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree IR-SIM is a practical, well-developed tool that eases repeated navigation experiments, with strong efficiency results especially in large multi-robot scenarios.
VpmBLzRi9r.main_concern: Speedups are weakly attributed: the RL speedup comes mostly from batching (matched TorchRL control 0.74 h versus 0.76 h), agent skills were tuned on the evaluated briefs, and cross-simulator timing workloads are not matched.

SZEO5MrQN5.one_liner: Simulates research agents writing and revising papers against LLM reviewers to measure fairness gaps between LLM- and human-authored papers.
SZEO5MrQN5.problem: Joint use of LLMs in research generation and peer review may harm scholarly fairness, and the risks of LLM reviewers are poorly understood.
SZEO5MrQN5.method: A simulation pairs a research agent that generates and revises papers with a review agent that evaluates them, followed by human annotations and analyses of linguistic profiles, LLM polishing, and limitation-oriented topics.
SZEO5MrQN5.key_idea: Run a closed generate-review-revise loop with LLM authors and reviewers and compare scores for LLM-authored and matched human-authored papers.
SZEO5MrQN5.evidence: Simulations with three reviewer models and human annotations on the 15 largest LLM-favoring gaps, plus content-preserving polishing experiments.
SZEO5MrQN5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is timely and the setup, which studies generation, review, and a revise-and-resubmit loop together, shows LLM reviewers favoring LLM-authored papers across several reviewer models.
SZEO5MrQN5.main_concern: Topic matching does not ensure comparable scientific quality because LLM-generated papers use different ideas and predicted results, and the revision gains lack an unchanged-paper control.

QCbrLkzuUX.one_liner: Flow matching that learns tangential transport with prescribed normal contraction toward the data manifold, guaranteed by contraction theory.
QCbrLkzuUX.problem: Geometric flow matching assumes a prior already on the data manifold, and low regression error alone does not ensure generated samples stay on the true manifold.
QCbrLkzuUX.method: MSFM starts from an arbitrary ambient prior and learns tangential transport with prescribed normal contraction, using analytical projectors for known manifolds or PCA-based local affine proxies for unknown ones, with compatible probability paths and a separated training loss.
QCbrLkzuUX.key_idea: Prescribe normal contraction toward the manifold (or a PCA affine proxy) and learn only tangential velocity, giving convergence to it within a chosen time window.
QCbrLkzuUX.evidence: Contraction-theory guarantees (explicit decay rates for known manifolds) and experiments including robotic tasks with 50 rollouts per task; the abstract is cut off before the results.
QCbrLkzuUX.claimed_gains: Guaranteed convergence to the data manifold within a desired time window (for example one second); empirical gains are not quantified in the visible abstract.
QCbrLkzuUX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the link between the algorithm and the geometric guarantees clear, with explicit decay rates for known manifolds.
QCbrLkzuUX.main_concern: The unknown-manifold theory stops at PCA proxies without bounding their distance to the true manifold, and empirical evidence is limited (for example no variation across training runs in robotic experiments).

oIaznhm0uU.one_liner: Shares NVFP4 4-bit codes across loops in looped Transformers while learning one block-scale table per loop.
oIaznhm0uU.problem: Looped Transformers must either tie weights fully (every loop identical) or pay linear storage for independent weights, while partial untying and per-loop LoRA limit between-loop changes.
oIaznhm0uU.method: LatticeLoop shares the 4-bit codes of block-scaled formats such as NVFP4 across loops and learns one table of block scales per loop, so each loop is a standard block-scaled matmul and each extra loop costs 0.5 bits per core weight.
oIaznhm0uU.key_idea: Split each weight into shared 4-bit block codes and per-loop 8-bit block scales, so loop-specific magnitudes give distinct weights at one ninth the cost of an independent copy.
oIaznhm0uU.evidence: Language model pretraining at matched storage up to 12 loops and 80B training tokens, with decode speed measurements; reviewers note a single 360M-parameter model on one corpus with a single seed.
oIaznhm0uU.claimed_gains: Closes 92.5% of the loss gap between full tying and independent weights at matched storage, versus less than a third for partial untying and per-loop LoRA, with decoding speed close to full tying.
oIaznhm0uU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hardware-native design is simple, each loop runs as a standard block-scaled matmul, and at matched storage it clearly outperforms LoRA and partial untying.
oIaznhm0uU.main_concern: Evidence is thin: one 360M model on one corpus with a single seed and no confidence intervals, uneven baseline sweeps, and questions about novelty relative to scale-based adaptation work.

R8a5AIvqQ1.one_liner: Continual Lasso that carries the historical squared-loss score rather than an l1-penalized estimate, recovering the full-history Lasso exactly.
R8a5AIvqQ1.problem: Reusing an l1-penalized estimate as the center of a historical quadratic loss propagates earlier penalty subgradients and can erase true signals even as more data arrive.
R8a5AIvqQ1.method: SP-CL separates sparse estimation from state transmission by preserving the historical squared-loss score; for related tasks it adds a regularized current-task correction that leaves the transmitted state unchanged, with Overall, BWT, and FWT decompositions.
R8a5AIvqQ1.key_idea: Transmit the squared-loss score (sufficient statistics) instead of a shrunken penalized estimate, so the cumulative estimator equals the full-history Lasso minimizer.
R8a5AIvqQ1.evidence: Theorems (exact equivalence to pooled Lasso under squared loss, sparse rates for coinciding and related task coefficients) validated in simulation.
R8a5AIvqQ1.claimed_gains: Under squared loss the cumulative estimator exactly recovers a full-history Lasso minimizer, inherits the full-history sparse rate when task coefficients coincide, and attains the offline source-assisted rate form under stated conditions; no numbers stated.
R8a5AIvqQ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the recursive shrinkage bias clearly explained and the exact equivalence to pooled Lasso, with Overall/BWT/FWT decompositions, a clear and rigorous contribution.
R8a5AIvqQ1.main_concern: Linear Lasso on fixed features is weakly connected to modern continual learning, novelty relative to online Lasso is unacknowledged, and replay baselines and storage of the p x p state are not addressed.

x3sQsa48sB.one_liner: Shows Wasserstein DRO linear regression equals a robust quadratic adversarial regression, yielding error bounds, pivotality, and solution equivalences.
x3sQsa48sB.problem: Properties known for two special cases of Wasserstein DRO regression, square-root Lasso and adversarial linear regression, had not been established for the general method.
x3sQsa48sB.method: They study Wasserstein DRO linear regression, which includes square-root Lasso and adversarial linear regression as special cases, and recast it as a quadratic form mimicking adversarial regression. From this they prove error bounds, a pivotal property, and solution equivalences for small and large ambiguity sets, and show the method can be solved efficiently.
x3sQsa48sB.key_idea: Recast Wasserstein DRO regression as a robust quadratic form that mimics adversarial linear regression with per-sample budgets, so adversarial-training proofs carry over.
x3sQsa48sB.evidence: Proofs of deterministic non-asymptotic in-sample error bounds, the pivotal property, and solution equivalences, plus numerical simulations.
x3sQsa48sB.claimed_gains: not stated (theory paper; in-sample error bounds of O(n^-1/2) in general and O(n^-1) under design matrix and sparsity conditions)
x3sQsa48sB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the connection between Wasserstein DRO and adversarial regression (Theorem 1) is clean and insightful, unifying square-root Lasso and adversarial regression.
x3sQsa48sB.main_concern: The technical contribution is incremental over prior proofs, and the benefit of intermediate p values is unclear since rates and experiments barely depend on p.

2HJwp8hMGE.one_liner: Reuses the training policy's accumulated token-level shift as mean-preserving credit allocation inside GRPO, with no separate teacher.
2HJwp8hMGE.problem: GRPO assigns one shared advantage to all tokens in a response, leaving accumulated token-level policy changes unused as explicit guidance.
2HJwp8hMGE.method: Delta-GRPO uses the training policy's accumulated shift to guide token-level credit allocation within outcome-driven GRPO. It needs no external teacher and preserves the mean and sign of the response-level advantages.
2HJwp8hMGE.key_idea: Redistribute each response's GRPO advantage across tokens according to the policy's accumulated probability shift, keeping the mean fixed.
2HJwp8hMGE.evidence: Eight mathematics benchmarks with Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-32B, compared with GRPO and SC-GRPO, with component ablations and three training seeds for the GRPO comparison.
2HJwp8hMGE.claimed_gains: Delta-GRPO improves macro accuracy over GRPO by 13.59, 12.04, and 11.91 percentage points with Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-32B, and exceeds SC-GRPO by 8.90 and 7.89 points at 4B and 8B.
2HJwp8hMGE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, teacher-free credit redistribution with large and consistent gains across eight math benchmarks, supported by component ablations.
2HJwp8hMGE.main_concern: It is not shown that historical policy shifts carry informative token credit (no shuffled or random mean-preserving controls), they may reinforce earlier errors, and per-step cost is 55.6% higher.

eElGjHpk6Y.one_liner: MPR-Flow warm-starts plug-and-play flow solvers from earlier reconstructions and constrains re-noising to preserve well-measured regions.
eElGjHpk6Y.problem: Imaging often combines measurements acquired sequentially, but solving each stage from scratch wastes computation when acquisitions should be minimized.
eElGjHpk6Y.method: MPR-Flow, a plug-and-play flow solver, exploits continuity at two scales: across acquisition stages, previous reconstructions serve as a prior, and across solver iterations, the re-noising step is constrained so well-measured regions are preserved. It needs no retraining or prior changes.
eElGjHpk6Y.key_idea: Reuse the previous stage's reconstruction as a warm start and constrain re-noising by measurement geometry so well-measured regions are preserved.
eElGjHpk6Y.evidence: Simulated and real datasets against flow-based inverse solvers; reviews cite inpainting and MRI experiments, component ablations (ADWS and RNC), and runtime comparisons.
eElGjHpk6Y.claimed_gains: Outperforms flow-based inverse solvers in reconstruction quality and acquisition time with no numbers in the abstract; a review cites 30% inpainting improving from 26.1 to 32.0 dB.
eElGjHpk6Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sequential-acquisition setting is practical, the method plugs into a pretrained flow model without retraining, and it beats cold-start baselines.
eElGjHpk6Y.main_concern: The contribution beyond simple warm-start continuation is not isolated: most of the gain comes from the warm-start schedule, there is no tuned fixed-start or warm-started FLOWER comparison, and why the re-noising coupling works is unexplained.

B9LfBribE6.one_liner: ART trains MAPPO actors to regress Koopman-autoencoder coordinates of joint team dynamics as an auxiliary, training-only target.
B9LfBribE6.problem: Actor-critic MARL shapes actor representations with only scalar rewards, leaving joint system dynamics unexploited, which limits performance under partial observability.
B9LfBribE6.method: A centralized bilinear Koopman autoencoder on joint transitions provides linearly evolving latent coordinates, and a linear auxiliary head on each actor's features regresses them during training only, leaving actor inputs, architecture, and execution unchanged.
B9LfBribE6.key_idea: Supervise decentralized actor features with linearly evolving Koopman coordinates of the joint dynamics through a linear auxiliary head used only during training.
B9LfBribE6.evidence: Multi-Agent MuJoCo experiments against MAPPO, with ablations of prediction losses and a fixed linear projection of the global state per reviews.
B9LfBribE6.claimed_gains: Up to a 76% performance gain on Ant under full observation and more than doubles the final return on Ant 2x4 under partial observation.
B9LfBribE6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is clean and clearly presented, adds no execution-time cost, and uses global dynamical information sensibly to improve decentralized actors.
B9LfBribE6.main_concern: Baselines are thin (only MAPPO), a fixed linear projection of the global state already gives much of the gain so the Koopman component's benefit is unclear, and close prior work (LDD, PTLD, IWoL) undercuts the novelty claim.

LM0hPQm1Eo.one_liner: PAE assigns feedback influence by source-observation overlap so repeated interpretations of the same observations are not counted as extra evidence.
LM0hPQm1Eo.problem: In self-improving agents, repeated interpretations of the same observations are counted as additional evidence when deciding which updates to keep.
LM0hPQm1Eo.method: Provenance-Adjusted Evidence is a fixed-budget acceptance rule that traces feedback to originating observations, removes replayed records, and pools judgments that share sources. It reduces to the mean paired task gain with complete direct scores and adjusts overlapping joint assessments when per-task scores are incomplete.
LM0hPQm1Eo.key_idea: Weight each update's evidence by source overlap rather than feedback volume, pooling judgments that share originating observations.
LM0hPQm1Eo.evidence: Optimizers GEPA, TextGrad, and MIPROv2-No-Demos with Qwen3-8B on GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP+, and IFBench under matched budget ceilings with five-run means, plus a controlled fixed-candidate study.
LM0hPQm1Eo.claimed_gains: Improves five-run mean accuracy and code pass@1 by 0.72-1.33 percentage points on GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP+, and IFBench under matched budget ceilings.
LM0hPQm1Eo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it identifies a real evidence-reuse problem (changing only feedback layout flips acceptance for 15.0% of candidate pairs in one review) and uses a careful controlled design with consistent small gains.
LM0hPQm1Eo.main_concern: The main end-to-end experiments use complete task scores where PAE reduces exactly to root averaging, so they do not test the provenance-overlap adjustment that is the paper's distinctive component.

HI5w6J11EC.one_liner: GRPO on TikZ code with compile and quality rewards, updating only tokens picked by reference differences and entropy.
HI5w6J11EC.problem: TikZ models trained on paired descriptions and reference code lack supervision of rendered diagram quality and weight all token positions equally during optimization.
HI5w6J11EC.method: Candidates are scored by compilation and code-quality signals plus three assessment models for logic, layout, and style. DE-GRPO then selects update positions using reference differences and generation uncertainty.
HI5w6J11EC.key_idea: DE-GRPO restricts policy updates to token positions flagged by combining differences from the reference code with generation entropy.
HI5w6J11EC.evidence: Multiple TikZ benchmarks (SKETIKZ named in reviews) against general-purpose and task-specific baselines, a token-selection ablation, and a human evaluation.
HI5w6J11EC.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports consistent gains in code-level performance and visual fidelity without numbers)
HI5w6J11EC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reward design covers distinct failure modes and that results beat general-purpose and task-specific baselines on several benchmarks, with extensive ablations.
HI5w6J11EC.main_concern: The token-selection rule is weakly justified and incremental over existing high-entropy token methods, and the metrics largely measure similarity to the reference.

6WbmZ3Qz0b.one_liner: Fine-tunes a VLM on rendered images of combinatorial optimization instances with SFT, RL, and inference-time visual augmentation.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.problem: LLM-based combinatorial optimization solvers use text encodings, which can lose spatial information and limit spatial reasoning for problems naturally presented visually.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.method: Instances are encoded into images with visual attributes, and self-evolutionary visual prompt optimization searches for effective designs. Training is SFT from domain-specific solvers followed by RL to cut constraint violations, and inference-time structure-preserving transformations generate diverse candidate solutions.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.key_idea: Render CO instances as images with evolved visual encodings, train a VLM to output solutions directly, and use structure-preserving image transformations for diverse candidates.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.evidence: Six NP-hard CO problems (routing, graph optimization, scheduling per reviews) with a Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct base per reviews, compared with GPT-6-Astra and Gemini-2.5-Pro and problem-specific methods, with ablations and OOD tests.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.claimed_gains: Achieves 100% feasibility with optimality gaps from 1.78% to 10.93%, and improves average feasibility over GPT-6-Astra and Gemini-2.5-Pro by 26.5% and 44.3%, respectively.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is broad across six problems and backbones, with ablations isolating the components and no architecture changes needed per problem.
6WbmZ3Qz0b.main_concern: It is not established why CO should be solved visually, since instances are rendered from numeric data with handcrafted features, and infeasible-solution gaps are computed inconsistently.

d5vZ7xmQef.one_liner: Separates belief, value, and action-selection failures of LM agents in text grid worlds using probes, inverse RL, and interventions.
d5vZ7xmQef.problem: LM agents can fail for different reasons (missing beliefs, wrong values, poor action selection) that require different explanations and interventions.
d5vZ7xmQef.method: They estimate task-relevant beliefs with report-based and representation-based probes and action values with inverse reinforcement learning, then track action preferences through reasoning. They also test transplanted reasoning prefixes and reasoning-window activation edits.
d5vZ7xmQef.key_idea: Compare decoded state beliefs and IRL-inferred values with chosen actions across reasoning steps to measure a belief-action gap.
d5vZ7xmQef.evidence: Text-rendered grid worlds with a single model (gpt-oss 20B per reviews), using probes, inverse RL, prefix transplant, and activation-edit interventions.
d5vZ7xmQef.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative findings: state and value information is represented more reliably than it is reflected in behaviour)
