rJlixblIiP.method: GestaltCLIP is a vision-language framework that integrates concept-, patient-, and disease-level phenotype signals via ontology-aware Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) learning, patient phenotype-set modeling, paired image-phenotype grounding, and disease-mediated weak supervision. At inference time, the trained vision encoder processes images alone without requiring phenotype inputs.
rJlixblIiP.key_idea: Aligns facial representations across multiple supervision granularities by combining ontology-aware HPO concept learning, patient phenotype-set modeling, and disease-mediated weak alignment.
rJlixblIiP.evidence: Evaluated on the GestaltMatcher Database across four disease recognition metrics, atomic image-to-HPO retrieval, unseen disease generalization, and component ablations.
rJlixblIiP.claimed_gains: On the GestaltMatcher Database, GestaltCLIP yields an average relative improvement of 15.58% across four disease recognition metrics and a 7.73-fold increase in mAP for atomic image-to-HPO retrieval.
rJlixblIiP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a practically important clinical problem by coherently integrating sparse image-level annotations with multi-granularity ontology, patient, and disease-level phenotype supervision.
rJlixblIiP.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not match supervision and data resources, making it difficult to separate gains from the three-stage training design versus additional weakly annotated images and external clinical priors.

Q42IhAZHwg.one_liner: Suppresses model-exposed harmful output trajectories without conditioning on triggering prompts, then restores utility on a retain set.
Q42IhAZHwg.problem: Question-answer safety alignment and unlearning remain vulnerable to jailbreak reformulations because finite training sets cannot exhaustively cover the space of harmful prompts.
Q42IhAZHwg.method: Answer-Centric Unlearning (ACU) probes the target LLM to expose latent harmful output trajectories, iteratively applies unlearning updates directly to those harmful answers without conditioning on input questions, and trains on a benign retain set to recover general utility.
Q42IhAZHwg.key_idea: Elicit latent harmful responses from the LLM, apply question-free unlearning updates directly on those answer trajectories, and fine-tune on a benign retain set.
Q42IhAZHwg.evidence: Evaluated across four 7–8B LLM backbones and one 32B model against eight unseen jailbreak types—including adaptive PAIR/GCG and weight-update attacks per reviews—with controlled question-free versus question-dependent ablations.
Q42IhAZHwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that controlled comparisons holding harmful responses fixed provide clear evidence that question-free answer suppression generalizes better across unseen jailbreak phrasings than question-conditioned suppression.
Q42IhAZHwg.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty relative to prior response-only defenses like Circuit Breakers, measurable utility drops, continued dependence on a finite probe pool for answer discovery, and non-trivial attack success under multi-attempt adaptive and weight-update attacks.

hJ9kQATIq3.one_liner: Compresses KV caches without calibration using three randomized Walsh-Hadamard rounds, E8 lattice rounding, and rANS coding.
hJ9kQATIq3.problem: KV-cache quantizers either rely on fixed-rate scalar codes far from the rate-distortion frontier or require model-specific calibration data to fit entropy coders.
hJ9kQATIq3.method: HybridQuant applies three rounds of randomized fast Walsh-Hadamard transforms to Gaussianize key and value vectors, rounds them to the E8 lattice, and compresses symbols with a static Gaussian rANS table sized directly to a target bit budget. It pairs this with pre-RoPE key centering, one fp16 sink token, 4-bit channel scales, and a 64-token fp16 recent window inside 2.125 bits per element.
hJ9kQATIq3.key_idea: Gaussianize KV vectors via three randomized Walsh-Hadamard rounds so a single static E8-lattice rANS code achieves target bitrates without calibration.
hJ9kQATIq3.evidence: Supported by non-asymptotic Gaussianity bounds across Hadamard rounds, CPU rANS bitstream verification, and simulated KV-cache quantization benchmarks against KIVI, TurboQuant, and Rot-ECSQ.
hJ9kQATIq3.claimed_gains: Operates inside 2.125 bits per element while reducing worst-case spike Kolmogorov distance from Gaussian from 0.34 (one round) to 1.2314/d after three Hadamard rounds.
hJ9kQATIq3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the calibration-free Hadamard-plus-E8-rANS formulation is theoretically well grounded and features rigorous, bit-exact rate accounting including all side information.
hJ9kQATIq3.main_concern: No fused GPU rANS decoder is implemented, so quality evaluations rely on simulated quantization and no end-to-end GPU latency or memory-bandwidth gains are demonstrated.

Saq65mY19o.one_liner: Derives non-asymptotic multistep consistency-model error bounds decomposing initialization contraction and approximation bias across noise schedules.
Saq65mY19o.problem: Multistep sampling in consistency models exhibits strong sensitivity to noise schedules and can degrade quality as steps increase, lacking practical non-asymptotic theory.
Saq65mY19o.method: The authors analyze multistep consistency sampling as a composition of forward noising and approximate denoising maps, deriving error bounds that separate early-step initialization contraction from late-step approximation bias accumulation. They instantiate explicit contraction profiles under log-concavity assumptions and propose model-estimable stability diagnostics.
Saq65mY19o.key_idea: Decompose multistep consistency-model recursion error into noise-schedule-dependent initialization contraction and accumulated denoising bias under explicit operator stability conditions.
Saq65mY19o.evidence: Validated analytically on Gaussian, strongly log-concave, and semi-log-concave targets and empirically on two latent consistency models.
Saq65mY19o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly explains the trade-off between initialization contraction and approximation error accumulation in multistep consistency sampling.
Saq65mY19o.main_concern: Empirical latent-covariance measurements do not verify the global stability and log-concavity assumptions required by the bounds, while the recursion builds closely on prior work by Lyu et al.

9mjFkoriaV.one_liner: Defines context-specific Bregman divergences on frozen contrastive embeddings via probability distributions over semantic anchors.
9mjFkoriaV.problem: Fixed cosine similarity on pretrained contrastive embeddings cannot adapt to context-dependent notions of similarity such as object identity versus visual style or clinical relevance.
9mjFkoriaV.method: Connecting contrastive objectives to exponential families and information geometry, the authors map probability distributions over reference anchor embeddings to Bregman divergences on the frozen representation space. Specifying or adapting the anchor distribution induces task-specific Anchor Divergences for retrieval without retraining the encoder.
9mjFkoriaV.key_idea: Induce context-specific Bregman geometries on frozen contrastive embeddings by specifying probability distributions over semantic reference anchors via exponential-family duality.
9mjFkoriaV.evidence: Evaluated on object-versus-style coordinate retrieval, ImageNet/WordNet adaptation, and CheXpert clinical retrieval across parametric and non-parametric anchor models.
9mjFkoriaV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that inducing context-dependent retrieval metrics on frozen contrastive representations via anchor distributions is well motivated and effective on attribute and clinical retrieval.
9mjFkoriaV.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the specific Bregman divergence and Bayesian adaptation rules from simpler distance metrics or combinations computed on the same anchor distributions.

2nZ4XaISsp.one_liner: Trains audio-language models to localize emotion spans using attention-masked emotion losses and distance-weighted timestamp supervision.
2nZ4XaISsp.problem: Utterance-level audio emotion recognition assigns a single label per recording, failing to localize affective speech spans in multi-speaker or overlapping audio.
2nZ4XaISsp.method: The authors curate multi-span and overlapping emotional speech recordings paired with vocal tone descriptions and train EMO-TAG under Masked Temporal Affective Grounding (M-TAG). M-TAG applies attention masking during emotion-token prediction to block textual tone shortcuts and uses a distance-aware cross-entropy weight on timestamp tokens.
2nZ4XaISsp.key_idea: Mask text and tone context on emotion tokens while penalizing timestamp errors by temporal distance to ground emotions in audio.
2nZ4XaISsp.evidence: Evaluated with fine-tuned EMO-TAG on reconstructed multi-span datasets derived from benchmarks including IEMOCAP and MELD against audio-language baselines.
2nZ4XaISsp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reformulating speech emotion recognition as temporal span grounding with shortcut-preventing attention masks is a useful task extension.
2nZ4XaISsp.main_concern: Supervised EMO-TAG is primarily compared against zero-shot audio-language models rather than supervised baselines, while synthetic utterance concatenation and unvalidated AI tone descriptions limit realism.

MjE6ciFgCd.one_liner: Attribute-factorized object latents improve imagined policy learning and transfer to unseen attribute combinations.
MjE6ciFgCd.problem: Object-centric world models usually give each entity one unstructured embedding, limiting transfer to unseen attribute combinations.
MjE6ciFgCd.method: COMB learns explicitly factorized per-entity latents without attribute supervision for online model-based RL, then uses frozen invertible maps to vary attribute entanglement without changing information.
MjE6ciFgCd.key_idea: Represent each object with named attribute latents, then test policy dependence by invertibly entangling those coordinates without changing information.
MjE6ciFgCd.evidence: Eight 2D and 3D manipulation tasks and held-out position-colour combinations support returns, with frozen-representation invertible-map controls separating format from information.
MjE6ciFgCd.claimed_gains: Entangling attributes reduces return by 31-37% at a fixed budget and held-out return by up to 30% at matched in-distribution skill, while linear scrambling produces no resolvable loss.
MjE6ciFgCd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled entanglement-dosing and matched-skill analyses provide stronger evidence than end-to-end benchmarks alone.
MjE6ciFgCd.main_concern: Reviewers most often caution that end-to-end gains remain confounded by other architectural and planning differences and that visual environments are narrow.

I375E7ynDc.one_liner: Conditional outcome probabilities replace sampled-event counting to reduce variance and token generation in EHR prediction.
I375E7ynDc.problem: Monte Carlo simulation of EHR futures produces sparse risk estimates at extreme computational cost and with high sampling variance.
I375E7ynDc.method: SCOPE sums conditional outcome probabilities and REACH estimates anticipated conditional hazards from next-token distributions, with unbiasedness proofs and a Rao-Blackwellization guarantee for REACH.
I375E7ynDc.key_idea: Compute outcome risk from next-token conditional probabilities, with REACH Rao-Blackwellizing importance sampling to guarantee variance reduction.
I375E7ynDc.evidence: Proofs and 11 clinical outcomes across MIMIC-IV and the UChicago health system compare accuracy, calibration, variance, and token use against 100-sample Monte Carlo.
I375E7ynDc.claimed_gains: SCOPE and REACH match 100-sample Monte Carlo accuracy with median token reductions of 2.5× to 3.4× and reductions exceeding 80× for the rarest outcomes, with calibration preserved throughout.
I375E7ynDc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the estimators are intuitive, theoretically grounded, and empirically yield substantial computational savings across clinical outcomes.
I375E7ynDc.main_concern: Reviewers most often question practical significance and missing supervised outcome-prediction baselines, alongside doubts about methodological novelty.

KkmVgtMGlM.one_liner: Differentiable temporal-logic attention guidance steers frozen video generators without fine-tuning.
KkmVgtMGlM.problem: Existing video controls do not reliably enforce temporal and logical requirements such as ordering, negation, and co-occurrence.
KkmVgtMGlM.method: T-LESSA converts temporal-logic requirements into differentiable guidance over cross-attention, steering frozen text-to-video backbones at inference time.
KkmVgtMGlM.key_idea: Bias cross-attention using a differentiable finite-trace temporal-logic score that expresses ordering, negation, and co-occurrence.
KkmVgtMGlM.evidence: Four video backbones are evaluated for temporal completion and temporal-logic satisfaction, with reviews noting three judges, three seeds per prompt, and significance tests.
KkmVgtMGlM.claimed_gains: T-LESSA improves temporal completion by 14.3% and temporal-logic satisfaction by 21.8% over the unsteered baseline across four backbones, at 1.7% to 13.5% additional generation time.
KkmVgtMGlM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that differentiable logic-guided attention is useful and that experiments show consistent improvements across several backbones.
KkmVgtMGlM.main_concern: Reviewers most often question evaluation reliability because VLM judges lack human-agreement validation and text-to-temporal-logic translation is unmeasured.

mXDeixZEEw.one_liner: Same-grid controls and activation patching expose failures to combine correctly recovered visual facts.
mXDeixZEEw.problem: Final-answer accuracy cannot distinguish failures to read individual facts from failures to combine them into valid global decisions.
mXDeixZEEw.method: The study combines same-grid local queries, conditional global evaluation, text oracles, retrieval and constraint controls, hidden-state probes, and activation replacement on subset-selection and path-finding tasks.
mXDeixZEEw.key_idea: Condition global validity on correct local answers for the same input, then patch solution-related hidden states to localize integration failures.
mXDeixZEEw.evidence: Controlled subset-selection and path-finding tasks span model families, with local queries, text oracles, probes, and activation replacement across depth and token positions.
mXDeixZEEw.claimed_gains: Gemma-3-27B recovers all evaluated isolated item facts correctly but achieves only 19.75% global validity on eight-item visual instances.
mXDeixZEEw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that same-grid behavioral controls clearly expose a local-to-global gap and that probes and patching support the analysis.
mXDeixZEEw.main_concern: Reviewers most often question generality beyond highly structured synthetic conjunction tasks and the added insight over known compositional-reasoning failures.

LCT7iCqsXa.one_liner: Execution-trained software world models predict downstream breakage to rank changes and schedule migrations.
LCT7iCqsXa.problem: Coding agents can break downstream consumers that repository-local tests miss, while exhaustive integration testing after every action is impractical.
LCT7iCqsXa.method: SWM explores candidate changes from restored states, fine-tunes a language model on execution outcomes, and converts sampled predictions into consumer break probabilities for ranking, migration, and execution decisions.
LCT7iCqsXa.key_idea: Learn per-consumer break probabilities from consequences of candidate changes executed from restored system states.
LCT7iCqsXa.evidence: Held-out synthetic systems and real-library evaluations assess blast-set F1, change-ranking regret, migration return, and comparisons with static reachability.
LCT7iCqsXa.claimed_gains: On held-out synthetic systems, SWM improves blast-set F1 from 0.431 for static reachability to 0.571 ± 0.037, more than halves ranking regret, and improves migration return at all nine evaluation checkpoints.
LCT7iCqsXa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that downstream breakage is an important underexplored failure mode and that same-state execution and decision-value evaluation are useful.
LCT7iCqsXa.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that simple supervised or reachability baselines match or beat SWM, especially on real libraries.

qS8NmjrgrL.one_liner: Finite-horizon rotational bounds derive learning-rate schedules that approach linear decay on spherical objectives.
qS8NmjrgrL.problem: Learning-rate schedule effects depend on parameter norms and rotational motion, which standard finite-horizon analyses do not directly capture.
qS8NmjrgrL.method: A geodesically convex spherical analysis derives a last-iterate bound for arbitrary rotational schedules and its unique minimizer, then compares predictions with LLM pretraining under Adam, Muon, AdamH, and MuonH.
qS8NmjrgrL.key_idea: Optimize a last-iterate spherical convergence bound over rotational step allocations, separating schedule scale from temporal distribution.
qS8NmjrgrL.evidence: Spherical convergence theory is compared with LLM-pretraining schedule behavior across model scales using Adam, Muon, AdamH, and MuonH.
qS8NmjrgrL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the exact finite-horizon allocation result is clear and theoretically useful, with supporting Hyperball experiments.
qS8NmjrgrL.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the link between theory and experiments, citing violated hypotheses and limited comparisons with bound-optimal schedules.

8JRPrcw01V.one_liner: Geometry-calibrated local semantic fields measure representation organization across network depth and neighborhood scale.
8JRPrcw01V.problem: Decoding and global-similarity evaluations do not describe how local semantic organization jointly changes with depth and neighborhood scale.
8JRPrcw01V.method: SCF combines continuous-weighted local composition estimates, adaptive effective-support accounting, and geometry-conditioned permutation calibration for post-hoc representation measurements.
8JRPrcw01V.key_idea: Estimate distance-weighted local label composition and calibrate its entropy against geometry-conditioned permutations at matched effective support.
8JRPrcw01V.evidence: Controlled geometry-semantics tests and cross-modal studies cover SimCLR, VICReg, audio, time series, text, and sleep EEG, with ablations and robustness checks.
8JRPrcw01V.claimed_gains: Calibration reduces geometric artifacts by 13.8× and reveals an audio fine-to-coarse reversal with interaction T = 0.591 nats and family-wise p = 0.0025.
8JRPrcw01V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the depth-and-scale measurement question is clear and that permutation calibration and robustness checks provide careful statistical analysis.
8JRPrcw01V.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the added value over multiscale kNN entropy insufficiently demonstrated.

VjZUDCi95h.one_liner: Both-side paraphrasing suppresses source-model shortcuts in DPO data built from unlabeled dialog logs.
VjZUDCi95h.problem: Cross-model preference pairs encode source-model fingerprints that let DPO exploit style rather than semantic response quality.
VjZUDCi95h.method: The pipeline chooses stronger-system responses and rejects weaker ones, then normalizes, length-balances, and paraphrases both sides at sentence level before DPO training.
VjZUDCi95h.key_idea: Paraphrase chosen and rejected responses with a shared sentence-level process to reduce model-specific fingerprints while preserving semantic preference signals.
VjZUDCi95h.evidence: Training uses 77K–11M pairs from about 12M real conversations, with held-out, WildChat, AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, cross-model, judge-family, and paraphraser controls.
VjZUDCi95h.claimed_gains: Phi-4 (14B) gains up to +7.8pp held out, and +6.2pp, +3.1pp, and +5.0pp on WildChat, AlpacaEval, and Arena-Hard; Qwen-2.5-14B gains +6.7pp held out and +2.9pp on WildChat.
VjZUDCi95h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the source-label confound is well motivated and that simple preprocessing receives unusually detailed ablations and cross-model controls.
VjZUDCi95h.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing reward-model or ordinary-DPO controls and small gains over cheaper preprocessing variants.

RkBLAhvxt3.one_liner: Proves fast learning-rate transfer rates and limiting distributions in shallow linear networks when width and horizon grow jointly.
RkBLAhvxt3.problem: Hyperparameter transfer across model width is poorly understood when the training horizon grows alongside network width.
RkBLAhvxt3.method: The authors analyze full-batch gradient descent in a shallow linear network with one trainable hidden matrix under spectral assumptions as width and horizon grow. They bound transfer error using perturbation scales, loss sensitivities, and local curvature, and derive limiting distributions for optimal learning rates and losses.
RkBLAhvxt3.key_idea: Characterizes joint width-horizon learning-rate transfer via finite-width perturbation scales, first-order loss sensitivities, and extreme Gram-matrix eigenvalues.
RkBLAhvxt3.evidence: Theoretical proofs for growing horizons up to o(sqrt(n)), a single-eigenvalue counterexample, and a numerical study over 5 to 16 updates.
RkBLAhvxt3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit transfer-error rates, limiting distributions, and counterexample showing optimal learning-rate convergence alone does not ensure fast transfer.
RkBLAhvxt3.main_concern: Reviewers point out the restricted linear fixed-feature setting with T smaller than sqrt(n) and substantial technical overlap with prior quadratic-objective analyses like Wen et al.

aUynhtf6Gk.one_liner: Benchmarks long-video understanding using 6,300+ open-ended theory-of-mind questions and rubrics built from film screenplays.
aUynhtf6Gk.problem: Existing long-video QA benchmarks rely on short answers or multiple choice, reducing evaluation to moment retrieval rather than cross-scene synthesis.
aUynhtf6Gk.method: LF-VideoQA automatically annotates 94 recent film screenplays with scene events and character first-order beliefs and meta-beliefs to generate verified question-answer-rubric triples. Models are scored for recall and precision against question-specific rubrics across screenplay, subtitle, video, and retrieval-agent settings.
aUynhtf6Gk.key_idea: Constructs open-ended multi-scene theory-of-mind questions and precision-recall rubrics automatically from annotated character beliefs in film screenplays.
aUynhtf6Gk.evidence: Evaluates four families of open-source VLMs across three settings on over 6,300 questions spanning 94 films, plus a 150-question human validation study.
aUynhtf6Gk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing long-video QA around distributed theory-of-mind reasoning and rubric-scored open-ended answers addresses a real evaluation gap.
aUynhtf6Gk.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing question-only contamination controls, reliance on screenplays rather than video as ground truth, and potential cascading errors with limited human agreement validation.

Ze8uIYTF99.one_liner: Reconstructs 3D multi-person sports poses from uncalibrated broadcast views by training a transformer solely on synthetic geometric modalities.
Ze8uIYTF99.problem: Dynamic broadcast sports lack 3D supervision and suffer from textureless, repetitive backgrounds and uncalibrated long-range cameras.
Ze8uIYTF99.method: MuPeT trains a Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer exclusively on synthetic renderings of human segmentations, dense landmarks, and pitch lines rather than RGB images. Because these structured geometric inputs are cheap to rasterize and easy to extract from real footage, the model transfers zero-shot to real broadcasts.
Ze8uIYTF99.key_idea: Replaces RGB with rasterized segmentations, dense landmarks, and pitch lines so a 3D transformer trains purely on synthetic data without appearance sim-to-real gaps.
Ze8uIYTF99.evidence: Evaluated on the RugbyBench dataset against COLMAP + LightGlue and UncaliPose on impact reconstruction scenarios.
Ze8uIYTF99.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using structured geometric modalities to bridge synthetic training and real uncalibrated broadcast reconstruction is practical and well-aligned with the task.
Ze8uIYTF99.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about reliance on an unpublished RugbyBench dataset, potential overfitting to benchmark-specific camera and player spatial priors, and missing geometric-pipeline baselines.

XtSWOIvvwp.one_liner: Decomposes only one side of Q-K and V-O weight pairs adaptively by rank sensitivity for vision attention compression.
XtSWOIvvwp.problem: Standard low-rank weight decomposition compresses Q, K, V, and O matrices independently, ignoring the linear Q-K and V-O pairings in multi-head attention.
XtSWOIvvwp.method: UniDec exploits Q-K and V-O weight-space symmetries to factorize only one matrix per pair and adaptively chooses which side to decompose per head using rank-sensitivity criteria without fine-tuning.
XtSWOIvvwp.key_idea: Applies low-rank decomposition to only one side of each Q-K and V-O pair, selected per head by rank sensitivity without fine-tuning.
XtSWOIvvwp.evidence: Evaluated across vision backbones (DeiT-Small, DeiT-S Distill, DeiT-Base), detection, segmentation, and multimodal tasks with latency and FLOPs.
XtSWOIvvwp.claimed_gains: At 60% MHA reduction, UniDec improves Top-1 accuracy by +34.0% on DeiT-Small, +46.3% on DeiT-S Distill, and +0.7% on DeiT-Base.
XtSWOIvvwp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that UniDec is simple, operates without fine-tuning, and consistently outperforms independent per-weight SVD across vision tasks.
XtSWOIvvwp.main_concern: It omits experimental comparison against COMCAT (which also exploits Q-K/V-O products), and dynamic side selection barely outperforms always decomposing K and O.

8cjasJqXfx.one_liner: Learns shared Tucker mode factors and task-specific cores via distributed spectral initialization and alternating projected gradient descent.
8cjasJqXfx.problem: Distributed multi-task tensor regression must capture both intra-task multidimensional structure and inter-task relatedness while remaining communication-efficient.
8cjasJqXfx.method: D-AltMin-PGD models task tensors with shared mode-wise factors and task-specific cores, initializes via distributed power iteration, and optimizes via communication-efficient alternating projected gradient descent (plus a preconditioned variant D-AltMin-P2GD).
8cjasJqXfx.key_idea: Combines shared-factor Tucker decomposition with distributed spectral initialization and alternating projected gradient descent for multi-task tensor regression.
8cjasJqXfx.evidence: Proves initialization, linear convergence, preconditioning, and minimax lower-bound theorems, alongside synthetic, HSI, and MRI experiments.
8cjasJqXfx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the shared-Tucker distributed optimization framework and its theoretical package (initialization, convergence, minimax bounds) are thorough.
8cjasJqXfx.main_concern: Experiments reuse samples rather than matching the sample-splitting theory, and SNR/scaling assumptions may weaken the practical multi-task gain.

3Y7jslvpCm.one_liner: Calibrates target-versus-pretrained log-probability gains using the fine-tuned LLM's own next-token distribution for membership inference.
3Y7jslvpCm.problem: In fine-tuned LLMs, token log-probability gains over the pretrained model reflect domain adaptation as well as memorization, inflating false positives in reference-based MIAs.
3Y7jslvpCm.method: Diana centers each token's log-probability gain by subtracting its expectation under the target model's own next-token distribution and divides by regularized gain variance, plugging into reference-based MIAs without auxiliary data or training.
3Y7jslvpCm.key_idea: Uses the fine-tuned model's own predictive distribution as a per-token null to center and variance-normalize target-reference log-probability gains.
3Y7jslvpCm.evidence: Evaluated Ratio+Diana across six corpora and multiple model families with ablations isolating centering and variance weighting at low FPR.
3Y7jslvpCm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Diana is simple, data-free, and substantially improves low-FPR membership inference performance across corpora.
3Y7jslvpCm.main_concern: Using the target model as its own null may absorb memorization signals, novelty over Min-K%++ is modest, and theory relies on idealized mean predictions.

hksHkmMbvU.one_liner: Uses preregistered agent-RL experiments to show seed re-execution variance and how budget rules and ceiling effects govern horizon-scaling claims.
hksHkmMbvU.problem: Agent-RL credit-assignment papers report comparisons over three seeds without specifying the unit of replication, estimand, or statistical support.
hksHkmMbvU.method: The authors run preregistered experiments on KnobChain and ALFWorld with GiGPO to measure bitwise reproducibility across configurations, variance explained by random seeds, and how horizon-dependent credit-assignment trends change under proportional versus fixed update budgets.
hksHkmMbvU.key_idea: Separating seed execution variance from training-budget rules and success-ceiling effects reveals when apparent horizon-scaling gains in agent RL are artifacts of experimental design.
hksHkmMbvU.evidence: Preregistered experiments on KnobChain and ALFWorld with GiGPO, plus a bitwise replay census across 15 configurations.
hksHkmMbvU.claimed_gains: At default settings, re-running a seed reproduces a run bit-for-bit in 1 of 15 configurations; pooled seed variance estimates range from 0.02 to 0.13 (upper bounds at most 0.28); KnobChain's gap shrinks about threefold under a horizon-proportional budget.
hksHkmMbvU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the methodological transparency, preregistration, and importance of examining replication and horizon-scaling artifacts in agentic RL.
hksHkmMbvU.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the dense, heavily hedged writing style that obscures primary claims and note that seed nondeterminism findings are largely known in classical deep RL.

quVsAPDOqR.one_liner: Benchmarks indirect prompt injection via 90 authority-boundary task-tampering cases targeting six distinct components of agent decision-making.
quVsAPDOqR.problem: Existing indirect prompt-injection benchmarks focus on task redirection rather than unauthorized tampering with parameters or beliefs inside an ongoing benign task.
quVsAPDOqR.method: The authors define IPI by source authority and construct a 90-case benchmark across three tool-use environments where attacks tamper with one of six decision components (objective, decision rules, actions, consequences, observations, or state beliefs) while holding task and harmful outcome fixed, evaluating five LLMs and runtime defenses.
quVsAPDOqR.key_idea: Holding the benign task and harmful outcome fixed while varying which of six decision-making components an unauthorized source tampers with isolates defense blind spots.
quVsAPDOqR.evidence: Evaluations of five LLMs across 90 validated cases under detection-and-removal and tool-policy (e.g., CaMeL) defenses.
quVsAPDOqR.claimed_gains: Detection-and-removal reduces objective-targeting attacks to 2.4% success but leaves observation- and state-targeting attacks at 9.5% and 12.1% across five LLMs.
quVsAPDOqR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled within-case design holding task, sink, and outcome fixed across six tampering targets and the mechanism-level defense breakdown.
quVsAPDOqR.main_concern: Reviewers note that omitting system prompts with role/trust instructions overstates attack success (appendix shows 17.0% drops to 8.9%), CaMeL's 13.3% benign success indicates adaptation issues, and scenario counts differ across attack types.

5oBtwoit2F.one_liner: Coordinates independent arm-local Vision-Language-Action policies by exchanging learned latent representations across policy boundaries.
5oBtwoit2F.problem: Centralized joint policies for multi-arm manipulation scale poorly, while how independent action-producing VLAs should explicitly interact during generation is underexplored.
5oBtwoit2F.method: VLA-Fabric assigns one complete VLA per arm while preserving local perception and action ownership, introducing learned interaction modules across shared context, peer-specific latents, and action-stage generation, instantiated across two VLA architectures.
5oBtwoit2F.key_idea: Keeps arm-local VLA policies modular while exchanging shared-context, private-latent, and action-stage signals across policy boundaries.
5oBtwoit2F.evidence: Evaluated on two VLA architectures (TwinVLA/SingleVLA and pi0.5) across two-, three-, and four-arm simulation and physical manipulation tasks.
5oBtwoit2F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the modular multi-arm coordination design and systematic ablations of interaction locations across two VLA architectures and real robots.
5oBtwoit2F.main_concern: Reviewers find the Common/Private interaction definitions under-specified, question whether dense per-layer synchronization preserves modularity, and note inconsistencies between evaluation tables.

YIKFIPyb8M.one_liner: Prototypes zero-knowledge LLM agents that bind inference to registered weights and privately parse and authorize tool calls.
YIKFIPyb8M.problem: Standard zero-knowledge LLM inference proofs verify computation correctness but not whether an approved model ran or generated actions are authorized.
YIKFIPyb8M.method: The authors build an interactive zero-knowledge prototype for Q12 fixed-point GPT-2 Small using streamed Reed-Solomon checks to bind consumed private weights to a registry, a shared authenticated lookup interface for top-k sampling and private call parsing, and public-policy authorization checks.
YIKFIPyb8M.key_idea: Chains streamed Reed-Solomon weight-registration checks with an authenticated lookup interface that proves exact top-k sampling and private tool-call parsing before authorization.
YIKFIPyb8M.evidence: Prototype implementation and matched optimization ablations on Q12 fixed-point GPT-2 Small with seven prescribed tool-call cases.
YIKFIPyb8M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting weight identity, verifiable generation, and private tool-call authorization addresses an important gap with careful ablations.
YIKFIPyb8M.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the narrow evaluation (GPT-2 Small, seven prescribed cases), high verification cost, and weaker 40-bit semi-honest security assumptions.

KhybCAUzl9.one_liner: Balances shared-policy multi-agent RL by averaging token losses per response and responses per role with explicit role weights.
KhybCAUzl9.problem: Shared-policy multi-agent RL objectives overweight roles that produce longer responses or are invoked more frequently in the workflow.
KhybCAUzl9.method: RBPO trains a single role-conditioned policy across Planner, Coder, and Reflector roles in an execution-guided refinement loop. It averages token losses within each response, averages responses within each role, and combines role losses with explicit weights independent of response length and invocation count.
KhybCAUzl9.key_idea: Applies hierarchical two-level averaging—tokens within responses, then responses within roles—with explicit role weights to decouple optimization from workflow exposure.
KhybCAUzl9.evidence: Evaluated on LiveCodeBench (LCB-v6) and DeepCoder with Qwen3-8B across 2x2 sequence/role-balancing ablations and role-removal analyses.
KhybCAUzl9.claimed_gains: Achieves 60.7% accuracy on LiveCodeBench with Qwen3-8B, beating Qwen3-8B GRPO by 9.8 percentage points, non-RL workflow by 10.4 points, and a Qwen3-14B multi-agent baseline by 1.3 points.
KhybCAUzl9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree workflow-exposure imbalance in shared-policy MARL is clearly motivated and cleanly tested by the 2x2 ablation.
KhybCAUzl9.main_concern: Reviewers critique reporting only 2-seed averages with small margins (0.7 pp sequence balancing), testing only one fixed workflow, and mixing PPO/workflow changes against GRPO.

a0st86YwNb.one_liner: Characterizes when linear-head cross-entropy stationarity guarantees multiclass calibration and derives high-probability finite-sample projected smooth calibration certificates.
a0st86YwNb.problem: A vanishing cross-entropy gradient on frozen features does not guarantee calibrated multiclass probabilities, and finite-sample calibration guarantees are limited.
a0st86YwNb.method: For finite-support inputs, they prove zero population cross-entropy gradient guarantees calibration for all label distributions iff linear feature combinations isolate each equal-prediction group. They further derive a high-probability finite-sample certificate for projected smooth calibration decomposing optimization error, computable representation error, and finite-sample uncertainty.
a0st86YwNb.key_idea: Establishes exact feature-isolation conditions for cross-entropy stationarity to imply calibration and decomposes finite-sample projected smooth calibration into computable error bounds.
a0st86YwNb.evidence: Supported by formal theorems and counterexamples plus empirical certificate evaluations on real features (restricted to m=1 and anchor approximations).
a0st86YwNb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the precise linear-algebraic condition linking cross-entropy stationarity to calibration and the post-training error decomposition.
a0st86YwNb.main_concern: Reviewers note dense, hard-to-follow presentation, restrictive assumptions (frozen features, finite support, worst-case over all label distributions), and loose anchor-based bounds in experiments.

5d77FDxMBe.one_liner: Steers frozen inverse-folding antibody decoders using a closed-form 19-parameter amino-acid logit bias estimated from reward differences.
5d77FDxMBe.problem: Inverse-folding models optimize structural compatibility rather than binding, while full-parameter fine-tuning fails to reweight within-backbone candidate designs effectively.
5d77FDxMBe.method: PACT estimates a shared 19-degree-of-freedom amino-acid bias in closed form from within-backbone Rosetta reward differences and adds it directly to frozen decoder logits without gradient training.
5d77FDxMBe.key_idea: Applies a closed-form 19-parameter global amino-acid composition bias to frozen inverse-folding decoder logits instead of full-parameter fine-tuning.
5d77FDxMBe.evidence: Evaluations across three antigens, six fine-tuning objectives, RF2 refolding, and zero-shot transfer to ESM-IF and AntiFold.
5d77FDxMBe.claimed_gains: Across three antigens, PACT improves mean Rosetta interface reward by 0.32–0.63 and outperforms filtered SFT by 0.99–1.83 units.
5d77FDxMBe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simplicity of the gradient-free intervention and the gradient-kernel diagnostic explaining why full-parameter fine-tuning fails.
5d77FDxMBe.main_concern: Reviewers note that PACT does not clearly outperform a side-chain volume prior on two targets, lacks intermediate-capacity baselines like LoRA, and uses an unvalidated surrogate reward.

NRkcXVPvTk.one_liner: Tracks sparse 3D points from monocular events using pre-trigger brightness history matching and anchor-relative trajectory prediction.
NRkcXVPvTk.problem: Monocular event cameras produce sparse, intermittent events without direct depth along the viewing ray, making 3D point tracking ambiguous.
NRkcXVPvTk.method: SPAR scores candidate correspondences via Hit-Survival (observed events plus implied pre-trigger brightness history) and predicts 3D displacements relative to an initial depth anchor using a Query-conditioned Anchor-Relative Trajectory head.
NRkcXVPvTk.key_idea: Score event correspondences by both observed events and implied pre-trigger brightness history, then regress 3D offsets relative to an initial depth anchor.
NRkcXVPvTk.evidence: Experiments evaluate 2D and 3D tracking on the newly constructed EventTraj3D dataset (13.630B events, 6,494 trajectories) and E-3DTrack.
NRkcXVPvTk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SPAR achieves strong 2D/3D tracking accuracy on EventTraj3D and E-3DTrack without requiring subsequent RGB or stereo frames.
NRkcXVPvTk.main_concern: Reviewers find the paper dense and difficult to read and note that ablations remove Hit and Survival together rather than isolating pre-trigger history.

E0fwXNGh5P.one_liner: Replaces linear dendritic branch readouts with distal-modulated proximal nonlinear modulation and causal-window soma firing.
E0fwXNGh5P.problem: Linear weighted-sum branch readouts in multi-compartment dendritic neurons collapse into single convolutions and limit intra-branch expressivity.
E0fwXNGh5P.method: NR-DN assigns proximal and distal roles within each branch, modulates proximal responses using distal state differences, and integrates branch outputs in a soma with a learnable causal window and bounded integer firing.
E0fwXNGh5P.key_idea: Modulate proximal dendritic compartment responses nonlinearly using state differences from distal compartments within each branch.
E0fwXNGh5P.evidence: Experiments evaluate NR-DN inside sequence backbones like S4 on image, speech, and Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmarks.
E0fwXNGh5P.claimed_gains: S4 equipped with NR-DN achieves 87.53% average accuracy on the Long Range Arena benchmark.
E0fwXNGh5P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical observation that linear multi-compartment readouts collapse to convolutions and the competitive, lightweight LRA/S-CIFAR performance.
E0fwXNGh5P.main_concern: Reviewers note the missing comparison to DendSN and missing controlled ablations replacing DMPR with a plain linear readout under identical soma and training settings.

tQwrwoX7Ob.one_liner: Retrieves Lean premises using a directed multi-relational GCN over normalized expression graphs followed by structural collapse-match reranking.
tQwrwoX7Ob.problem: Semantic similarity misses syntactic roles in Lean premise selection, while elaboration creates varying expression trees for similar terms.
tQwrwoX7Ob.method: R-DGCN normalizes expression trees, encodes typed constructor-field and reverse edges with a relation-specific GCN using mean and attention pooling, and reranks precomputed embeddings via directed collapse-match.
tQwrwoX7Ob.key_idea: Encode normalized Lean expression graphs with typed constructor-field and reverse edges in a relational GCN, then rerank retrieved theorems by directed structural collapse-match.
tQwrwoX7Ob.evidence: Evaluations test retrieval recall and latency over 218K Mathlib theorems across three test sets.
tQwrwoX7Ob.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that R-DGCN is a well-engineered system showing strong recall gains and low latency, with complementary learned and structural scores.
tQwrwoX7Ob.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about potential data leakage from record-level train/validation splits sharing parent declarations and missing comparisons to fine-tuned pretrained language models.

RPC0exv7EG.one_liner: Factorizes feature interaction power in quadratic modular-addition networks into mode magnitude, block balance, and cross-block overlap.
RPC0exv7EG.problem: Understanding how neural networks co-locate and combine learned Fourier components across hidden units during grokking remains incomplete.
RPC0exv7EG.method: The authors derive an exact factorization of interaction power in quadratic networks for modular addition, a state-dependent covariance law for overlap under gradient flow, and a finite-step optimizer identity, tested via surgical interventions on Adam and Muon runs.
RPC0exv7EG.key_idea: Decomposes multiplicative feature interaction power into mode magnitude, block balance, and cross-block overlap under gradient flow and finite-step updates.
RPC0exv7EG.evidence: Theoretical derivations and controlled surgical intervention experiments on Adam and Muon quadratic networks trained on modular addition.
RPC0exv7EG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear distinction between tied and untied streams and the careful, well-controlled surgical intervention experiments.
RPC0exv7EG.main_concern: The theoretical identities hold by definition without predicting grokking dynamics, and empirical overlap growth is mostly driven by within-block sparsity (~70%) rather than cross-block alignment (~10%).

C9ojgSCfGv.one_liner: Pretrains a Prior-data Fitted Network with supervised cross-entropy to select the best Bayesian optimization candidate in one forward pass.
C9ojgSCfGv.problem: Standard Bayesian optimization requires refitting surrogates and numerically maximizing acquisition functions at every step, while learned acquisitions rely on reinforcement learning.
C9ojgSCfGv.method: IQS-BO pretrains a transformer on synthetic prior functions using supervised classification labels identifying the maximum candidate in a finite set, predicting winner probabilities in a single forward pass with or without a surrogate.
C9ojgSCfGv.key_idea: Pretrains a PFN via supervised cross-entropy on synthetic functions to predict which candidate maximizes the objective in one forward pass.
C9ojgSCfGv.evidence: Evaluations on synthetic and benchmark black-box and batch Bayesian optimization tasks comparing optimization performance and query-selection runtime.
C9ojgSCfGv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the supervised formulation simpler than RL-based acquisition learning and note substantial query-proposal speedups.
C9ojgSCfGv.main_concern: Predicting the highest-value candidate aligns with 0-1 loss rather than regret minimization or exploration-exploitation, and comparisons against surrogate Monte Carlo sampling are missing.

UUnKWJdy0h.one_liner: Benchmarks how varying valuation disclosure granularity changes efficiency and surplus division across ten LLMs in economic games.
UUnKWJdy0h.problem: It is unclear when disclosing more detailed private information to interacting LLM agents improves or degrades collective economic outcomes.
UUnKWJdy0h.method: Empirical information design holds markets, models, and interaction rules fixed while varying disclosure policies (such as coarse preference rankings versus exact valuations) across multi-resource trade, single-good bargaining, and double auctions. Outcomes are compared against ground-truth utilities across ten frontier LLMs.
UUnKWJdy0h.key_idea: Holds markets and models fixed while varying information disclosure granularity across three economic games to measure effects on total gains and division.
UUnKWJdy0h.evidence: Tested ten frontier LLMs across multi-resource trade, single-good bargaining, and double auctions using ground-truth utility benchmarks.
UUnKWJdy0h.claimed_gains: Relative to coarse disclosure in trade, GPT-6 Sol's total gains fall from 98% to 91% while Claude Sonnet 5's rise from 72% to 86%; in auctions, full disclosure lowers Claude Opus 5.5's total gains from 95% to 64% and Grok 4.7's from 97% to 62%.
UUnKWJdy0h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written and addresses an interesting question with controlled comparisons across economic games.
UUnKWJdy0h.main_concern: Reviewers question generalizability beyond three simple games, note the lack of repeated runs, and challenge the assumption of truthful, noise-free valuation disclosure.

WRsjovOOdb.one_liner: Probes and patches spectral subspaces in Prior-Data Fitted Networks and decodes frozen representations into explicit stationary GP kernels.
WRsjovOOdb.problem: It is unknown whether Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) internally represent context frequency spectra or whether those representations can be read out as explicit kernels.
WRsjovOOdb.method: The authors apply linear probes and activation/subspace patching to seven PFNs (including pretrained TFMs and a decision-tree-prior model) to locate low-dimensional spectral directions driving predictions. They also introduce a Filter Bank Decoder to extract explicit stationary Gaussian process kernels from frozen PFN representations.
WRsjovOOdb.key_idea: Uses linear probing, subspace patching, and a Filter Bank Decoder to show PFNs encode context frequency in low-dimensional subspaces readable as explicit stationary kernels.
WRsjovOOdb.evidence: Tested across seven PFNs (including four pretrained TFMs and a decision-tree-prior model) on synthetic and real tabular datasets with up to 499 features.
WRsjovOOdb.claimed_gains: Linear probes recover context frequency with R^2 >= 0.95 across all seven PFNs, and 64 of 192 TabPFN directions carry 85-95% of causal context effect on real datasets.
WRsjovOOdb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spectral-structure analysis across diverse PFNs (including a non-spectral decision-tree prior) is novel, thorough, and well-written.
WRsjovOOdb.main_concern: Reviewers flag reproducibility issues in the code supplement, a mismatched random-PFN decoder control, and a raw-input decoder matching the latent decoder.

S7iWleTOw2.one_liner: Studies how much and which executable specification conditions external runtime supervision needs to prevent agent false completion.
S7iWleTOw2.problem: Language model agents routinely declare unfinished workflows complete, and it is unclear how many and which success conditions an external runtime verifier must hold.
S7iWleTOw2.method: Using a dose-response experimental design with fixed agents, tasks, and step budgets, the authors vary the fraction and selection of executable success conditions held by the runtime, comparing silent gating, informative feedback, cross-model failure targeting, and learned verifiers.
S7iWleTOw2.key_idea: Varies runtime specification coverage in a controlled dose-response design to show supervision reliability depends on holding agent-failing policy and data conditions.
S7iWleTOw2.evidence: Evaluated across four models from four vendors on business workflow tasks with matched condition-swap and cross-model transfer experiments.
S7iWleTOw2.claimed_gains: Masks covering conditions an agent fails on its own pass more than twice as often as masks missing one across four models.
S7iWleTOw2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous controlled dose-response design, condition-swap interventions, and cross-model failure transfer findings.
S7iWleTOw2.main_concern: Reviewers question practical applicability because the supervisor relies on ground-truth executable conditions and notes limited novelty over prior test-based verification work.

DCbbbnzpEQ.one_liner: Optimizes a single transferable adversarial patch on a public visual encoder to disable world action models without target queries.
DCbbbnzpEQ.problem: Existing adversarial attacks on robotic world action models require querying target-model actions or predicted futures.
DCbbbnzpEQ.method: TAPDreamer optimizes a fixed 6.5%-area patch over six frames from one source task by maximizing the global L1 distance between clean and patched representations of a public visual encoder, exploiting attention-value interactions that broadcast representation shifts across the image.
DCbbbnzpEQ.key_idea: Maximizes global L1 feature shift on a public visual encoder using six frames to craft a query-free patch that broadcasts disruption via attention.
DCbbbnzpEQ.evidence: Closed-loop evaluations on 40 LIBERO tasks and 50 RoboTwin tasks across multiple world action architectures, plus attention-restoration diagnostics.
DCbbbnzpEQ.claimed_gains: Reduces FastWAM success rate from 97.7% to 0.0% across 40 LIBERO tasks and from 90.8% to 0.0% across 50 RoboTwin tasks (random patches retain 81.5% and 79.2%).
DCbbbnzpEQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the strong closed-loop attack rates without target queries and the mechanistic attention-restoration analysis.
DCbbbnzpEQ.main_concern: Reviewers note high sensitivity to exact patch position limiting physical deployability, possible reliance on shared Wan2.2 encoders across victims, and limited novelty over feature-space L1 attacks.

nleAansyLY.one_liner: Benchmarks long-term web-agent memory across 451 questions over 115M-token trajectory histories, plus RAG and coding-agent baselines.
nleAansyLY.problem: Existing agent memory benchmarks test user preferences or short traces rather than whether memory systems internalize environment workflows, state dynamics, and gotchas.
nleAansyLY.method: LongMemEval-V2 introduces 451 curated questions across five web-agent memory abilities paired with up to 500 history trajectories (115M tokens). The authors also propose AgentRunbook-R (multi-pool RAG) and AgentRunbook-C (file-based coding agent) baselines.
nleAansyLY.key_idea: Evaluates agent memory over massive trajectory haystacks across five operational abilities using a context-gathering QA formulation.
nleAansyLY.evidence: Evaluated RAG and coding-agent memory baselines on 451 manually verified questions across four web-agent domains.
nleAansyLY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the five well-defined memory abilities, large-scale human-verified trajectory benchmark, and domain relevance.
nleAansyLY.main_concern: Reviewers point out confounded comparisons between RAG (Qwen3.5-9B + dense search) and coding-agent baselines (GPT-5.4-mini + lexical search), plus artificial haystack construction.

NzzWQSTuyp.one_liner: Learns linear projections of text embeddings into Brier and Log-Cosh proper scoring rules aligned with human or LLM judges.
NzzWQSTuyp.problem: Reference-based text metrics and LLM judges are vulnerable to strategic manipulation, while traditional proper scoring rules align poorly with human judgments.
NzzWQSTuyp.method: The framework encodes reported and ground-truth texts in a shared representation, learns a common linear projection, and fits Brier or Log-Cosh proper scoring rules to target judge scores, bounding strategic manipulation gains by squared representation error.
NzzWQSTuyp.key_idea: Projects shared text representations linearly into Brier or Log-Cosh proper scoring rules fitted to target judge scores for manipulation-resistant evaluation.
NzzWQSTuyp.evidence: Theoretical properness bounds and experiments on peer grading and question answering measuring judge alignment and manipulation robustness.
NzzWQSTuyp.claimed_gains: Improves alignment with target judge scores while resisting evaluated manipulation strategies (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
NzzWQSTuyp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining proper scoring rules with learned textual judges addresses an important manipulation-alignment tradeoff.
NzzWQSTuyp.main_concern: Reviewers question whether real LLM embeddings satisfy the linear belief-encoding assumption, note mismatched backbones across Brier/Log-Cosh comparisons, and cite closely related prior work.

A0Z6QdvyPi.one_liner: Accelerates degree-profile random graph matching via selective distance computation and high-noise continuous refinement.
A0Z6QdvyPi.problem: Degree-profile graph matching requires computing all pairwise vertex distances in O((n^2 + nd^2) log n) time and degrades under high noise.
A0Z6QdvyPi.method: LiDP first selectively computes degree-profile distances to reduce complexity to O(n^2 + nd^2) while preserving exact recovery certificates, then warm-starts a continuous nonconvex optimization stage when recovery fails under high noise.
A0Z6QdvyPi.key_idea: Pairs certified selective pairwise-distance computation with a continuous doubly-stochastic refinement stage triggered under high noise.
A0Z6QdvyPi.evidence: Provides exact-recovery and stationary-point theory alongside experiments on synthetic correlated Erdos-Renyi graphs and real-world networks.
A0Z6QdvyPi.claimed_gains: Reduces complexity from O((n^2+nd^2)log n) to O(n^2+nd^2) and achieves 10x-20x speedups in low-noise regimes.
A0Z6QdvyPi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical speedup of selective distance computation, skipping over 94% of the distance matrix.
A0Z6QdvyPi.main_concern: Reviewers challenge the O(n^2 + nd^2) complexity proof for regular graphs and note that the continuous-stage recovery guarantees rely on unverified separation conditions.

iQ0n4eljPQ.one_liner: Probes fMRI brain alignment of instruction-tuned multimodal LLMs under identical naturalistic movie stimuli and varying task prompts.
iQ0n4eljPQ.problem: Prior brain-alignment studies of instruction-tuned models used unimodal stimuli, leaving unclear whether multimodal IT models encode task structure beyond prompt wording.
iQ0n4eljPQ.method: Predicts fMRI responses during naturalistic movie watching from three matched pairs of pretrained (ICL-prompted) and instruction-tuned MLLMs given identical instructions, comparing RSA correlations and task-conditioned cortical maps.
iQ0n4eljPQ.key_idea: Compares matched pretrained and instruction-tuned MLLMs on naturalistic audiovisual fMRI encoding across varying task prompts while holding stimuli fixed.
iQ0n4eljPQ.evidence: Evaluated on naturalistic movie fMRI data across three matched MLLM pairs (Qwen-2-VL, Qwen-2.5-VL, InternVL3) plus audio and unimodal baselines.
iQ0n4eljPQ.claimed_gains: ICL representations track instruction-text semantics (r = 0.69-0.78), whereas IT representations are largely decoupled from wording (r = 0.13-0.16).
iQ0n4eljPQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the matched pretrained-vs-IT model comparisons and the fixed-stimulus multi-instruction fMRI probing design.
iQ0n4eljPQ.main_concern: Reviewers argue that using a single prompt per task confounds task identity with prompt wording and response format, and question novelty over prior instruction-brain studies.

odbGl8MVa0.one_liner: Models Riemannian dense associative memory as Epanechnikov kernel-density mode seeking and characterizes curvature effects on capacity and emergent modes.
odbGl8MVa0.problem: How manifold curvature and volume corrections govern memory retention, storage capacity, and emergent spurious modes in associative memories is poorly understood.
odbGl8MVa0.method: The paper defines intrinsic dense associative memories on Riemannian manifolds via Epanechnikov kernel-density mode seeking with one-step Riemannian mean shift, comparing geodesic and volume-corrected energies and deriving Ricci-curvature stability thresholds, capacity scalings, and Poisson limits for emergent subset modes.
odbGl8MVa0.key_idea: Casts Riemannian associative memory as Epanechnikov kernel-density mode seeking to derive Ricci-curvature stability thresholds and emergent mode limits.
odbGl8MVa0.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs, simulations recovering curvature transitions and 2^N-1 subset modes, and retrieval experiments on WordNet's full noun hierarchy (plus EEG/leaf checks noted by a reviewer).
odbGl8MVa0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical connection between Ricci curvature, geodesic versus volume-corrected energies, and mode persistence.
odbGl8MVa0.main_concern: Retrieval guarantees apply only to geodesic energy while the headline WordNet improvement relies on volume-corrected energy, and the practical evaluation on 16-memory banks is narrow.

L1u3iJc9Yd.one_liner: Updates persistent episodic memory and state-graph repair rules from completed agent trajectories guided by a domain Evolution-SOP.
L1u3iJc9Yd.problem: LLM agents repeat the same execution failures across tasks because post-episode feedback does not update the persistent harness.
L1u3iJc9Yd.method: Living-Harness converts completed trajectories and evaluator scores into bounded updates guided by a domain-level Evolution-SOP, writing trigger-action pairs to episodic memory and state nodes/repair edges to a state graph while keeping tools and base context frozen.
L1u3iJc9Yd.key_idea: Turns post-episode trajectory evidence into persistent episodic-memory and state-graph updates under a domain Evolution-SOP while freezing tools and base context.
L1u3iJc9Yd.evidence: Evaluated on eight interactive environments derived from tau^2-Bench and MultiWOZ-2.4.
L1u3iJc9Yd.claimed_gains: Living-Harness improves average Pass@1 over the strongest interactive baseline by 10.07 percentage points on tau^2-Bench and 9.91 percentage points on MultiWOZ-2.4.
L1u3iJc9Yd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the separation of task-local reflection from persistent cross-episode procedural repair practical and well-motivated.
L1u3iJc9Yd.main_concern: Reliance on manually written, benchmark-specific Evolution-SOPs containing concrete tool repair rules raises doubts about whether gains come from self-evolution or hand-crafted domain knowledge, alongside missing cost-matched and train/test isolation details.

XPsKX0Stse.one_liner: Fusing Hermite physical bridges with frozen-model snapshots corrects off-cadence PDE predictions without retraining or temporal integration.
XPsKX0Stse.problem: Direct off-cadence queries can bias PDE foundation-model predictions, while ordinary temporal upsampling ignores the governing dynamics.
XPsKX0Stse.method: KMF evaluates spatial PDE operators at neighboring snapshots, constructs a cubic Hermite candidate, and blends it with model estimates using a calibrated scalar. For rollout, it applies causal defect corrections and exact constraint projections before reusing the frozen model.
XPsKX0Stse.key_idea: Local spatial operator evaluations turn neighboring model snapshots into a physical bridge whose output is fused with the frozen model's estimate.
XPsKX0Stse.evidence: The paper derives local physical-bridge and endpoint-perturbation error bounds and evaluates multiple PDE systems, temporal cadences, and frozen foundation-model architectures.
XPsKX0Stse.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the frozen-model interface is practical and that the experiments carefully distinguish refinement, causal rollout, calibration sensitivity, and failures.
XPsKX0Stse.main_concern: Reviewers most often see limited novelty because the method combines established interpolation, defect correction, fusion, and constraint-projection techniques.

UqmrxAZQNE.one_liner: Unifying moment tensors within one detector localizes mean, covariance, and higher-order changes in dependent multivariate time series.
UqmrxAZQNE.problem: Existing change-point procedures do not jointly handle changes across moment orders while accommodating temporal dependence and growing dimension.
UqmrxAZQNE.method: The method represents moments through tensors in a common linear-algebraic framework and detects changes up to a fixed order p. It derives localization theory, minimax limits, jump distributions, and confidence intervals.
UqmrxAZQNE.key_idea: A tensor representation places different moment orders in one detection procedure, allowing higher-order distributional changes to alter the same statistic.
UqmrxAZQNE.evidence: Support includes a matching minimax lower bound, limiting distributions for nonvanishing and vanishing jumps, numerical experiments, and real-data analyses.
UqmrxAZQNE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the unified moment framework and its localization and inference theory are substantial contributions.
UqmrxAZQNE.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the empirical evaluation too narrow relative to the broad theory, with sparse baselines and limited real-data coverage.

PQsVU4kcQR.one_liner: Comparing adaptive patching with tuned uniform layouts shows little accuracy benefit and motivates a budgeted resolution-allocation theory.
PQsVU4kcQR.problem: Adaptive patching is assumed to help time-series forecasting, but controlled evidence against equally tuned uniform patch sizes remains limited.
PQsVU4kcQR.method: The paper compares three adaptive methods with uniform counterparts under shared backbones and training protocols. It then models patch layouts through resolution density and derives conditions for beneficial nonuniform allocation under a fixed budget.
PQsVU4kcQR.key_idea: A common resolution-density representation separates where patches place resolution from how much resolution they redistribute, enabling exact same-budget comparisons.
PQsVU4kcQR.evidence: Experiments evaluate three adaptive patching methods on long-horizon benchmarks, while theory gives local quadratic and global strongly convex loss bounds.
PQsVU4kcQR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the negative result is useful and that the resolution-density framework and routing-overhead measurements clarify accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs.
PQsVU4kcQR.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that the theory is disconnected from the experiments because its losses, weights, and resolution dispersion are not measured on real predictors.

9o7AwHHoKy.one_liner: Adapting Personalized PageRank seeds and outgoing transitions through multiplicative weights improves iterative long-document multi-hop retrieval.
9o7AwHHoKy.problem: Fixed-seed graph diffusion can miss distant multi-hop evidence or disperse probability across competing edges before intermediate reasoning reveals relevance.
9o7AwHHoKy.method: RCT-PPR uses an LLM controller to choose new seed entities and a semantic direction from retrieved context. A linear alignment loss drives multiplicative-weights updates over each node's outgoing simplex across retrieval rounds.
9o7AwHHoKy.key_idea: Semantic feedback updates normalized outgoing PageRank transitions with multiplicative weights, accumulating directional evidence while adapting restart seeds between rounds.
9o7AwHHoKy.evidence: Experiments on three LongBench multi-hop QA datasets include HippoRAG 2 comparisons, significance tests, failure analysis, and single-round and no-OCO ablations.
9o7AwHHoKy.claimed_gains: RCT-PPR achieves 53.3 average F1, exceeding HippoRAG 2 by 6.4 points, while ablations reduce F1 to 48.1 with one round and 51.3 without the OCO update.
9o7AwHHoKy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly adapting restart seeds and transitions is coherent and that the theoretical claims are appropriately limited to semantic-alignment regret.
9o7AwHHoKy.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that the incremental value of cumulative transition adaptation is not isolated from graph-configuration differences and simpler reweighting controls.

YKBjG1vgle.one_liner: Checking map geometry against foot support and collisions gates visual residuals for humanoid locomotion under faulty elevation maps.
YKBjG1vgle.problem: Obsolete or incomplete elevation maps can make visual terrain corrections cause misplaced humanoid steps and collisions.
YKBjG1vgle.method: SURE adds a visual residual to a proprioceptive base policy and compares mapped support heights and obstacle geometry with proprioceptive estimates. Physical contradictions withdraw the residual, while renewed foothold-map agreement restores it.
YKBjG1vgle.key_idea: Cross-modal physical consistency determines when to withdraw and later restore visual residual actions while the proprioceptive policy remains active.
YKBjG1vgle.evidence: Simulation tests cover accurate maps, map mismatch, and transient delay, and real-robot experiments use measured elevation maps with obstacle omission and delay.
YKBjG1vgle.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the physical gating rule is interpretable and that same-weight controls and restoration ablations isolate its behavior well.
YKBjG1vgle.main_concern: All three reviewers cite the missing comparison with VB-Com, leaving the advantage over return-based vision-blind fallback unresolved.

OeEE8LIkNg.one_liner: Reparametrizes continued-fraction network denominators via tridiagonal Hamiltonian spectral constraints to stabilize FFN replacement without incremental training.
OeEE8LIkNg.problem: Continued-fraction neural networks suffer from denominator poles and high sensitivity to non-smooth lower bounds, previously requiring complex incremental training procedures.
OeEE8LIkNg.method: Spec-CoFrGeNet introduces a smooth transformation of partial denominators motivated by Green's functions and tridiagonal Hamiltonian spectral bounds, eliminating poles and removing the need for incremental training. The authors replace Transformer FFNs with this architecture across language and diffusion generative models.
OeEE8LIkNg.key_idea: Applies a smooth diagonal-dominance spectral reparametrization to continued-fraction partial denominators to bound tridiagonal Hamiltonian spectra away from poles during standard training.
OeEE8LIkNg.evidence: Evaluated by replacing FFNs in GPT-2 XL, nano Llama-MoE, 2.14B Granite, and ImageNet DDT-XL/2 diffusion models with parameter-matched controls.
OeEE8LIkNg.claimed_gains: Achieves performance comparable to FFN-based architectures across GPT-2 XL, nano Llama-MoE, and Granite while maintaining roughly 30%-50% parameter savings.
OeEE8LIkNg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise fixing a real training instability (especially enabling diffusion training where prior CoFrGeNet fails) and investing in billion-parameter multi-architecture experiments.
OeEE8LIkNg.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental novelty over CoFrGeNet, point out that the 30%-50% parameter savings belong to the prior architecture rather than this reparametrization, and observe minimal language gains.

Re3dvjG4dX.one_liner: Identifies cross-statement attention as a driver of LLM neural collisions and mitigates them via attention blocking and targeted fine-tuning.
Re3dvjG4dX.problem: LLMs can fail on computations processed together within one forward pass even when each computation succeeds independently.
Re3dvjG4dX.method: The authors define and measure neural collisions across factual and multi-step reasoning prompts in three LLMs. Using causal attention-blocking interventions, they show that attention transfers interfering information between statements, and demonstrate that fine-tuning reduces collisions without hurting cross-statement integration tasks.
Re3dvjG4dX.key_idea: Diagnoses interference between co-occurring prompt computations via attention blocking and reduces collisions through targeted fine-tuning.
Re3dvjG4dX.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs (including Llama-3.1-8B) on paired factual and multi-step reasoning prompts with activation-patching, attention-blocking, and fine-tuning experiments.
Re3dvjG4dX.claimed_gains: Blocking interfering attention corrects 57-99% of collisions across three models, and fine-tuning lowers the collision rate in Llama-3.1-8B from 6.1% to 0.4%.
Re3dvjG4dX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear writing, clean paired-statement experimental setup, and use of causal interventions.
Re3dvjG4dX.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the analysis remains descriptive without pinpointing the underlying disruption mechanism, question whether evaluating one statement proves two simultaneous computations collide, and note limited scale and simple prompts.

8FnebG4Qb3.one_liner: Introduces a four-dimension behavioral rubric and harmonic-mean drop-penalized trajectory verifier to expose late-stage multi-turn LLM failures.
8FnebG4Qb3.problem: Aggregate task-success metrics and turn-averaged LLM judges mask severe late-stage behavioral breakdowns in multi-turn interactions.
8FnebG4Qb3.method: The authors propose RHCA, a literature-informed rubric scoring reasoning transparency, helpfulness, consistency, and context alignment, paired with the Behavioral Trajectory Verifier (BTV). BTV aggregates turn scores via a harmonic mean with a penalty for score drops from earlier highs to flag late-stage failures.
8FnebG4Qb3.key_idea: Combines a four-dimension behavioral rubric with a harmonic-mean trajectory score penalized for performance drops across turns.
8FnebG4Qb3.evidence: Supported by a formal property (Proposition 1), an in-depth music programming study, and cross-domain tasks created by 16 AI practitioners.
8FnebG4Qb3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that task success alone misses multi-turn behavioral breakdowns and that RHCA and BTV offer an interpretable, failure-sensitive alternative to simple averaging.
8FnebG4Qb3.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons to existing trajectory benchmarks and whole-conversation LLM judges, limited human validation (only four real conversations), and degradation of BTV sensitivity over longer dialogues.

UnHlDsjeoV.one_liner: Uses a fast-slow dual-system harness with a hypothesis graph, value-of-information experiment selection, and reward-grounded memory for continual robot adaptation.
UnHlDsjeoV.problem: Self-evolving agentic harnesses around robot foundation models waste physical trials when choosing which code and skill modifications to test.
UnHlDsjeoV.method: EmbodiedEvo maintains competing code and skill hypotheses in a Hypothesis Graph and selects physical trials via Value-of-Information Experiment Selection to distinguish among them for Code-Skill Co-Evolution. A Slow System builds Hierarchical Memory trained with Reward-Grounded Memory Learning to retain entries that improve later Fast-System adaptation.
UnHlDsjeoV.key_idea: Guides continual robot code-skill co-evolution by selecting physical trials via Value-of-Information over a Hypothesis Graph and learning memory retention from downstream adaptation rewards.
UnHlDsjeoV.evidence: Evaluated on RoboCasa365 (including Composite-Unseen), LIBERO-Pro, and real-world robot transfer with frozen VLA backbones.
UnHlDsjeoV.claimed_gains: Reaches 77.0% overall success and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen on RoboCasa365 (vs. 40.1% for the best baseline), and 86.8% overall success on LIBERO-Pro.
UnHlDsjeoV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise turning trial selection into an explicit cost-aware Value-of-Information decision over a structured Hypothesis Graph and report strong benchmark gains.
UnHlDsjeoV.main_concern: Reviewers flag unclear and inconsistent evaluation protocols (per-task evolution on test tasks with mismatched seed descriptions), unexplained higher success on Composite-Unseen than Composite-Seen, and uncounted LLM/VOI compute costs.

d5hmyYQVHg.one_liner: Traverses a dependency DAG of 214 prescriptive secure coding principles at inference time to iteratively harden LLM-generated code.
d5hmyYQVHg.problem: Vulnerability-centric code security defenses rely on curated past-vulnerability data, fail to generalize to unseen weaknesses, and are impractical for proprietary models.
d5hmyYQVHg.method: GRASP organizes 214 prescriptive Secure Coding Principles (from OWASP) into a directed acyclic graph encoding specialization and prerequisite dependencies. At inference time, it prunes irrelevant branches and iteratively applies applicable principles to the evolving program without training, weight access, or a static analyzer.
d5hmyYQVHg.key_idea: Traverse a 214-node dependency DAG of prescriptive secure coding principles to prune irrelevant rules and iteratively refine generated code at inference time.
d5hmyYQVHg.evidence: Evaluated across five models and three benchmarks against zero-shot, planning-based, retrieval-augmented, and analyzer-guided prompting.
d5hmyYQVHg.claimed_gains: Across five models, GRASP raises Security Rate from 0.46-0.55 at baseline to 0.70-0.84.
d5hmyYQVHg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using prescriptive coding principles in a training-free, analyzer-free, model-agnostic pipeline is clear and practical.
d5hmyYQVHg.main_concern: Ablations show removing the principle dependency DAG leaves Security Rate nearly unchanged (0.84 vs 0.82), reducing the graph's role to efficiency while lacking compute-matched baseline comparisons.

Ch62pc2CZs.one_liner: Trains a local clinical agent with RL to curb multi-turn quasi-identifier leakage to remote specialists while distilling reusable guidance.
Ch62pc2CZs.problem: Local clinical LLM agents consulting remote specialists risk patient re-identification as quasi-identifiers accumulate across multi-turn dialogues and repeated visits.
Ch62pc2CZs.method: PrivMeSA uses reinforcement learning to train a local encounter agent that balances task accuracy against direct disclosure and registry-based re-identification risk over full outbound transcripts. A local lesson memory distills completed consultations into generalized clinical guidance retrieved before transmission to avoid repeated remote queries.
Ch62pc2CZs.key_idea: Optimize a local clinical agent with RL against transcript-wide re-identification risk while caching distilled remote-specialist guidance in a local memory to reduce future disclosures.
Ch62pc2CZs.evidence: Evaluated on an emergency-department benchmark built from MIMIC-IV-ED records against delegation baselines (including Papillon noted in reviews).
Ch62pc2CZs.claimed_gains: Improves mean task accuracy over delegation by up to 15.8 percentage points and lowers disclosure of personal details from 98.0% to 0.2%.
Ch62pc2CZs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling multi-turn and cross-visit quasi-identifier accumulation in local-remote clinical delegation is timely and clinically relevant.
Ch62pc2CZs.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to a single dataset with missing self-evolving baselines and ablations, and the LLM-based re-identification audit excludes extraction errors in ways that may overestimate privacy.

0sCzFRK2Vs.one_liner: Demonstrates that curating synthetic LLM training data requires group-level interaction signals rather than isolated per-sample utility scores.
0sCzFRK2Vs.problem: Standard data curation scores samples individually, missing cross-sample redundancy and interactions that degrade LLM generation as synthetic data shares grow.
0sCzFRK2Vs.method: The authors compare individual-level and group-level influence signals across synthetic pre-training and post-training pipelines, showing datasets indistinguishable to individual scorers diverge sharply under group-level influence. They derive a gradient-variance bound and translate it into a practical gradient-diversity diagnostic (GradDiv) for group curation.
0sCzFRK2Vs.key_idea: Capture cross-sample gradient interactions via group-level influence and gradient diversity rather than scoring synthetic training examples in isolation.
0sCzFRK2Vs.evidence: Supported by a theoretical proposition and proxy-matched experiments across synthetic pre-training and RLVR post-training settings.
0sCzFRK2Vs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving from individual sample scoring to group-level interaction signals addresses an important practical problem in synthetic data curation.
0sCzFRK2Vs.main_concern: The theoretical analysis assumes a single plain gradient step and raw gradient variance, whereas the implemented group oracle uses AdamW and GradDiv uses normalized projected cosine diversity.

RI0eJ5cMix.one_liner: Intervenes on distributional and asserted uncertainty in training and context data to show LLM internal and verbalized probabilities are coupled.
RI0eJ5cMix.problem: It is unknown whether an LLM's verbalized confidence tracks its internal sampling probabilities when training data frequencies and explicit probabilistic assertions diverge.
RI0eJ5cMix.method: The authors construct controlled training and in-context interventions that independently vary distributional event frequencies and explicit verbal probability assertions. They measure how both internal token probabilities and verbalized confidence readouts respond and test residual correlation between the two.
RI0eJ5cMix.key_idea: Independently manipulate event frequencies and explicit probability assertions in training and context data to test whether internal and verbalized LLM probability readouts co-vary beyond shared inputs.
RI0eJ5cMix.evidence: Evaluated via controlled synthetic from-scratch training and 10-example in-context learning experiments with mixed and contradictory uncertainty sources.
