RI0eJ5cMix.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the synthetic multi-set intervention design is clean, controlled, and effectively isolates pretraining priors.
RI0eJ5cMix.main_concern: Correlated residuals do not establish a shared internal representation without mechanistic perturbation experiments, and the synthetic setup and coarse 1-digit readout limit real-world generalization.

h0pUFbO53w.one_liner: Selects, orders, and batches LLM RL post-training data using Sparse Autoencoder activation clusters and projected sample gradients.
h0pUFbO53w.problem: RL data engineering for LLMs relies on external outcome metrics like pass rates, overlooking model-internal functional structure when choosing, ordering, and batching samples.
h0pUFbO53w.method: SAERL maps samples into Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) feature space to identify functional regions from activations and project sample gradients onto SAE features. It retains samples with strong non-redundant projected gradients, orders each region easy-to-hard, and draws batches primarily from single activation clusters, transferring schedules built on small models to larger ones.
h0pUFbO53w.key_idea: Uses Sparse Autoencoder activation clusters and SAE-projected sample gradients to filter non-redundant RL samples, order easy-to-hard curricula per cluster, and construct cluster-focused batches.
h0pUFbO53w.evidence: Mathematical reasoning RL experiments across Qwen model scales (1.5B to 7B) and RL algorithms, plus component ablations and cross-scale schedule transfer.
h0pUFbO53w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using SAE model internals for RL data selection and transferable curriculum construction is an interesting direction with practical gains on 1.5B-to-7B transfer.
h0pUFbO53w.main_concern: Reviewers note the full pipeline barely beats selection-only or curriculum-only ablations (52.6% vs 52.4%/52.5%), omits SAE training costs, evaluates only math on Qwen models, and relies on unsigned gradient magnitudes.

jThHEpesHI.one_liner: Trains LLMs with RL and grammar-constrained program mutation to compose search primitives into executable retrieval programs.
jThHEpesHI.problem: Retrieval-augmented LLMs typically use fixed pipelines or atomic tool calls, tying search breadth directly to context consumption while making flexible multi-step retrieval hard to explore under sparse RL rewards.
jThHEpesHI.method: Retrieval Program Learning (RPL) lets a policy compose search primitives into executable programs with local state and control flow so large candidate sets are filtered before entering context. To overcome sparse RL exploration, grammar-constrained, execution-verified program mutation generates local variants of suboptimal rollouts and distills verified trajectories back into the policy.
jThHEpesHI.key_idea: Trains policies to write stateful retrieval programs over search primitives and improves RL exploration via grammar-constrained, execution-verified local program mutation and distillation.
jThHEpesHI.evidence: Open-domain QA and corpus-level reasoning experiments across model sizes (including a 4B model) on in- and out-of-domain multi-hop benchmarks, plus ablations and training-dynamics analyses.
jThHEpesHI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree composing executable retrieval programs cleanly decouples search breadth from context usage and yields consistent QA and efficiency gains.
jThHEpesHI.main_concern: Reviewers point out that baselines lack matched retrieval primitives (such as rerankers) to isolate programmatic composition, and that mutation ablations confound structural exploration with extra supervised updates.

TemtPBeapU.one_liner: Argues in a position paper that higher-order graph learning needs cross-representation portability and transfer across hypergraphs and complexes.
TemtPBeapU.problem: Higher-order neural networks are fragmented across incompatible representations (hypergraphs, simplicial complexes), mathematical formalisms, and tasks, preventing models and tools from transferring across representations.
TemtPBeapU.method: Through a meta-analysis of ten recent surveys and an illustrative Gram-mate example separating representations, encodings, and propagation rules, this position paper argues for cross-representation portability and outlines open problems around translation, pretraining, and transfer learning.
TemtPBeapU.key_idea: Frames fragmentation in higher-order graph learning via representations, encodings, and propagation rules, advocating cross-representation transfer and portability as a unifying research agenda.
TemtPBeapU.evidence: Meta-analysis of ten surveys on higher-order network representations and an illustrative numerical distinguishability example.
TemtPBeapU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-representation portability is a relevant research direction and appreciate the illustrative example separating representation, encoding, and propagation rules.
TemtPBeapU.main_concern: Reviewers state the paper overpromises a 'Rosetta stone' without providing a concrete testable transfer framework or new mathematical bridges, relying mostly on a survey-of-surveys.

byk68Sob9X.one_liner: Optimizes scientific survey generation workflows over an object-oriented class hierarchy using local task rubrics and global survey rubrics.
byk68Sob9X.problem: Optimizing agentic workflows for long-form scientific survey generation is difficult because local improvements to individual subtasks do not reliably improve overall survey quality.
byk68Sob9X.method: OZONE defines the workflow search space via abstract classes and task-specific subclasses with inherited contracts, connecting execution units into a DAG. It pairs local rubrics for diagnosing unit edits with a global rubric for selecting workflows, supports rubric-guided runtime editing and review-based revision, and introduces CROFTBench covering recent CS survey topics with figures and tables.
byk68Sob9X.key_idea: Constrains agentic DAG workflow search with an object-oriented class hierarchy of operator contracts and guides edits via paired local-task and global-document rubrics.
byk68Sob9X.evidence: Evaluations with GPT-4o-mini on SurveyBench, Bloom-Eval, and CROFTBench, plus a 6-expert human evaluation across 40 topics.
byk68Sob9X.claimed_gains: With GPT-4o-mini and inference refinement, OZONE achieves 72.2 on SurveyBench, 45.78 on Bloom-Eval, and 44.77 on CROFTBench.
byk68Sob9X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation of local diagnosis from global selection for long-form survey workflows is well motivated and appreciate the transparent human-study reporting.
byk68Sob9X.main_concern: Reviewers note that the core object-oriented class hierarchy is never ablated separately from local rubrics, memory, and round reviews, leaving its contribution over AFlow-style search unproven.

0N1QHJQuZz.one_liner: Triggers full-attention KV-cache recomputation whenever sparse-decoding next-token entropy exceeds a threshold to fix accumulated KV errors.
0N1QHJQuZz.problem: Sparse attention degrades reasoning accuracy and lengthens generations because errors accumulate in the KV cache during sparse decoding and most strongly harm high-entropy steps.
0N1QHJQuZz.method: HERA monitors next-token entropy during sparse decoding and triggers a KV repair—a full-attention pass that recomputes and replaces cached KV states to produce the dense next-token distribution—whenever sparse entropy is high.
0N1QHJQuZz.key_idea: Monitors sparse next-token entropy at decoding time to trigger full-attention KV-cache recomputation that removes inherited sparse-decoding errors.
0N1QHJQuZz.evidence: Causal intervention analyses separating local versus historical KV error, plus evaluations on three reasoning models across four benchmarks (including MATH-500 with Qwen3-8B) against Quest and ReSA.
0N1QHJQuZz.claimed_gains: On MATH-500 with Qwen3-8B, HERA improves accuracy by 18.8 percentage points over Quest with 25.7% fewer tokens, and by 5.6 points over ReSA with 7.4% fewer tokens and 13.7% fewer repair calls.
0N1QHJQuZz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical finding that high-entropy degradation comes mainly from accumulated historical KV errors is well supported and yields strong accuracy-token improvements over Quest.
0N1QHJQuZz.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that no wall-clock latency or throughput measurements are reported to verify practical efficiency, and evaluation is limited to a single sparse-attention backend (Quest).

vdEpw0rJlH.one_liner: Prunes VLA visual tokens training-free using proprioception-weighted instruction attention and Jaccard-stability adaptive layer selection.
vdEpw0rJlH.problem: Existing visual token pruning for Vision-Language-Action models ignores robot proprioceptive state and prunes at a fixed layer regardless of whether shallow token rankings have stabilized.
vdEpw0rJlH.method: PropPrune weights each instruction token's visual attention by its attention to the proprioceptive state to score visual token importance. It then computes the Jaccard similarity between top-k visual token sets across adjacent shallow layers, deferring pruning to a later layer when rankings are unstable, using only existing pretrained attention maps.
vdEpw0rJlH.key_idea: Weights instruction-to-vision attention by instruction-to-proprioception attention for token scoring and defers pruning when adjacent-layer top-k Jaccard similarity is low.
vdEpw0rJlH.evidence: LIBERO benchmark evaluations at 50% and 25% token retention, distribution-shift and real-world manipulation tests, and component ablations.
vdEpw0rJlH.claimed_gains: On LIBERO at 50% and 25% visual-token retention, PropPrune stays within 0.7 and 1.3 points of the full-token model while reducing latency by 16.0% and 34.9%.
vdEpw0rJlH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-free method is simple, achieves strong accuracy-latency results on LIBERO (especially long-horizon tasks), and includes useful shift and real-world tests.
vdEpw0rJlH.main_concern: Reviewers note that proprioceptive weighting adds only modest average gains (0.25-0.50 points), fixed late-layer pruning matches or beats adaptive selection at slightly higher FLOPs, and validation lacks architectural diversity.

DOyEVw3ff9.one_liner: Improves clustering-based ANN partition routing by precomputing vector-to-neighbor-partition links and iteratively expanding scanned partitions from intermediate results.
DOyEVw3ff9.problem: Partition-based approximate nearest neighbor search routes queries solely by centroid distances, ignoring neighborhood information discovered during intermediate candidate scanning.
DOyEVw3ff9.method: Query Expansion Routing (QER) precomputes neighborhood links between indexed vectors and the partitions containing their nearest neighbors. At query time, after initial centroid-based retrieval, QER iteratively expands the partition ranking using the precomputed neighbor partitions of intermediate top candidates, implemented inside ScaNN and LoRANN.
DOyEVw3ff9.key_idea: Precomputes vector-to-neighbor-partition links during indexing and uses intermediate retrieved vectors at query time to iteratively expand the set of scanned IVF partitions.
DOyEVw3ff9.evidence: Evaluations of ScaNN-QER and LoRANN-QER across 19 VIBE and ANN-Benchmarks datasets measuring QPS, recall, memory overhead, and exact-scoring scanned vector counts.
DOyEVw3ff9.claimed_gains: Improves 14 of 19 datasets for ScaNN-QER and 18 of 19 for LoRANN-QER, with geometric-mean QPS speedups of 1.19x and 1.58x across improved datasets.
DOyEVw3ff9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree QER is simple, preserves IVF memory layouts, and delivers convincing high-recall throughput and vector-scan reductions across 19 datasets.
DOyEVw3ff9.main_concern: Reviewers view the two-hop partition expansion idea as incremental, note missing comparisons to other modern routing methods (like SOAR or Quake), and flag a confounded cross-partition pre-filter in LoRANN-QER.

YBetch4Bok.one_liner: Models Graph Transformer attention matrices as samples from dataset-specific attention graphons with cut-distance variance bounds and an empirical estimator.
YBetch4Bok.problem: It is unclear whether dense n-by-n pairwise attention matrices learned by Graph Transformers converge to a size-invariant continuum limit as graph size n grows.
YBetch4Bok.method: The authors treat each attention matrix as a finite sample from an underlying attention graphon and derive worst-case and regularity-aware cut-distance variance bounds. They operationalize this via a canonicalize-then-block-average estimator for dataset-level attention graphons and a variance-based diagnostic for continuum stabilization.
YBetch4Bok.key_idea: Treats Graph Transformer attention matrices as graphon samples, proves cut-distance concentration bounds, and estimates dataset-level attention graphons via canonicalization and block averaging.
YBetch4Bok.evidence: Cut-distance variance bounds plus experiments across multiple graph benchmarks and architectures testing variance decay with n and transfer to larger graphs.
YBetch4Bok.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree applying dense graph limit theory to give a size-agnostic continuum description of Graph Transformer attention is an interesting and creative direction.
YBetch4Bok.main_concern: Reviewers argue the theory assumes generic i.i.d. graphon sampling on symmetrized sigmoid-transformed logits rather than actual softmax Transformer attention, and that sorting/averaging may inflate observed stability.

rcu9ueyLes.one_liner: Learns sparse static and dynamic multi-agent medical QA communication policies by estimating corrective versus harmful peer effects against matched self-review.
rcu9ueyLes.problem: In multi-agent reasoning, peer messages can mislead initially correct agents as well as fix errors, and ordinary self-reflection confounds measurement of true peer influence.
rcu9ueyLes.method: MedDAC evaluates receiver-specific sender-subset interventions against matched self-review to estimate both corrective and harmful incremental communication effects. MedDAC-Static aggregates these estimates into a fixed sparse directed graph under a message budget, while MedDAC-Dynamic predicts question-conditioned communication actions from the multi-agent state.
rcu9ueyLes.key_idea: Contrasts sender-subset peer interventions against matched self-review to quantify corrective and harmful effects, then learns budgeted static or dynamic directed communication policies.
rcu9ueyLes.evidence: Evaluations across five medical QA benchmarks with four agents, comparing MedDAC-Static and MedDAC-Dynamic against single-agent, Majority Vote, ReConcile, and Full Communication.
rcu9ueyLes.claimed_gains: MedDAC-Static reaches 74.57% macro-average accuracy versus 69.77% for single-agent inference; under Majority Vote, its 6-message policy achieves 73.13% versus 72.99% for 12-message Full Communication.
rcu9ueyLes.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree modeling both corrective and harmful peer effects with a matched self-review control is well motivated and matches full communication with half the messages.
rcu9ueyLes.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over strong baselines like ReConcile (+0.37 points) and Random-K6 (+0.61 points) are small with no confidence intervals or significance tests, and scalability beyond four agents is untested.

D2ryMJBKWZ.one_liner: Trains a lightweight residual action adapter on paired clean-vs-perturbed frozen VLA predictions to correct transient visual mislocalization.
D2ryMJBKWZ.problem: Brief visual mislocalization redirects chunked Vision-Language-Action execution and causes manipulation failures that persist even after the visual error disappears.
D2ryMJBKWZ.method: Paired Residual Adaptation (PRA) evaluates a frozen VLA policy on clean and visually perturbed observations of the same physical state with matched sampling noise, using the action difference as supervision for a lightweight residual adapter alongside balanced zero-residual targets. At deployment, the adapter adjusts translational actions from current images, robot state, and the proposed action chunk.
D2ryMJBKWZ.key_idea: Supervises a lightweight translational residual adapter using action differences between clean and visually perturbed frozen-VLA queries under matched sampling noise.
D2ryMJBKWZ.evidence: Closed-loop evaluations on LIBERO-Spatial under rendering-only target displacements across frozen pi0.5, pi0, and OpenVLA backbones, plus matched-budget ablations.
D2ryMJBKWZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree transient visual errors in chunked VLA execution are a practical problem and that the lightweight residual adapter consistently improves perturbed-task success across three backbones.
D2ryMJBKWZ.main_concern: Reviewers point out the problem is unidentifiable without observation history because rendering-only and physical target shifts look identical, causing failure under genuine physical displacements.

uvktl4GnAh.one_liner: Mines failure-predictive n-grams from RL rollouts to retrieve a 35M-token pretraining subset for targeted continued pretraining before RL.
uvktl4GnAh.problem: RL with verifiable rewards often fails persistently on specific reasoning patterns that the base model already partially solves, raising the question of how to cheaply repair base-model gaps.
uvktl4GnAh.method: The authors identify small sets of characteristic n-grams in RL rollouts that strongly predict rollout failure, then use exact-match retrieval with those n-grams to build a 35M-token continued pretraining (CPT) corpus from pretraining data. Continuing pretraining on this corpus before RL repairs failure modes without labels or a teacher.
uvktl4GnAh.key_idea: Extracts failure-predictive n-grams from RL rollouts and runs exact-match retrieval on pretraining text to construct a small targeted continued-pretraining corpus before RL.
uvktl4GnAh.evidence: Experiments on OLMo2 and Qwen3 models trained with RL on GSM8K, mixed math/commonsense/knowledge tasks, and general math/science reasoning against label-free CPT and no-CPT controls.
uvktl4GnAh.claimed_gains: Outperforms label-free-query continued pretraining on the same 35M-token budget in 9 of 11 settings, including by 2.0 points on one reported benchmark.
uvktl4GnAh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the rollout-failure-to-retrieval pipeline is simple, concrete, inspectable, and economical in data requirements without needing a teacher model.
uvktl4GnAh.main_concern: Reviewers find the downstream gains marginal and often within noise on single RL seeds, with weak direct evidence that targeted CPT actually repairs the failure n-grams beyond matched CPT.

mp8gxY1vPk.one_liner: Distills multi-rollout Chain-of-Thought answer distributions into short per-question continuous latent tokens in a frozen LLM.
mp8gxY1vPk.problem: Explicit Chain-of-Thought reasoning requires long autoregressive traces that are discarded after answering, and prior latent-reasoning methods fail to match CoT performance efficiently.
mp8gxY1vPk.method: To test whether short latent contexts matching CoT exist, the authors freeze an LLM and optimize continuous latent input tokens via knowledge distillation over at least 1,024 teacher CoT rollouts per question, analyzing held-out rollout loss, answer-distribution similarity, and template augmentations.
mp8gxY1vPk.key_idea: Distill the answer distribution induced by many long CoT rollouts into a short continuous latent prefix optimized for a frozen LLM.
mp8gxY1vPk.evidence: Evaluated on HumanEval+ and MATH-Hard across two model sizes and latent-length sweeps with >=1,024 rollouts per question and template-variation tests.
mp8gxY1vPk.claimed_gains: A single latent token recovers 98% of CoT performance on HumanEval+ (median CoT >1,000 tokens), and 256 latent tokens exceed CoT on MATH-Hard (median CoT >3,000 tokens).
mp8gxY1vPk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the existence question is relevant to latent reasoning and appreciate the thorough rollout evaluations and answer-distribution diagnostics.
mp8gxY1vPk.main_concern: Reviewers view per-question continuous prompt optimization as unsurprising from an information-capacity standpoint, note it cannot rule out answer memorization rather than reasoning, and point out it provides no inference-time method to generate latents.
